what_and_how: When estimated input reaches a set share of the window (75 to 90 percent, or a token count), the model writes a summary of older turns; recent turns, system prompt and original task stay verbatim; work continues from the summary. Tune the trigger per model.
problem: Long runs overflow the context window and models degrade as the history grows.
models: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.6 Sol
best_number: mean RHAE 9.24 (S0, dropping) vs 63.08 (S1, summary) (2610.26632)
verdict: survived: on strong models with very large windows, default self-summarization is as good as engineered compaction strategies
recommendation: build-in-regime: pays when the window is tight or the task outgrows it; gain vanishes with ample windows.

pattern: Clear old tool results with placeholder
what_and_how: Past a token threshold or every turn, keep the newest tool outputs and replace older ones with a short placeholder or line pointer, no model call. Age tiers cap older results at shrinking character counts. Cheapest compaction step.
problem: Old tool outputs fill the window yet are rarely reread.
best_number: SWE-bench Verified 28% → 49% mean per-task F2PF, 43 → 72 complete solutions (2608.26218)
verdict: contested: replacing old tool outputs with a placeholder is as good as model summarization and cheaper
recommendation: test-first: contested verdict, gains measured in the authors' own setups. Cheap to try first for small local models and on cheap hosted models; compare with summarizing.

what_and_how: Escalate by context pressure: first mask or clear old tool outputs and save originals to files; at a higher threshold summarize the oldest events; near the limit truncate. Clear tool results before summarizing so the summarizer reads less.
problem: One summarize step fires too late or loses detail; small models are sensitive to trigger timing.
best_number: +7.7, +9.7, +9.7 percentage points resolve rate (2609.32961)
verdict: survived: with small open models compaction details matter by 8 to 12 points: trigger timing, clearing tool output before summarizing
recommendation: build-in-regime: small open models, where order and trigger moved scores 8 to 12 points; calibrate per model.

what_and_how: Cut noisy tool output with learned or fixed patterns (boilerplate, borders, repeats), or a model-written script run in a sandbox that returns only a summary. Output with explicit errors bypasses the rules unchanged. Rule filters need no model call at inference.
problem: Terminal and log output is mostly noise that wastes tokens and hides the signal.
best_number: TerminalBench 2.0 25.86 vs 23.90 baseline (2604.19572)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one measured gain of two points by its own authors. Keep the error bypass so signals are never filtered.

pattern: Cap tool output, keep full file
what_and_how: Cap each tool result (for example 18,000 bytes or 20,000 characters): show head and tail, cut at whole lines or records, say content was removed, name the saved full file and a narrower command to fetch it. Return small reports inline.
problem: One huge tool result floods the window or silently loses evidence fields.
best_number: token cost 1,271 vs Pi baseline 1,339; average score 47.208 vs 44.833 (2609.20519)
verdict: survived: limits on tool output length cause much of the loss between harnesses; truncation markers telling the model how to narrow the query recover it
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; cut by record not position and keep the full output readable.

what_and_how: Give the model tools to compact its own context (a summary plus which turns to keep) at task boundaries, to replace acted-on results with a one-line note, or to cache, truncate or summarize its outputs, with a reminder listing the largest outputs.
problem: Fixed thresholds compact at the wrong moment; the model knows when a phase is done.
best_number: 34 % lower cost than its explicit 200k-window configuration (2610.34425)
verdict: survived: compaction machinery fails silently in practice, and weaker models never call a self-managed compaction tool
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models only; weaker ones never call the tool. Keep a threshold backstop.

what_and_how: Decide when and what to compact by predicted payoff: estimate remaining requests and compact only when projected input savings beat the cost of rewriting the prompt cache; predict line reuse with trained trees; classify turns by type and summarize by segment. No model call.
problem: Compacting at fixed thresholds can raise billed cost by breaking the prompt cache.
best_number: GPT-6-Luna cost ratio 0.88 in isolation (Table 4) (2611.12122)
novelty: novel: compaction chosen by predicted net savings against cache rewrite cost, not by size
verdict: survived: cutting context saves money only when the prompt cache stays intact; blind truncation or token-count targets can raise billed cost
recommendation: test-first: the cache rule survived, but the measured policies were tested by their authors and one lost score (41.993 vs 44.833).

what_and_how: Keep the system prompt and walk backward, keeping the newest turns that fit a token budget; drop older ones with no summary and no retrieval. No extra model calls. Facts that appear once are lost for good.
problem: The history exceeds the window and a hard cut is needed with no extra calls.
best_number: 15/200 window vs 200/200 full history, fact not recoverable (2610.26632)
verdict: survived: a truncated or summarized window drops facts the agent cannot observe again; keep them in persistent state or make them re-readable
recommendation: do-not-build: as the only strategy; measured recall 15/200 and rule violations 51.5%. Use only as a floor under a state record.

what_and_how: Keep the last eight steps verbatim, summarize older steps, and fetch the few older steps or episodes most relevant to the current question by keyword ranking or embedding; for sequential decisions fetch fewer entries. Cap context at 32k tokens.
problem: Old facts are needed only occasionally; keeping all or none loses them or wastes tokens.
verdict: survived: keeping task state, evidence or notes in a persistent record outside the transcript raises results for mid-strength models
recommendation: build-in-regime: mid-strength models; tune retrieval depth, since more entries lowered success. A relevance filter alone scored below full history.

what_and_how: Keep only the newest screenshots or frames in the prompt; replace older images by text placeholders or one-line action summaries, keep text and action records, archive the rest for search; give each view image tokens by how much it changed.
problem: Images cost many tokens each and old ones rarely matter.
best_number: success rate +1.7, +5.7 and +2.1 points over positional allocation on R2R-CE (2610.10787)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: two measured papers with tiny samples (eight runs in one). Fine for any screen-driving agent; check on your own tasks.

what_and_how: At each state entry or iteration discard the message list and rebuild context from a fixed template: task and paths, step plan, committed memory, step log, newest observations. Entry hooks inject the phase prompt and valid transitions. No transcript is carried.
problem: Transcripts grow and drift; a rebuilt prompt stays small and predictable.
best_number: $0.13 per task on the Volvo IVI benchmark (2610.33636)
verdict: survived: keeping task state, evidence or notes in a persistent record outside the transcript raises results for mid-strength models
recommendation: test-first: one measured paper gives a cost figure only, the other four are argued.

what_and_how: Run each stage or subtask in its own fresh context that receives only a written brief, declared inputs and file references to earlier results; it returns a bounded report (about 40 lines, or 1,000 to 2,000 tokens), not its transcript. The parent writes the brief.
problem: One shared context grows, confuses roles and lets earlier noise leak into later steps.
best_number: WeaveBench PassRate 51.8% to 80.7% (2608.01964)
verdict: survived: splitting work across subagents helps only when each gets a complete task-specific brief and returns a bounded report
recommendation: test-first: survived on weak evidence and 13 of 18 papers only argue it; generic delegation hurt. Test per task. Core of a multi-role pipeline.

what_and_how: Compile each role's prompt from one versioned state: planner, verifier and recovery each see only the fields their template names; control and audit fields stay hidden, the verifier excludes the planner's conclusions, other roles' turns shrink to summaries, readers get only entries new since their last read.
problem: Shared context lets roles anchor on each other's conclusions and bloats every prompt.
best_number: invalid information 0/30 versus 11/30 (2610.26101)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: two measured papers, one found no difference; the rest argued.

what_and_how: Keep one model context per agent across all peer conversations, or one execution context that the policy and the evaluator both read, so information from different peers or modules can be combined; transitions reset only the needed parts.
problem: Separate contexts stop an agent combining what it learned in different conversations.
best_number: M2's success rate increased from 0% to 90% (2609.17527)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one measured paper, one argued; it contradicts most isolation designs, so test it against isolation on your own tasks first.

what_and_how: On failure, delete the failed step and retry from clean context, or replace the failed call by a runtime-built line (tool name, error family); roll back the last low-value turn with corrective guidance; give the next attempt only prior answers with confidence, never reasoning traces.
problem: Greedy decoding repeats the same failed call and failed turns pollute context.
models: Qwen2.5-0.5B, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Sonnet-4.6, GLM-5.3
best_number: probe removes 76% of the inversion; Qwen2.5-0.5B rollouts: exact repeat rate 31% to 16% (2608.23651)
verdict: survived: after a failed attempt pass compact feedback on what failed; neither full earlier reasoning nor a clean restart from an empty workspace performs best
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence; rollback added nothing on Claude Sonnet 4.5 (40.3 against 41.6). Keep a failure description, not a bare restart.

what_and_how: Hold a very long input as a variable in a persistent REPL, split it, send each piece to a sub-call with its own context (a handle returns at once), and let the main model combine results; restore the answer options in each worker prompt.
problem: Single prompts exceed the window or degrade on aggregation over long inputs.
best_number: OOLONG .700 vs .420 (Pi-mono, whole harness) (2608.23552)
novelty: novel: model holds the long prompt as a variable and delegates slices to sub-calls
verdict: contested: splitting a very long input across fresh sub-agent harnesses beats a single coding agent on long-context aggregation tasks
recommendation: test-first: contested; one paper found it far worse than a direct call (2% against 44%). Try only for inputs that exceed the window.

what_and_how: Rank chunks by keyword scoring plus embeddings fused by reciprocal rank, rerank the top candidates with a cross-encoder and pass the top three to five; filter by metadata first; route queries by keyword cues to subject retrieval; split manuals along their own structure.
problem: Plain embedding or plain keyword search misses relevant chunks and returns noise.
best_number: average 38.8 vs 34.1 with no retriever (ext-meta-harness-beyond-reward-agent-improvement)
verdict: stale: whether exact-text search or vector search wins in an agent flips with the harness and with whether results print inline or go to files
recommendation: test-first: verdict stale, the winner flips by harness. Measure keyword-only against hybrid on your own documents first.

what_and_how: Parse the repository with a syntax tree, build call-graph, keyword and embedding indexes once per repository (updated by diffs) and expose search, list, read and definition-lookup tools; or prepend a precomputed per-file block of callers, callees, inputs and sinks. Rank files by import fan-in.
problem: Agents on large repositories waste turns locating the right files and definitions.
best_number: deepseek-v4-pro 89% vs 77% (2609.04898)
verdict: survived: when material is too large to read, a structure-aware code index or retrieval tool raises localization and pass rates, most for weaker models
recommendation: build-in-regime: repositories larger than the window; lift is largest for weaker models and zero for GPT-5.5 in one test (80.0 to 80.0).

what_and_how: Store knowledge as typed records or a graph (entities, rules, evidence packs, declared sources); each step queries only what it needs by variable match, scenario preset, declared source list or criterion selector and injects a few top items in a bounded block. Build the graph without a model where possible.
problem: Raw documents are too large; the model needs a small, relevant, checkable slice.
best_number: Qwen3.8-Flash (Qwen Code) 62.1 to 73.7 (2610.07753)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: 13 papers, 8 measured only by their authors, and one loses on Claude Opus 5 (62.6 to 53.5). Fits where an organisation's own records apply.

what_and_how: Leave the manual, statute or experience history out of the prompt. Store it as files (one JSON line per node, ordered shards, directories of traces) and give the agent search, grep and shell tools; it reads sections per turn and outputs append to context.
problem: Reference material is too large to inline and a prebuilt index adds a layer to maintain.
best_number: SARA-Numeric 0.303 direct vs 0.600 Terminus-KIRA (2606.05009)
verdict: survived: giving a strong model the data as files with a shell or code matches or beats pre-built query and search tools, and is cheaper
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models only; Qwen3.5-35B fell from 0.340 to 0.114 on the same task.

what_and_how: Put the whole rule catalog, statute or full session transcripts in one prompt and let the model select or answer in one pass, with no retrieval layer, summary tree or tools; let the window grow with workflow size.
problem: Retrieval layers lose items and add moving parts.
best_number: full coverage 75% (full episode) vs 26% (first message) (2611.02440)
verdict: survived: when material fits in context, give it inline; an index, summary tree or search layer in front lowers accuracy for weaker models
recommendation: build-in-regime: material that fits the window; an index in front hurt weaker models.

what_and_how: A small model reads each chunk or paper once and writes claims or stance-labelled facts with verbatim source spans; claims whose span is absent are dropped; the reasoning model sees only these facts, or the top four sentences by keyword score, or claim-evidence pairs in place of the located chunk.
problem: Raw documents are long and noisy; the reasoning model pays for text it does not need.
best_number: pooled 0.77 vs. 0.65 for abstracts and 0.70 for full text (p = 0.024) (2610.40906)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: all five measured only by their authors and one found no gain (50.00 against 51.76).

what_and_how: List skills and tools only as name, description and path in the prompt; the full body or schema is read from disk or loaded when needed; show a compact memory index and fill detail on demand; strip descriptions of tools the task does not use; look tools up by search.
problem: Full skill and tool texts inflate every prompt and the model needs few of them.
best_number: skills block 1,411 tokens default vs 457 all-off (2608.20389)
verdict: survived: whether offered skills get loaded depends mainly on the model and how they are offered; weak models and always-on listings rarely load them
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models; weak models rarely load skills, so preload rules they must obey.

what_and_how: Inject instructions or facts only when a trigger fires: a rule file when a matching path is read, only the active phase body, a memory when intent and word-overlap gates pass, a reminder when a detector sees failure, or a scored top item under a token budget.
problem: Always-on instructions cost tokens every turn and dilute attention.
best_number: +55.0 points of pass rate on held-out rule families (2610.14216)
verdict: survived: load instructions and skills for the current phase, chosen by the harness, rather than all at once or at the model's discretion
recommendation: test-first: verdict rests on weak evidence; two papers measured by authors (+55.0 points, +6.2 mid-run). Cheap to build.

what_and_how: Turn raw run traces into layered views for an analysis agent: typed nodes sharing line numbers, a one-line-per-call overview, a filtered view, then pointers into the verbatim record; per-task digests with an overview; the agent drills down only where needed.
problem: Analysis and improvement agents drown in full traces.
best_number: without it 69.44%; vs full trace, time 42.5% and tokens 41.5% lower (2611.03868)
verdict: survived: the optimizer needs rich curated failure evidence: raw traces, repeated runs or diagnosed feedback beat scores or one rollout; ranked top items beat the pool
recommendation: build-in-regime: harness improvement loops; keep raw traces reachable, since summaries alone gave less.

what_and_how: Order every request most stable first: tools sorted by name, fixed system prompt, per-chat role, append-only transcript; changing values (clock, files, plan) go in a volatile tail appended as messages; set cache breakpoints. Answer side questions in a new context seeded with a ledger.
problem: Changing early prompt bytes breaks the cache and multiplies billed cost.
best_number: Fable 5.1 pinned $0.90 vs Sonnet 5 ledger side lane $0.36 (2609.28919)
verdict: survived: cutting context saves money only when the prompt cache stays intact and what is dropped is chosen with care
recommendation: build: free to do and the idea survived with medium evidence. Needed wherever a hosted model is billed per token.

what_and_how: Before the first model call run guarded code (15 second limit) that collects facts the model would otherwise discover: working directory, languages, package managers, profiled data files and output formats, operator profiles; place them at the start of the prompt as a fixed contract.
problem: Models spend early turns discovering the environment or guess the data layout.
best_number: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct: 43% correct, 27% faster than baseline (zero-shot 30% correct) (2611.12079)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: bootstrap measured only inside whole harnesses (76.4 against 74.7); the data-profile contract by its authors only. Cheap.

what_and_how: Keep a short versioned file (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) at the repository root that the agent loads at session start: conventions, which tools exist or are absent, the test runner, review constraints. Tell the agent the reviewer's constraints too.
problem: The agent repeats avoidable mistakes about project tooling and norms each session.
best_number: recurrence from 5 of 5 sessions to 0 of 5 (2610.34938)
verdict: survived: general skill libraries and broad guidance documents add little over a bare strong model; only content matched to the task moves results
recommendation: build: keep it short and task-specific; general guidance adds little. Stating reviewer rules raised joint success but lowered plain success.

what_and_how: Add one short, positive, factual sentence that changes one measured behaviour: what the verifier receives, that listed ideas were tried and rejected, that the report is authoritative, round to nearest, a true provenance comment above a table. Put it in the system message; avoid prohibitions.
problem: Models drift on small points that one clear sentence fixes at no cost.
verdict: survived: one short, positive, factual sentence reliably changes a measurable behaviour; in the system message it beats the user message
recommendation: build: cheap and survived with medium evidence; check that each sentence moves its behaviour, since one rounding sentence lost 3.8 points.

what_and_how: For small models rewrite the system prompt as a numbered workflow naming each fragile step, fix the tool contract (call formats, admissible actions, output structure) in the prompt, enforce output format in the harness, and pick context richness per task class by testing levels from model-only to full simulation.
problem: Small models cannot plan the procedure themselves or hold the output format.
best_number: gemma-4-26b-a4b: budget-approval 75.0% to 98.3% (2607.08938)
verdict: survived: against a minimal prompt a general engineered prompt lifts every model, most for the weakest; no strong model lost
recommendation: build-in-regime: small models, where the lift is largest; extra structure can hurt other small models, so test each.

what_and_how: Protect what compaction destroys: tell the summarizer to keep each rule with force, scope and exceptions; capture every detail first, then prune; keep recent tool evidence or stable references to it; test after compaction that key facts are recoverable and retry with lighter compression.
problem: Summaries silently lose rules, scope limits and recent evidence the agent still needs.
best_number: violation at three runs 9.0% against 11.9% full-history baseline (2611.03223)
verdict: survived: compaction summaries lose instructions, rules and scope limits; persist rules outside the conversation and re-inject them
recommendation: build: re-inject rules from outside the transcript; the summarizer-prompt and check variants are argued or authors-only.

what_and_how: Preprocess raw state before the model sees it: parse tracebacks, order and filter entities, compute distances, group units, keep only task-relevant page elements, render spatial state as a text grid or entity brief, and return success with affected objects after each action.
problem: Raw state output is long, unordered and misleading for the model.
best_number: weighted success rate 82.43±6.31 with HELM vs 25.42±8.24 ReAct (Table 1) (ext-helm-harness-engineering-emergency-agents)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: large gains, all measured by authors (82.43 against 25.42 on GPT-OSS:20b); no neutral test. Strong fit for small local models.

what_and_how: Convert video and audio to text once: transcribe speech with word times, add acoustic features as words, mark silent gaps and shot cuts, number each cue so later calls cite it; the model searches the text, then inspects only the matching frames or windows.
problem: Long audio and video cost far too many tokens to feed raw.
best_number: Qwen3.8-27B (medium): 80.3 vs 62.9 without transcript on Daily-Omni (2611.06083)
novelty: novel: speech transcript with word times used as a search index to pick frames
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: strong gains by authors; one test showed no change (92% under both conditions). Only for media tasks.

what_and_how: Give the model the game frame as a 512 by 512 image (an 8x nearest-neighbour upscale of the 64 by 64 frame, about 308 image tokens) instead of the official text grid of numbers.
problem: A text grid of numbers is hard for the model to read spatially.
best_number: 13.33 official text grid, 47.32 with image observations (2610.02200)
novelty: novel: image of the frame replaces the text grid; one paper reports 13.33 to 47.32
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper on its own benchmark, opposing the text-grid designs in this kind. Test both forms on your task; only for visual or grid tasks.

what_and_how: Do not show the optimizer every failure. Group failed instances by stage and error signature, send one representative per group, tag each as regressed, persistent or changed since last round, rank groups by coverage, and show success clusters beside failure clusters.
problem: The self-improvement prompt overflows with failures and overweights repeated ones.
best_number: Qwen3.8-Max average hold-out +16.67 for full ingestion, +8.23 without successes, +6.56 without failures (2610.39884)
novelty: novel: one tagged representative per failure group, group count shrinking as pass rate rises
verdict: survived: the optimizer needs rich curated failure evidence: raw traces, repeated runs or diagnosed feedback beat scores or one rollout; ranked top items beat the pool
recommendation: build-in-regime: harness improvement loops only; gains are small (65.7% against 64.7% random order) except full ingestion.

what_and_how: Match training data to the harness: split each recorded session at every compaction boundary, score each token only against the context it saw (branch masks or one packed sequence with a 4D mask), distil the compacted view from the full prefix, merge calls only on exact token prefixes, keep trajectories whose harness fingerprint matches.
problem: Training on whole sessions mismatches the compacted contexts the model sees at run time.
best_number: AgentFold logdiff 0.012 versus 0.366 for Naive-Compressed (Table 1) (2609.00865)
novelty: novel: training sequences split at compaction with masks matching what the model saw
verdict: survived: a context harness added only after training recovers little of the benefit of training with it in place
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, authors only, needs fine-tuning. Fits only if you tune a small local model inside your own harness.

what_and_how: Each round the harness or planner updates a compact record: progress, facts, outcomes, uncertainty, best score so far and when it was reached, sub-goal summaries of rollouts; fetch the latest pipeline state at each turn start. Keep it after raw observations leave the window.
problem: Raw observations scroll out of the window and the agent loses where it is.
best_number: terminal-only observation return 68.1 vs full 74.0 (2608.30396)
verdict: survived: keeping task state, evidence or notes in a persistent record outside the transcript raises results for mid-strength models
recommendation: test-first: three of four papers only argue it and the one measurement favours the full record (74.0 against 68.1). Cheap to add to any harness.

what_and_how: Keep source label, trust tier and carrier type on every tool result and retrieved item as it enters context; copy the tag onto values derived from it so later gates can see it; admit documents only through a registered source manifest.
problem: Injected or untrusted text gets the authority of a user instruction.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: harnesses give text from tools, subagents, plugins and repository files more authority than it deserves
recommendation: test-first: all argued, no measurement of the labels themselves. Strong fit where an organisation's own rules apply and for any harness with web tools or outside reviewers.

what_and_how: Delete earlier reasoning blocks before summarizing, or have a judge mark restated and padding spans in current reasoning, delete them and regenerate the reply from the pruned text; keep messages and tool calls.
problem: Reasoning text fills the window with repeats of what is already known.
best_number: solved 89.0 with nothing deleted, 89.5 with 41 (% deleted) (2611.07238)
novelty: novel: judge marks restated spans, deletes them, regenerates the reply from pruned reasoning
verdict: survived: on strong models with very large windows default self-summarization is as good as engineered compaction; discarding reasoning hurt two of three models
recommendation: do-not-build: dropping reasoning before summaries cut GPT-5.4 from 0.59 to 0.43; the pruning variant gained only half a point. Keep reasoning.

what_and_how: Send back the model's own earlier reasoning items in the provider's native format, with thought signatures, on every new request instead of only the visible reply text.
problem: Visible text alone loses the model's reasoning state between requests.
best_number: mean RHAE 36.32 without replay (S2) vs 71.83 with replay (S4) (2610.26632)
novelty: novel: provider-native reasoning items and signatures sent back every turn; 36.32 to 71.83
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper, one game benchmark, large lift by its authors and provider-specific. Cheap check on any hosted model that returns reasoning items.

what_and_how: A coding model reads rollout traces and scores of the current harness on training tasks, writes an edit to prompts, tools or control code, re-runs, and repeats for a fixed number of rounds, keeping the best version. Feed it full traces, not only scores.
problem: Hand-tuning a harness for each model and task does not scale or react to observed failures.
best_number: GPT-5.2: 83.09 average Pass@1 on τ 2-Bench, against 57.39 bare (2607.26598)
verdict: survived: a harness evolved with strong models scores several points above its own seed on coding and terminal benchmarks, with repeated runs
recommendation: build-in-regime: gain is real where the seed harness or bare model is weak and shrinks otherwise.

what_and_how: Run the candidate edit against the incumbent on fresh held-out tasks and keep it only if it beats the incumbent by a stated margin with no loss on kept cases; otherwise restore the snapshot. Stop after a set number of rounds with no accepted edit.
problem: Unchecked self-edits pile up noise, overfit the tuning tasks and can end below the starting harness.
best_number: Qwen3.8-Max average hold-out 31.56 to 43.65 (2610.39884)
verdict: survived: every self-edit to a harness needs a held-out regression check and rollback; unchecked accumulation lowers earlier behaviour
recommendation: build: nine papers agree on direction. Use fresh tasks and a margin above run noise.

what_and_how: Keep every evaluated harness in an archive with scores and traces. Pick each parent by score, bandit sampling or Pareto dominance with some random exploration, let the proposer inspect any earlier candidate, and report the Pareto frontier after one final test run.
problem: Hill climbing on one incumbent stalls in local optima and wastes earlier candidates.
models: Claude Opus 4.8, Kimi-K3, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen3.8-27B
best_number: Kimi-K3 held-out resolve rate 69.00% with recomposition, 59.00% without (2609.32423)
verdict: survived: when candidates can be scored cheaply and reliably, structured search beats greedy, random or deep refinement at equal budget
recommendation: test-first: measured by the authors of each search method, and another judged idea finds the search rule matters little on strong models.

what_and_how: Draw several independent or branch-refined attempts from one harness and pick one by an executed check, a verifier or a majority vote. Restart rounds, tree search and parallel races are variants. A reliable checker must choose the winner.
problem: One attempt fails often, and extra attempts help only when something reliable picks the best.
best_number: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini; average pass@1 72.3 vs 68.2 direct sampling (2607.12227)
verdict: survived: running several attempts and keeping the best raises success, more for weaker models, costs in proportion and needs a checker
recommendation: build-in-regime: weak or cheap models with a real checker; gains shrink against matched-budget sampling.

pattern: Train the model inside the harness
what_and_how: Roll out the policy under the harness or a pool of harnesses, compute group-relative advantages and update the weights, often alternating training blocks with a harness-edit step that keeps a candidate only if it solves more held-out tasks than it breaks.
problem: Small models fail inside harnesses built for large models, and training outside the harness does not transfer.
best_number: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B: 58.5% (Baseline) to 78.9% (Round 2) (2607.22688)
verdict: survived: training a small model with the harness in the loop beats training outside it, and varied harnesses transfer better than one fixed harness
recommendation: build-in-regime: small models you can train, shown on the authors' own benchmarks with single runs.

what_and_how: During a run a separate reviewer or evolver reads the recent trajectory at checkpoints or on a stall and applies a bounded edit (notice, instruction, hook or tool) in the same session. A slower researcher changes configuration only when the change beats the incumbent.
problem: A harness fixed offline cannot fix failures that appear only in this task.
models: GPT-5.6-Terra, GPT-5.6-Luna, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Haiku 4.5
best_number: GPT-5.6-Terra: Terminal-Bench 2.1 74.67 with evolver, 66.33 task agent alone (2611.05139)
verdict: survived: edits made for the current task, instance or batch (in-run review, per-instance patch, per-batch update) beat one global harness evolved offline
recommendation: build: six papers agree, though the main result is one model with three runs. Add rollback to every in-run edit.

what_and_how: A router reads the task, the base trajectory or cheap profiles and picks one harness, prompt template, model tier or adapter per task, step or turn, often by calibrated vote or bandit. Some routers fall back to the default when unsure.
problem: No single harness or model wins everywhere, and the strongest costs most.
best_number: PinchBench: Opus 4.8 (OpenClaw) 93.35 at $0.2224; routed 93.14 at $0.0204 (2607.11399)
verdict: contested: routing steps or sessions to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache
recommendation: test-first: savings come from the authors' own routers and simulations, and cache loss is unmeasured.

what_and_how: Run a cheap check on every step (confidence score, deterministic trigger on repeated failure or finish request, event queue) and call the expensive verifier, controller or larger model only when it fires. Cap how often it may fire.
problem: Checking or consulting a strong model on every step multiplies cost for small gains.
best_number: MiniMax-M2.7: 75.47% to 77.20% at 1.09× total cost, 3.43% of steps verified (2610.30284)
verdict: survived: verifying once or selectively costs about 1.1 to 1.3 times; checking every step or gating completion costs 1.5 to 3.4 times
recommendation: build: selective gates cost little, but thresholds were hand-set, so tune per model.

what_and_how: Give the harness proposer raw per-task traces and failure groups (mixed groups plus a few all-fail groups, confident-wrong cases first), keep validation items and answers out of its reach, and rank candidates only on a separate split.
problem: Optimizers shown only scores or leaked validation data overfit and chase noise.
best_number: Qwen3.5-9B: AppWorld pass@2 67.7 with both group kinds vs 16.9 all-success only (2609.33146)
verdict: survived: the optimizer needs rich, curated failure evidence; raw traces and diagnosed feedback beat scores, and ranked top items beat the whole pool
recommendation: build: seven papers agree on rich evidence. Hold validation data away from the proposer.

pattern: Limit what one edit may change
what_and_how: Restrict each proposal to one module or slot, cap edits per candidate with a decaying schedule, widen permissions in stages, freeze the scoring rubric for the round, and make a no-change patch the default.
problem: Whole-harness rewrites make gains unattributable and break behaviour that worked.
best_number: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8: TimeLens-Bench R@.5 46.86 to 53.53 (2610.01766)
verdict: contested: one module per edit beats whole-harness rewriting in offline search, but whole-harness edits during a run beat a predefined scope
recommendation: test-first: small samples, one run per ablation, and the two judged results point opposite ways.

what_and_how: Each turn the model reasons about the latest observation, calls one tool, reads the result and picks the next call until it answers or a cap is hit. No full plan is written first. Per-action replanning beat multi-action batches in some tests.
problem: A plan fixed in advance cannot react to what tools return.
models: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5
verdict: survived: when the bare model already answers the task in one call, an agent loop multiplies cost about 2 to 100 times for no gain
recommendation: build-in-regime: tasks the bare model cannot finish in one call; otherwise cost multiplies for no gain.

what_and_how: Run an unmodified general coding agent or a roughly 100-line scaffold with shell and file-edit tools, adding perception or other tools as commands, and leave planning, context and recovery to the model. Use it as the baseline every added mechanism must beat.
problem: Engineered harnesses cost effort and often fail to beat a plain loop on strong models.
verdict: survived: with strong models, swapping among mature general coding harnesses moves score about as much as a rerun; it mostly moves token cost
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models only, since models near four billion parameters need a harness sized to them.

what_and_how: An ordinary program, state machine or declared document owns step order, loops, transitions and termination. The model fills in content at each node and cannot skip, reorder or end stages; only registered transitions run, with checks before each commit.
problem: Free model-chosen order skips steps, loops and breaks required procedure.
models: GPT-5.5 xhigh, Gemini-3.6-Flash, Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek-v4-flash
best_number: Gemini-3.6-Flash 68.84 full vs 55.48 without controller (-13.36) (2609.38143)
verdict: contested: whether the harness fixes the order of agent calls or a model orchestrates is unsettled; fixed order won on rule checking, a model on puzzles
recommendation: test-first: widely built yet judged unsettled, so compare against a model-chosen order on your tasks.

what_and_how: A strong model launches workers, reads each result and rewrites the plan or workflow during the run, or picks its own next step from a suggested sequence, instead of running a program written once before the run.
problem: A frozen workflow cannot adapt to what workers return.
models: Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, DeepSeek V3.2
best_number: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 65.37 full-space vs 56.59 fixed pool (2610.16966)
verdict: survived: a workflow chosen or composed per task at run time, with execution evidence, beats one fixed pipeline, mostly for mid-tier models
recommendation: test-first: supporters are the authors' own composers and the margin over good fixed harnesses is small on the strongest models.

pattern: Replace model calls with scripted steps
what_and_how: Put repeated or checkable decisions in code: precomputed case files, fixed rules, template replay with fallback to the model, validated plan repair that calls the model only for unresolved failures, deterministic handoff controllers.
problem: Model calls on routine steps cost tokens, vary run to run and fail unpredictably.
best_number: Qwen3-4B: 88.8 ± 1.6 success with 1.7 calls (sayplan 55.4 ± 1.9) (2609.19315)
verdict: survived: moving repeated steps from model calls into fixed code or batched calls cuts cost or latency about 10 to 25 times, same success
recommendation: test-first: savings are the authors' own systems, mostly single runs. Keep a model fallback.

what_and_how: Store model-chosen tool calls as graph nodes. When a node's predecessors finished, its guard passes on the latest tool receipt and its arguments are closed, run the stored call through the real tool interface with a certificate instead of calling the model. A typed selector or abstention hands control back.
problem: Repeated tasks pay the model again for decisions already made and verified.
best_number: DeepSeek Harness, HumanEval: 147 certified bypasses, 96.28 to 11.62 Tokens/task (k) (2610.32813)
novelty: novel: stored decisions replace model calls under guards and certificates binding the receipts
verdict: survived: moving repeated steps from model calls into fixed code or batched calls cuts cost or latency about 10 to 25 times, same success
recommendation: test-first: one paper on two code benchmarks, with token use falling sharply; check guard misses on your own tasks.

pattern: One planner call at first edit
what_and_how: Intercept the first file-edit request that targets a source path, send the task and transcript to a stronger planner once, append the plan as a user message, then disable the interceptor. Searching and reading before the first edit run untouched.
problem: Weak executors start editing before they understand the task.
best_number: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Executor, GPT-5.6 Sol Planner: 50.2% to 65.0% on Verified (2610.29870)
novelty: novel: one-time interception at the first source edit calls a stronger planner
verdict: survived: one plan from a stronger model, handed to a weaker executor before its first edit, lifts success by many points; plan quality follows planner strength
recommendation: build-in-regime: weak executor with a stronger planner at hand, since a weak planner can fall below no plan.

what_and_how: Generate code or a pipeline, run it, feed back the compiler error, test result, log or timing report, and regenerate for a few turns, submitting the best turn. Cap rounds near three and send checker output rather than the model's own opinion.
problem: One-shot generations fail on details that only execution reveals.
best_number: deepseek-v4-flash: RealFin-Bench 45% baseline to 65% (2606.08348)
verdict: survived: concrete outside feedback that names what failed raises success far above no feedback, and detailed feedback beats minimal
recommendation: build: cap rounds near three, since gains flatten after that.

what_and_how: A different model or session, given the task and the changes, writes its own checklist, checks each item and returns repair advice. The editor revises for up to a fixed number of rounds. The author never reviews its own work.
problem: A model re-checking its own work adds cost without catching its blind spots.
models: GPT-6.1-sol, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5
best_number: GPT-6.1-sol 64.7 single-shot to 85.6 with full reviewer feedback (2610.38231)
verdict: survived: a separate critic or different coding product, given the task and the changes, raises accuracy at modest extra cost; self-review at completion does not
recommendation: build: separate critics lift accuracy at modest cost and self-review does not.

what_and_how: Split one task into manager, executor and auditor (or planner, developer, tester) invocations, each with a narrow brief and a bounded report. The auditor checks the environment, not the executor's summary.
problem: One agent session mixes planning, doing and checking, and drifts.
best_number: Qwen 3.7-Plus: WeaveBench PassRate 51.8% to 80.7% (2608.01964)
verdict: survived: with a strong model, specialist roles, model-chosen delegation, parallel runs and peer broadcast add nothing measurable over one plain session at equal budget
recommendation: do-not-build: strong models gain nothing at equal budget and pay more; small models on narrow checkable tasks are the exception.

what_and_how: Split the task into ordered stages. A stage advances only when a deterministic check passes on fresh evidence tied to the current state, such as tests or tool receipts. A failed gate returns the failed value for bounded repair.
problem: Models claim stages are done when they are not, and later stages build on broken ones.
best_number: gpt-5.4-20260305: 90.7 final success; 46.3 without block partitioning (2611.18443)
verdict: survived: on tasks the bare model rarely completes, staged decomposition with orchestration, validation and feedback raises success by tens of points
recommendation: build-in-regime: tasks the bare model rarely completes; on single atomic steps it adds little.

what_and_how: When the agent ends a turn or calls done, a hook checks outside evidence (real files, tests, deliverables, uncommitted edits) and rejects the first premature stop, reopening the loop once. An explicit finish tool with a reason code ends the run.
problem: Agents declare completion early, and their own report is unreliable.
best_number: Qwen3.6-27B; AppWorld verify-finalize +15.4 test Pass@1 (2607.13683)
verdict: contested: a finish gate that checks outside evidence before handoff gives small to moderate gains on strong models, but the gain is uncertain
recommendation: test-first: widely built, yet gains of a few points have intervals crossing zero in some tests.

what_and_how: Cap model steps, tool calls, tokens or wall-clock in the harness. Warn the agent at set fractions of the budget and, when another tool round no longer fits, remove the tools and force an answer from the evidence gathered.
problem: Failed and looping runs burn most of the tokens.
best_number: Kimi-K2.6 with Qwen3.6 vision expert: unanswered 14.7% to 0.0% (2609.12818)
verdict: survived: token use is heavily right-skewed and failed or looping runs consume most of it, so caps and early stops belong on the failure tail
recommendation: build: failed runs consume most tokens, so cap the tail and warn before the limit.

pattern: Raise reasoning effort and run time
what_and_how: Run the model at its highest reasoning-effort setting and extend the wall-clock budget from two to six hours, or append a duration instruction or a per-family nudge about tool-call counts.
problem: Hard tasks may need more thinking and longer search than defaults allow.
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol [max] in Codex: Max 72.0 at 2 hours, 82.0 at 6 hours (2609.33356)
verdict: survived: more reasoning effort, forced full deliberation or more turns does not buy accuracy past a medium setting; it mostly costs time and tokens
recommendation: do-not-build: past the middle setting gains are flat for most tasks. Try it only on hard tasks near the model's limit.

pattern: Loop and stall detection with nudge
what_and_how: Hash each tool call (name plus normalized arguments) or watch cheap counters. After a few identical calls, unchanged patches or no new state, inject a one-time hint to change approach, then block the call or end the run.
problem: Small and mid-size models repeat failed actions until the budget is gone.
best_number: MiniMax M2.5 Terminal-Bench-2.0 overall 42.2 to 53.9 (2606.09498)
verdict: survived: small models loop and repeat failed actions, so the harness needs repeat detection, failed-action blocking, budget warnings and a finish gate
recommendation: build-in-regime: small models loop most; strong models need it less.

pattern: Resume after cut-off or early stop
what_and_how: When a reply ends before a complete action, or the model stops early or without a completion marker, call it again with the request and a length-limited draft, reasoning off, or resume the same session with a fixed continue prompt.
problem: Small models hit output limits and stop mid-action, ending the episode.
best_number: gpt-oss-120b: 58.0% to 73.3% BrowseComp-Plus accuracy, recovery off to on (2610.15208)
verdict: survived: a harness built for small local models, with fixed control code such as recovery of cut-off replies and finish gates, lifts them from near zero
recommendation: build-in-regime: small local models; one larger-model test of output-cap recovery was not significant.

what_and_how: On a failed step retry up to a fixed bound with the error text added to the prompt. Classify errors so transient ones back off exponentially and malformed calls get extra tries, halt on terminating errors, and keep one repair counter that edits cannot reset.
problem: Transient and format failures end runs that one more attempt would save.
models: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GLM-5.1, GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.6
verdict: contested: retrying a small model with plain error text helps a lot on some tasks and nothing on others; test per task
recommendation: test-first: widely built, yet the gain is task-specific and measured on authors' own tasks. Measure per task before adding more retries.

what_and_how: Snapshot state before consequential steps and restore it when a check fails. On a late failure name the earliest faulty block, invalidate it and everything after, and redo only from there. Some work trains models to emit backtrack tokens.
problem: A failure late in a run forces a full restart or leaves corrupted state.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: no judged idea covers runtime rollback, so measure snapshot cost and redo gain on your tasks.

pattern: Policy gate before every tool call
what_and_how: A layer outside the model checks each proposed call (capability scope, argument validity, provenance, callback order) and returns allow, modify, deny or ask. Apply it where the call executes so no route skips it, and send the reason back on denial.
problem: Prompt-level rules and batched approvals can be bypassed or skipped.
best_number: DeepSeek-V4-Pro: policy safety rate 55.0 (ReAct) to 95.0 (E-LEDGER) (2610.11552)
verdict: survived: deterministic checks outside the model, such as capability scope, provenance and a per-action policy gate, block attacks at near-zero benign refusals
recommendation: build: gates outside the model hold regardless of model strength. Apply at execution time.

what_and_how: The agent stops at set points (round cap, unknown failure, high-stakes act) and raises a question with options and consequences. A person or controller answers and the answer returns as tool feedback. Approvals are signed to the exact request.
problem: Irreversible or ambiguous steps need a person but should not stall the loop.
models: GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6
best_number: GPT-6 Astra, R2R SR 86 without interaction, 100 with it (2610.39446)
verdict: unmeasured: human gates at irreversible or high-stakes steps are widely argued as the safe design but no paper measures them against no gate
recommendation: test-first: argued, never measured against no gate. Keep it where people review each change anyway.

what_and_how: After a failed check or rejection, return where it failed, the expected value, mechanical fixes and typed repair options, routed to the component that owns the failure. Mark fields that already passed as read-only so repairs do not undo them.
problem: Coarse failure messages leave the model guessing and repairs break working parts.
best_number: gpt-oss-120b: 0/48 with coarse feedback and L0 versus 38/48 (79.2%) (2608.28363)
verdict: survived: diagnosis that names the failing component and routes the failure back raises repair success; free-text self-reflection finds the region but rarely the cause
recommendation: build: four papers agree. Name the component and the expected value in the message.

what_and_how: Add one short, positive, factual instruction to the system message that changes a measurable behaviour: verify the work, print a retrieval status line, compact at task boundaries, run what you changed. Pair it with a code check that reads the output.
problem: Models skip verification and report success without checking.
best_number: gemini-2.5-flash: dishonest rate 14.10% to 0.87% (2609.14758)
verdict: survived: one short, positive, factual sentence reliably changes a measurable behaviour; in the system message it beats the user message
recommendation: build: narrow behaviours move reliably, while prohibitions do not.

what_and_how: Start each round in a new model session that reloads only saved memory files, repository state and reports, discarding the earlier transcript. Or drop the failure history and restart clean instead of appending errors.
problem: Long transcripts and appended failures drag the agent back into failed approaches.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: after a failed attempt, pass compact feedback on what failed; neither the full earlier reasoning nor a clean restart from an empty workspace performs best
recommendation: test-first: no measured gain against baseline in these papers and the judged idea favours compact feedback over a clean restart.

what_and_how: One coding agent session spans the whole time budget. The harness re-prompts with the remaining time when a turn ends, keeps full tool history so the model can recover from errors, and lets it edit, compile and test in its own order.
problem: Handoffs between sessions lose context and stall long builds.
best_number: GLM 5.2 medal rate 62.5% (Malena) vs 47.1% (best external harness) (2609.40303)
verdict: survived: on long tasks that outgrow the window, one continuous conversation with summarized old turns and a note-taking instruction scores far above a stateless default
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence from single runs with unequal limits. Try it against a fresh-session loop on your own long tasks.

what_and_how: A reasoning model plans waypoints and calls a frozen low-level policy for bounded bursts. It reviews each proposed motion, restages after contact outcomes, and halts on a stall or tolerance miss, returning a receipt of what completed.
problem: Low-level policies fail silently and cannot recover without a planner.
best_number: GR00T N1.5: 73.56% to 93.56% macro average (RoboCasa) (2608.16590)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: robot benchmarks only. Reuse only the review-and-halt idea.

what_and_how: The model issues every command itself as chunks of one to six absolute end-effector waypoints from camera views and measured state, and sees each executed result. No learned low-level policy sits between model and robot.
problem: Delegating to a learned policy hides failures from the planner.
best_number: GPT-6-Astra 46.7 on EBench (2611.11509)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: in the same paper family the policy-supervised variant scores higher. Robot only.

what_and_how: Stop when a deterministic target is met, a small trained scorer over state features crosses a threshold, a judge says the marginal gain is small, or a stagnation counter fires. End in a named state and never record success by default.
problem: Loops either stop too early or burn budget after no further gain.
best_number: Claude Sonnet-4.6: pooled accuracy 48.3 to 56.9 (2605.14186)
verdict: survived: having the same or a cheaper model re-check its work or decide when to stop, without new evidence, adds cost and confidence but not correctness
recommendation: test-first: model judges without new evidence add cost, and only deterministic or trained scorers carry author measurements.

what_and_how: The model writes one program per decision. Model calls appear as primitives inside it, a runtime fills each call, and a coroutine bridge pauses the program on a tool call and resumes the same stack frame with the result.
problem: Prompt-only loops waste calls and lose state between tool calls.
best_number: GPT-5.4 nano (high); StuLife all pass 72.6 ± 0.1 (2609.26891)
novelty: novel: the program blocks on a tool call and the runtime resumes the same frame
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one recursive variant scored far below direct calls and the coroutine form was measured once.

pattern: Predict the next observation before acting
what_and_how: Before each committed action the program predicts the next observation. On the first mismatch the harness drops the remaining queued actions and returns the transition to the agent, while matching actions continue without a model call.
problem: Batched plans keep running after reality has diverged from the model's expectation.
best_number: Claude Fable 5; relative human action efficiency 99.2% in Schema vs 58.7% in Claude Code (2609.39140)
novelty: novel: predicted observation mismatch cancels queued actions
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper on interactive games measured against its own baseline. Promising for batched actions on a cheap hosted model.

pattern: Read back before retrying a write
what_and_how: Intercept a repeated write after an ambiguous error, run the declared read-back, and re-send only if the effect is absent. Wait out the in-flight bound plus the documented visibility lag before verifying.
problem: Retries of timed-out writes duplicate side effects.
best_number: wait 120 s 99% exactly-once success (2609.29095)
novelty: novel: wait out visibility lag, then read back before any retry
verdict: survived: transparent retries of side-effecting actions duplicate the effect and lower exactly-once success; retries need idempotency keys or deduplication
recommendation: test-first: the wrapper alone matched vanilla in one paper while waiting out the lag did well; idempotency keys may beat both.

what_and_how: Stop each run at a fixed ceiling on tokens, dollars, steps, turns or wall-clock time, checked by the harness loop after every model call. Report a budget stop as partial or no verdict, never as success.
problem: Runs that loop or stall burn most of the spend and never end by themselves.
models: claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6-sol, GLM-5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V3
best_number: spending limit was the binding constraint for twelve of sixteen agents (2609.23957)
verdict: survived: Token use is heavily right-skewed and failed or looping runs consume most of it, so caps or early stops belong on the failure tail.
recommendation: build: Strong evidence that spend sits in the failure tail; cheap to build. Set caps high enough not to truncate good runs.

what_and_how: Compute each task's budget from something known up front: shortest-path length plus fixed slack, twice the reference solver's actions, or a share of evaluations that depends on whether the start is warm or cold.
problem: One fixed budget is too large for easy tasks and too small for hard ones.
best_number: zero-shot 0.0, in-context 15.0, skill 7.0 (2610.13021)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Two of three papers only argue it and the third reports one small model; needs a reference plan per task.

what_and_how: Before issuing a request or starting an iteration, estimate its cost and check it against what is left, including a retry buffer; refuse or resize work that does not fit. Scoped hooks can apply the same check to every subagent.
problem: A request already in flight can overshoot the budget, and multi-agent runs end with partial results.
best_number: 200 units vs Self-Harness 4,800 TRAIN rollouts (2608.27311)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Only one paper measured it, with no baseline for the gate itself; cheap to build and a natural fit where an organisation's own rules apply.

what_and_how: Append a reminder to tool results after fixed counts of calls or timeouts, then block further calls past a hard count. Reminders ride in the result so the cached prompt prefix stays unchanged.
problem: Agents keep retrying or exploring until the budget is gone, with no warning.
best_number: RHO plus budget hooks 75.0% pass at $1.75, versus RHO 80.0% at $2.68 (2610.26770)
verdict: survived: A harness that trims waste cuts cost per task about 17 to 60 percent at equal or higher success, if success is rechecked.
recommendation: test-first: Measured cost cuts came with a five point pass loss in one paper and slower runs in the other; recheck success on your own tasks.

pattern: Limits on the harness's own interventions
what_and_how: Count nudges, reviews, negotiation rounds and repricings in code. Allow one notice per checkpoint, a cooldown after each review, and a fixed number of rounds per window, and refuse calls past the limit.
problem: Supervisors that review or nudge without limit add cost and interrupt the worker.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: All four papers only argue it; no measurement shows the limits help. Cheap to build for any harness.

what_and_how: Start with a few attempts and grant more only when an attempt reaches a new step or the failure signature changes. Halt after repeated identical failures, a repeated patch, a stalled workspace or a repeated tool call; retry only on signals the system can observe.
problem: Retries of the same failure repeat the same cost without new evidence.
best_number: 1.91, 1.82, and 1.33 attempts per solved task cold-start against baseline of five (2610.31789)
verdict: survived: Token use is heavily right-skewed and failed or looping runs consume most of it, so caps or early stops belong on the failure tail.
recommendation: build: Strong evidence that spend sits in failed runs; stopping repeats is cheap.

pattern: Resume or rerun on budget hit
what_and_how: Continue a failed run from its restored checkpoint with only the remaining budget, or rerun once with two to four times the tokens and more wall time when a limit is hit without an answer.
problem: A fresh restart repeats all the spent work, and a hard cap can cut a good run short.
best_number: resume 58.2% vs restart 58.6%, 347.4M vs 519.1M Executor tokens (2610.29870)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Resume matched restart at about two thirds of the tokens in one paper; the rerun rule is only argued. Needs checkpoint replay support.

what_and_how: Keep the last 50 rejected or uncertain patches; before verifying a new proposal, compute its similarity to each stored denial and skip it above 0.6.
problem: The proposer keeps suggesting near copies of edits already rejected, wasting verification calls.
best_number: 9.4 calls without the buffer, 6.2 with it (2610.39158)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: One image-generation paper, authors' own system, no named baseline model.

what_and_how: Before each optional tool call or question, estimate the expected loss from acting without its answer and run it only if that exceeds its cost; ask for labels only when the top action's probability sits in a middle band.
problem: Agents run every available check or question whether or not it can change the decision.
best_number: regret 0.00 at 30% of the deliberation cost of executing every tool (2610.16015)
novelty: novel: prices each optional tool call or question against its expected gain, stops when none pays
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Tested with scripted oracles and a no-language-model learner, never a live agent; worth a trial where tool calls are expensive.

what_and_how: Set the model's reasoning effort to low, medium or high for the whole run and measure accuracy, time and tokens at each level on your own tasks before choosing the default.
problem: Reasoning effort changes accuracy and cost by large factors and the right level depends on the model.
best_number: Claude Opus 5.5 low effort 49.5 vs high effort 76.6 overall (2610.16577)
verdict: survived: On strong Claude models, raising reasoning effort from low to medium or high buys large score gains; beyond high it flattens.
recommendation: build-in-regime: Raise effort on Claude models, where gains are large; above medium on GPT models it adds cost for little.

what_and_how: Map each task description or each request to a reasoning effort level, and sometimes a tool-call budget, using a rubric or a wrapper, and enforce the choice with runtime hooks; abstain to the shipped default when unsure.
problem: One effort level wastes tokens on easy tasks and under-thinks hard ones.
best_number: DeepSeek Harness effort arm −74.7% billed cost, 15/15 success (2608.01347)
verdict: survived: Raising reasoning effort above the middle setting on GPT models multiplies time and tokens for little or no mean score change.
recommendation: test-first: One arm cut billed cost by 74.7 percent, the rubric router lost four pass points at 21 percent lower cost; authors' own tasks.

what_and_how: Bind each role, graph node or step type to a fixed model: a stronger one for planning and verdicts, a cheaper or local one for high-volume mechanical steps, with fallback chains when a role is unset.
problem: Using the strongest model for every step spends most money on routine work.
best_number: none
verdict: contested: Routing to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache and delegation raised cost.
recommendation: test-first: All four papers only argue it and none measured a saving; contested idea.

what_and_how: Score each route by predicted success probability minus a weight times its mean observed cost, or fit cost and success models on logged runs and pick the cheapest action whose predicted success stays above a floor.
problem: Fixed routing ignores that cost and success vary by task and state.
best_number: 8.5 percentage points over Avengers-Pro at 2 US dollars per task (2609.32213)
verdict: contested: Routing to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache and delegation raised cost.
recommendation: test-first: Authors' own routers on their own benchmarks; one paper only argues it. Needs logged runs to train.

what_and_how: Run the cheapest deployable model or judge first and move to a stronger one only when training accuracy stalls, the budget overruns, or a summed risk score over recent steps passes a threshold; clear traffic is screened by a cheap pre-check.
problem: Stronger models are needed only on a minority of steps or tasks.
verdict: contested: Routing to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache and delegation raised cost.
recommendation: test-first: One paper saved 4.7 times the strong-judge calls, another saved only 4.3 percent of cost because most traffic still reached the reviewer.

pattern: Session-level model choice with payback rule
what_and_how: Pick the model per session by estimated total cost over its expected length and tool steps, not list price. Switch mid-task only when the cheaper stretch lasts longer than n requests, from the write and read prices of both models.
problem: Switching models mid-session discards the prompt cache, so a cheaper model can cost more.
best_number: Fable 5.1 to Sonnet 5 gives n∗ = 291 requests with return (2609.28919)
novelty: novel: break-even request count computed from cache write and read prices of both models
verdict: contested: Routing to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache and delegation raised cost.
recommendation: test-first: Simulated on trace logs with no live run, vendor prices of one date. The arithmetic is cheap to add on a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Have a cheaper model shorten a large tool result and insert only the short text into the main transcript, leaving the strong model's cached prefix intact; delegate only when the remaining turns exceed the weak model's input price over the cached-read price.
problem: Large tool outputs are re-read every turn at the strong model's price.
best_number: delegation saves 13.5% at most aggressive threshold (2610.15093)
verdict: contested: Routing to cheaper models is reported to save 13 to 90 percent, but per-request switching can break the prompt cache and delegation raised cost.
recommendation: test-first: Delegation raised cost in two of four cells at conservative thresholds; savings top out at 13.5 percent in one simulation.

what_and_how: Replace the main model with a smaller, cheaper one when it writes the context summary during compaction, and compare the score against the baseline on the same tasks.
problem: Summaries are written often and the main model's price makes each one costly.
verdict: survived: A cheaper summarizer or discarding reasoning hurt two of three strong models; default self-summarization matched engineered compaction.
recommendation: do-not-build: The cheaper summarizer lowered the score on two of three models in the only measurement; keep the main model for summaries.

what_and_how: Set the summary allowance to the total budget minus protected and kept tokens with a floor of 64, tell the compactor the allowance, and cut the returned text to four times it in characters.
problem: Summaries that overrun or collapse break the context budget or lose rules.
best_number: violation at three runs 47.1% at 300 tokens and 50.0% at 200, against 24.2% to 28.1% at 750 to 2,500 (2611.03223)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: One paper on two cheap models; it shows tiny allowances raise rule violations, so test the allowance on your model.

what_and_how: Let the model emit a short chunk of actions that run without a model query, or review several proposed actions in one call, or compute the next chunk while the current one executes; shrink the chunk when conditions are uncertain.
problem: Each model call costs time and tokens, and many steps need no fresh decision.
best_number: 25.83% at 2.796 million tokens versus 23.61% at 7.664 million (2610.22471)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Measured on robot and interface tasks only; one paper shows forced chunking dropped success from 96% to 74%. Chunk only when safe.

what_and_how: When the model's output matches a stored signature across several calls, run a parameterized template or evaluate the rule in code and skip the model; call the model when a value is missing or the template fails.
problem: Repeated steps pay model cost and latency for an answer code can compute.
best_number: 19–50× latency reduction on pdf-extract (2604.03088)
verdict: survived: Moving repeated steps from model calls into fixed code, compiled behaviors or batched calls cuts cost or latency about 10 to 25 times.
recommendation: test-first: Authors' own systems and latency, not money; the verdict is weak. Strong fit where gateway rules are explicit.

what_and_how: Score every candidate agent against the observed state in one batched yes or no probability call, drop those below a threshold, and always keep at least a third of the pool.
problem: Running every candidate agent costs time though most are irrelevant.
best_number: 26m 53s versus 32m 12s wall clock, one run each (2609.28940)
verdict: survived: Moving repeated steps from model calls into fixed code, compiled behaviors or batched calls cuts cost or latency about 10 to 25 times.
recommendation: test-first: One run per arm and a saving of under a fifth of wall clock; the verdict is weak.

what_and_how: Keep a subset of each skill's stored keys chosen by farthest-first traversal, so every dropped key lies within a set distance of a kept one; the score then drops by at most that distance.
problem: Skill banks grow large and slow routing and memory.
best_number: shrinks the skill banks about 8.5× at a cost of at most 1.6 points (2609.15982)
novelty: novel: farthest-first key pruning with a stated bound on score loss
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Applies to a hidden-state skill router, so reuse needs similar keys; one paper, authors' own benchmarks.

what_and_how: Put each tool definition in the system message once, in compact typed syntax, and count tokens per trajectory, instead of resending definitions in every turn.
problem: Repeated tool definitions inflate input tokens on every turn.
best_number: Harmony overflow 0.2% (1/500) MEDIUM, 2.8% (14/500) HIGH (2604.00362)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: One small-model paper, no baseline; context overflow rose at high effort. Likely free on providers with prompt caching, so measure first.

what_and_how: Cap generated tokens per model request, such as 1,024, and end the episode when a response is cut off at the cap.
problem: Long generations cost tokens and time and can run away.
best_number: menu penalty -43.7 to -2.7 pp at 16,384 tokens (2610.21098)
verdict: survived: Limits on tool output and reply length, such as completion caps and truncation, cause much of the loss between harnesses.
recommendation: test-first: The paper shows a low cap truncates replies and costs accuracy; if you cap, set it high and count truncations.

what_and_how: Pack all model calls of one conversation into a single sequence: each call's prompt branches off the previous prompt, and an attention mask lets each branch see only the trunk before it and itself.
problem: Training on each call separately repeats the shared prefix many times.
best_number: packed sequences average 16.5k tokens versus 107k to 120k tokens on average when processed separately (2611.15268)
novelty: novel: one sequence per conversation with a branch-aware mask, removing repeated prompt tokens
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Measured on one 12B model in a training pipeline; only useful if you train small local models on your own conversations.

what_and_how: Deduct every decoded frame from a per-question budget, reject requests past the remainder, let transcript lookups cost nothing, and cap frames per answering call at 40 while allowing several calls.
problem: Video questions can pull unlimited frames and the cost grows without bound.
best_number: AKS-90 held-out 49.2 vs searched 54.8 (2608.24302)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Two papers on video questions only; the budget is enforced by the interface, which suits any input type with a metered cost.

what_and_how: Read input, cached-input and output tokens from each transcript, weight them at the billed prices, release the raw counts, and reconcile ledger totals against raw events and the invoice; estimate cache reads from prefixes shared within a task.
problem: List prices and flat token counts misstate real cost, up to threefold or more.
best_number: weighting alone changes a cost effect up to threefold (2610.20673)
verdict: survived: Cost claims need cost per solved task from checked usage; token counts, flat input pricing or list-price weights mislead.
recommendation: build: Nine papers found cost errors from sloppy accounting; cheap deterministic code. Reconcile against the real invoice.

what_and_how: Sum tokens of every attempt including failed ones, divide by the number solved, and record tokens by the action that caused them; report this beside the success rate, not per-attempt cost.
problem: Per-attempt cost hides what a deployer pays for each success.
models: Qwen 3.6 Plus, MiniMax M2.5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, gpt-5.4-nano
verdict: survived: Cost claims need cost per solved task from checked usage; token counts, flat input pricing or list-price weights mislead.
recommendation: build: Cheap deterministic code that every cost decision needs. The efficiency formula in one paper is arbitrary, so test it.

what_and_how: Keep a configuration only if no other has equal or better score at equal or lower mean cost, optionally after a usability threshold fixed in advance, and choose from the resulting frontier per budget.
problem: A single scalar score hides that near-equal harnesses differ by several times in cost.
models: GPT-6 Luna with Codex, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with Codex
best_number: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with Codex 85.6% (2610.35767)
verdict: survived: Between mature harnesses pass rate differs little while cost per task differs up to three times, so compare cost with pass rate.
recommendation: build: Simple reporting rule backed by six papers on cost spread.

what_and_how: Run the unchanged base harness with the evolved harness's average call budget, using majority vote or pass at k, plus direct and retry-once arms on the same tasks, and credit only the gain beyond them.
problem: Extra attempts alone explain a share of reported harness gains.
best_number: 49% of the gain recovered by a compute-matched baseline (2610.22466)
verdict: survived: Credit a harness gain only after comparing it with equal-budget repeated sampling of the starting harness; extra attempts recover a share of the gain.
recommendation: build: A control run catches false savings; low cost.

pattern: Cost term in objective or admission
what_and_how: Add an efficiency term to the reward counted only on success, put context size on the search objective, or break score ties by the lower verified cost when admitting a candidate.
problem: Optimizers chase accuracy and ignore the tokens and steps spent.
best_number: ALFWorld average success 95.0 full, 92.9 without diversity, 86.4 without efficiency (2608.05446)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Three papers by their own authors; one only argues it. Cheap to add to a self-improving loop in a multi-role code pipeline.

what_and_how: Run many candidates through cheap stages first: static check, short prefix, a bootstrap gate, then a full set; or run to checkpoints and keep top survivors; or halve with growing prefixes of one shared item order, reusing cached outcomes.
problem: Evaluating every candidate on the full set is the bulk of search cost.
best_number: average test score 0.7084 vs 0.6973 for Full (ShinkaEvolve), cost 43.8% vs 84.4% (2610.37276)
verdict: survived: Harness search can score candidates on a subset, race or cascade them, cutting evaluation cost about 40 to 60 percent for a near-equal harness.
recommendation: test-first: Four papers by their own authors, no outside replication, verdict weak; the cost saving is large enough to try in any harness search.

what_and_how: Score candidates with a one-step ranking test or on micro-scale generated data of 50 to 200 samples so each rollout ends in seconds, instead of running a full optimization or a full evaluation.
problem: Full evaluation runs take hours and hundreds of dollars.
verdict: survived: Harness search can score candidates on a subset, race or cascade them, cutting evaluation cost about 40 to 60 percent for a near-equal harness.
recommendation: test-first: Two papers, authors' own proxies, no outside check that the proxy ranks like the full run; verify rank agreement first.

what_and_how: Keep results from earlier work: live lookups in a process cache with prewarming, paper analyses under their link, compiled artefacts once per epoch, a saved run when a successor equals a probed candidate, and the validation score of the active baseline.
problem: The same fetches, analyses and evaluations are paid for again each cycle.
best_number: mean latency 1648.23ms to 69.40ms (2607.08028)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Gains are large but come from authors' own systems; two papers only argue it. Invalidate on change, or stale results mislead.

what_and_how: Give each optimizer role one request with no tools and structured output, so one round costs about five calls instead of a tool-using session that resends growing context; write one new harness per round, not several candidates.
problem: Tool-using optimizer sessions resend long context and cost many times more.
best_number: $8.24 to $24.30 per run vs $118.47 to $190.32 for HarnessX reproduction, 13.0× lower (2609.33146)
novelty: novel: optimizer built from single tool-free structured calls, no growing session context
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Compared only against the authors' reproduction of one system, one evolution run per benchmark; worth testing in a pipeline's self-improving loop.

what_and_how: A stronger model writes candidate harness updates or skills offline; accepted updates persist and only the small model runs online, so online latency stays near the small-model baseline. Training-time teacher calls are one-off.
problem: A frontier model on every request is too costly for small-model deployments.
verdict: survived: A stronger model adapting skills to fit a weak executor beats giving the weak model the generic skill or bank directly.
recommendation: build-in-regime: Helps weak executors, up to a capability floor; one paper is measured, one argued.
