what_and_how: Use the target model itself, not a stronger external model, to write and revise skills from its own rollouts, so evaluation stays on the target model and optimization costs about half.
problem: A stronger teacher adds cost and teaches in a style the target model may not follow.
best_number: 72.5 self-teaching versus 73.5 with GPT-5.5 teacher (2609.11682)
verdict: survived: A model can edit its own harness; an outside stronger proposer or teacher adds little.
recommendation: test-first: One point behind a strong teacher on one model; ideas on teacher strength disagree. Cheap to try for small local models.

what_and_how: Run a cheap single-slot probe to find the slot with the largest gain, then spend the whole search budget on that slot instead of splitting it evenly across slots.
problem: An even split across harness parts dilutes the budget over parts that carry no gain.
best_number: all-to-control 0.761 at 32 rollouts vs 0.657 for the four-way split at 64 (2609.02889)
opposes: Even budget split across harness parts
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: One small model on one benchmark, no repeated runs; the finding is that most gain sat in one slot.

what_and_how: Let a cheap lexical retrieval keep the top 20 candidates, then have a small model re-rank only that shortlist; use it only where the re-ranker beats the retrieval baseline.
problem: Scoring every candidate with a model is costly, and small models can be worse than plain retrieval.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: Helped at 4B, hurt at 0.6B and 8B in one paper; check per model before relying on it.

what_and_how: Quantize each local model to 4-bit with round-to-nearest, GPTQ or AWQ, about 4.125 bits per weight, rerun the frozen protocol and check whether the model stays eligible for its role.
problem: Smaller weights cut memory and cost but may break the model's reliability in a role.
best_number: AWQ-4B T1 false approval 0.41 to 0.89; none become eligible (2610.00025)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: do-not-build: None of the quantized models became eligible and false approvals rose sharply; do not quantize a model used as a checker.

what_and_how: Split tasks into search, selection and test sets. The optimizer sees feedback only on the first two. Freeze the chosen harness, run the test set once, and report that score. Keep graders and hidden labels outside the optimizer workspace.
problem: Gains measured on the tasks that guided the search overstate real gains.
best_number: held-out 47% at B=5, 67% at B=100, baseline 51% (2609.39304)
verdict: survived: A harness gain measured on the tasks that guided its search overstates the held-out gain; always report a separate held-out split.
recommendation: build: cheap and proven; every harness needs a frozen test split that no search or tuning step reads.

what_and_how: Run every task several times (three to ten) in fresh sessions. Report the mean with spread or interval, plus any-pass and all-pass counts, pass@k from the unbiased estimator, and mean-of-n beside best-of-n.
problem: One run per task cannot separate a harness effect from run-to-run variation.
best_number: 81.35 at $1.01 (three runs) against 75.71 at $0.97 (one run) (2611.02079)
verdict: survived: A single run per task cannot separate a harness effect from run-to-run variation; repeat runs and report spread before trusting any difference.
recommendation: build: for any harness; a cheap hosted model pays for repeats directly, a small local model can afford many.

what_and_how: Rerun the baseline arm with identical settings and count tasks whose outcome flips; treat gaps under that flip rate as noise. Add paired tests (exact McNemar, Wilcoxon, task bootstrap, resolution band) and a null built from split halves or placebo series.
problem: Small score gaps between harnesses are often only run-to-run noise.
best_number: 9 changed outcome (18.75%) of 48 tasks (2611.19359)
verdict: survived: A single run on tens of tasks cannot separate harnesses: swapping the harness flips about as many tasks as rerunning the same harness.
recommendation: build: measure your own rerun flip rate before reading any harness gap; for any harness, cheapest for small local models.

what_and_how: Run the candidate and the current harness on the same tasks, seeds, model and budget, changing one thing. Compare per-task differences (mean, median, sign test) instead of two separate averages. Use fresh isolated workspaces so runs do not leak state.
problem: Separate averages mix harness effect with task mix, model and budget differences.
models: Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen3.8-Flash, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
best_number: Splendor +58.3 percentage points [50.0, 75.0] (2610.35773)
verdict: survived: With the model held fixed, switching the whole harness can swing results by 10 to 44 points, and the best harness depends on the model.
recommendation: build: use for every harness change in any harness; it is the base of every other comparison.

what_and_how: Run every model under every harness on one fixed task set. Report the model average, harness average and the interaction residual per pair, a fit score against the best harness, and variance split into model, harness, interaction and run noise.
problem: A harness that helps one model may hurt another; pooled averages hide it.
models: GLM-5.1, GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.6, MiniMax M3
best_number: Ranking reversal pairs: 6 out of 9 (2605.23950)
verdict: survived: No single harness wins everywhere: the best harness changes with the model and the benchmark, so test model and harness as a pair.
recommendation: build: test each model you ship on in your harness as a pair; do not publish a harness-versus-model variance ratio, that claim was superseded.

what_and_how: Before crediting a harness, run the bare model or a plain default agent with the same call, token and attempt budget, including self-consistency with matched samples. Also report what a deterministic tool alone finds and what the union adds.
problem: Extra retries and compute can explain much of a harness gain.
best_number: extended single-product budget 33.3% vs heterogeneous pair 62.5% on HSTU (2609.39551)
verdict: survived: Retries, limits and call counts explain much of reported harness gains, so compare against a bare model given the same budget.
recommendation: build: required on a cheap hosted model and in a multi-role pipeline, where extra attempts are the main cost.

what_and_how: Add an arm that keeps the form of the change but removes its content: a neutral note, shuffled answers, shuffled timing, shuffled context, padding of equal length, identical clones of the baseline, or a sham controller that fires at the same moments.
problem: A gain may come from extra text, extra training or luck rather than the mechanism.
models: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5 xhigh
best_number: shift 60.00%, capacity-aligned LoRA 54.74%, base 54.74% (2611.01415)
verdict: survived: Judging a memory feature needs matched controls and repeated runs; neutral or placebo arms explain apparent gains.
recommendation: test-first: the surviving idea covers memory features only; add one neutral-note arm to your own change and see if the gain survives.

what_and_how: Change one thing and observe the effect: remove a decisive record, delete marked reasoning and resume, inject a stale observation, plant a fact or a fault, reverse field order, or degrade the task spec. Measure rescue and harm per case.
problem: Whole-harness comparison cannot show which mechanism causes an effect.
best_number: 3.0% of SWE-bench Verified turns changed vs 25.0% with all reasoning deleted (2611.07238)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: widely built but no idea judges the method itself; useful for diagnosis in any harness, treat single results as hypotheses.

what_and_how: Record a run, freeze the computation up to one point, then replay the same history under different harness contracts, report placements or scrubbed cues. Reuse saved trajectories to compare many candidates or scorers without new model calls.
problem: Comparing live runs mixes the harness effect with new sampling noise.
best_number: 1.07× to 5.38× from native to scrubbed (2610.09944)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: cheap and deterministic, but no verdict exists; try it in a multi-role pipeline to compare reviewers on stored runs.

what_and_how: Remove or isolate one harness component at a time, or run all subsets (Shapley, leave-one-in, leave-one-out), same night and same model. Compare each part to the full harness and to a generic reminder; reintroduce one defect to check the effect.
problem: A harness gain cannot be credited to a specific part without controlled removal.
best_number: development 0.366 full, 0.317 without lessons file (2610.11655)
verdict: survived: Harness parts do not add up: single gains do not sum to the full harness, and some parts lower scores.
recommendation: build: one change per run in any harness; do not assume part gains add up.

what_and_how: Freeze the harness chosen with one model, then run it unchanged on unseen tasks and on models absent from the optimization. Report the gain over the seed harness for each model, with no feedback flowing back.
problem: A harness tuned on one model may not carry over to other models.
models: Opus 5, GLM-4.7 Flash, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, GPT-OSS-120B
verdict: contested: Evolved harness edits transfer unevenly: they can help other models, but coverage falls on other task families, so test transfer on both.
recommendation: test-first: results disagree across papers; check any shipped harness on each target model, especially small local models.

what_and_how: Feed experience in batches that alternate between task mixtures or change tool schemas, with a fixed task-disjoint test set. Fill a stage-by-cohort accuracy matrix, report backward transfer, and count tasks gained and lost separately.
problem: Net scores hide forgetting and drift when a harness keeps changing.
models: GPT-5 Codex, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5.4, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
best_number: backward transfer −34.7% on ALE (2609.04280)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: useful for any harness that learns across sessions; no verdict exists, so run it only on harnesses that change over time.

what_and_how: Write binary or weighted checklist items per task before scoring. A strong model judge scores each item separately against a reference, the output files and the logged tool calls. Cap high-volume items and hide the rubric from the solver.
problem: Open-ended outputs have no executable test, so quality needs graded criteria.
models: Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.8, GLM-5.1
best_number: 90.4% agreement with human labels, kappa 0.80 (2610.38231)
verdict: survived: A strong judge scoring each rubric item separately, with a reference or evidence, agrees with human labels in about 83 to 96 percent of cases.
recommendation: build: for generated outputs with no test; check the judge against human labels on a sample first.

what_and_how: Test the judge before trusting it: repeat it three to five times and take the median, add a second judge from another model family, swap the order of pairs, compare with human raters, and score judges against planted defects.
problem: Model judges drift with prompt, session and model family.
models: GLM-5.3-Flash, Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Astra
best_number: usability agreement 93.0% versus 92.9% for humans (2611.06506)
verdict: survived: Model-judge scores shift by several points with judge choice, prompt or session, so fix and validate the judging protocol before comparing harnesses.
recommendation: build: any harness with outside reviewers or a model judge needs these checks; start with repeat judging and a second model family.

what_and_how: Score by running deterministic code on the result: hidden tests, database or file state diffs, rule-based checkers, kernel or service records, exact answer matching with aliases. No model judge; the verifier is the only scorer.
problem: Model opinions are noisy; real effects can be checked by code.
best_number: 88.3% test pass rate, 63.9% reward pass rate (2606.07462)
verdict: survived: An agent's own finish report is unreliable on strong models; a read-only outside check of real files or state catches false completion.
recommendation: build: default grading for code-change pipelines and for change requests inside an organisation; put the grader outside the agent.

what_and_how: Run the grader in a separate container or process with its own seeds, timer and hidden inputs. The agent cannot read hidden labels or reference answers, and score tools return only a number. Start each trial from a fresh container.
problem: An agent or search loop will exploit a visible or fixed-input grader.
best_number: TSVC s311 answer scores 5309× on fixed inputs and 20× on new draws (2610.20673)
verdict: survived: A weak or fixed-input evaluator is exploited by search or by the agent, so score with a repaired check, fresh inputs or an outside oracle.
recommendation: build: cheap hygiene for every harness that lets a model search or iterate against a score.

what_and_how: Grade beyond the final output: a separate constraint suite, authorization contract, trajectory checks, safety-gated or checkpoint-weighted completion, and first-failure grading. A run passes only if outcome and process both pass.
problem: Passing the output check hides policy violations and skipped steps.
models: Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6
best_number: 221 of 644 functional passes fail the constraint suite (2609.04167)
verdict: survived: Passing the functional or final-output check overstates acceptable work, so add process and policy checks.
recommendation: build: required where an organisation's own policy rules apply, since policy breaches matter as much as correctness.

what_and_how: Pair each risky or trap task with a twin that removes the trap but keeps the workflow. Count a defence or failure only if the twin passes. Add decoy tools or targets so a wrong pick is detectable.
problem: A safe-looking run may only reflect a model that cannot do the task.
best_number: the input connection moves Llama-3.3-70B from 7th to 3rd place (2611.01930)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: sound idea, no verdict; try it where a defence can be confused with inability, mainly for small local models.

what_and_how: Before using a task, require its reference solution to pass and the unmodified start state to fail. Filter by difficulty and blind-guess rate, scrub the answer from history, check each grader, and review cases with experts.
problem: Broken tasks and graders move scores by tens of points.
models: Qwen3.7 Plus, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro
best_number: gate on stale labels admitted 0 of 8,490 candidates (2610.10629)
verdict: survived: Benchmark and grader defects are common and move scores by tens of points; audit tasks, oracles and scorers with a reference solution and replay.
recommendation: build: run before any harness comparison in any harness; one reference-solution check per task is cheap.

what_and_how: Generate tasks from real sources: mined issues, scenario frames, masked arguments, seeded faults. Gate each with a reference solution, real solver rollouts, a difficulty band and a validator agent, then admit by expert review.
problem: Hand-written test sets are small, stale and leak into training.
best_number: best single method below 20% (2609.02302)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: widely built but not judged; for a software pipeline, synthesize tasks from your own repository history and gate each with a reference fix.

what_and_how: Score harness candidates on a small task subset chosen by difficulty bands, energy distance or information gain, with sparse or multi-fidelity scoring in search and full scoring only for finalists. Weight sampling by outcome variance.
problem: Full evaluation of every candidate harness costs too much.
best_number: partial rank correlation 0.983 at 50 tasks; 5.9× fewer tasks (2609.40284)
verdict: survived: A small task subset keeps the coarse model ranking but cannot resolve harness gaps under about five points.
recommendation: build-in-regime: use for coarse ranking and search screening only; confirm a final choice on the full set.

what_and_how: Estimate a harness score from the model decision state instead of full runs: ceiling minus mismatch from sampled actions, a value head trained on measured harness utility, or an item-response model fitted on warm-up candidates.
problem: Running every candidate harness with the target model is expensive.
best_number: success 85.0% to 19.2% with reversed fields (2610.37255)
novelty: novel: scores a harness from the model decision geometry, with no target-model runs.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: three papers by their own authors, no outside check; try for ranking harnesses for small local models.

what_and_how: Label each failed run by a fixed ordered list (earliest break, exception-first, first signal that fires) using code or a blinded reviewer. Report counts per category, stage-wise recall, and failures per harness rather than one score.
problem: A single score hides where and why runs fail.
models: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Kimi-K3, Claude Opus 5, Codex GPT-5.5
best_number: 14.6 closed book, 89.6 open book on context-grounded reasoning (2609.18270)
verdict: survived: Which way a run fails is shaped by the harness, so failure patterns repeat across models; check failure mode counts per harness.
recommendation: build: cheap diagnosis for every harness; use code rules first and a blinded model reviewer only for ambiguous cases.

what_and_how: Route every request through one proxy that logs input, cached and output tokens and tool calls. Report cost per solved task, cost of failed runs separately, cache-aware billing, and time split into agent and environment parts.
problem: Pass rate alone hides large cost differences between harnesses.
models: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, DeepSeek V4 Flash, gpt-5.6-luna, Fable 5.1
best_number: flat pricing overstates cost 7.14 times on average (2610.15093)
verdict: survived: Between mature harnesses on a fixed model, pass rate differs little while cost differs up to 3 times, so compare cost and tokens too.
recommendation: build: essential on a cheap hosted model; one logging proxy serves any harness.

pattern: Pareto frontier instead of one score
what_and_how: Keep every evaluated candidate, score accuracy, cost and latency separately, and keep only candidates no other candidate beats on all of them. Run held-out tests only on that frontier.
problem: One weighted score forces an accuracy-cost trade-off to be fixed in advance.
best_number: average Pareto rank 5.59 vs 10.83 (2609.38883)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: sensible for choosing between harness candidates, mostly argued; try on a cheap hosted model where cost matters.

what_and_how: Score an attack only when the payload reached the model and the tool call matches by name and argument. Test many carriers and channels, source-to-sink traces, and fault-seeded corpora with benign twins to grade tamper detection.
problem: Scoring attacks by tool name gives wrong security numbers.
best_number: 21.7% attack success by tool name vs 1.2% by argument level (2609.32691)
verdict: survived: Scoring attacks by tool name instead of checking payload delivery gives wrong security numbers; validate scoring on saved traces.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence; validate attack scoring on saved traces before trusting a defence result.

what_and_how: Combine weighted parts into one score: partial credit, artifact plus process, safety gate times quality, soft matching, hard gate on failed artifacts. Report answer rate, completion and full-pass rate beside it.
problem: Pass or fail hides partial progress and unusable runs.
models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-5.6
best_number: Collab Toolbox mean reward 22.3 to 35.1 percent (2610.34679)
verdict: survived: A mean score hides answer rate, partial completion, full-pass rate and task turnover, so report completion and full-pass rate next to it.
recommendation: build: report partial credit with full-pass rate and answer rate; avoid inventing weights without checking they rank like humans.

what_and_how: Report model, harness, environment, evaluator, token cap and protocol as separate fields on every score. Classify each condition as locked, shared or native and route model calls through one bridge. Use a structured card per score.
problem: Scores from different setups are not comparable.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Scores from different setups are not comparable: channel, harness version, judge, model or token cap each move results, so report the full setup.
recommendation: build: free to do; keep a setup record next to every score in any harness.

what_and_how: Commit the analysis plan, thresholds and decision rules before results, as a hash-chained registry with a timestamped change log; fix splits, budgets and tolerances in a sealed manifest or acceptance gate before the held-out run.
problem: Choosing contrasts and thresholds after seeing results inflates findings.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only; cheap for a release gate for an organisation that ships code changes, no measured value yet.

what_and_how: Run the task with no history (blind) and with the correct hidden state (oracle) to bound what a harness can gain, or give the model the gold abstract to bound the effect of perfect retrieval.
problem: Without bounds, a harness score cannot show how much headroom is left.
models: Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
best_number: Oracle 95.4 vs Blind 14.1 average Hidden (2610.07792)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: simple upper and lower bounds, three papers; run once per new task family to see if a harness can matter.

what_and_how: Have several raters score outputs blind, under neutral labels, on a fixed scenario set with paired tests, or use two blind raters with an agreement check. Use experts to admit finalist tasks.
problem: Model judges may agree with each other and not with people.
best_number: pooled mean 4.08 vs ASA (GPT-5) 1.23 across ten raters (ext-llm-academic-supervision-harness-case-study)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: small samples by system authors; use a few human raters to calibrate model judges.

what_and_how: Compute counts from logged trajectories: no-action turns, interface mismatch rate, prescribed versus model-chosen calls, tool-usage rate by outcome, reading boundary, initiator labels, answer rate. Report beside the score.
problem: Equal scores can hide very different working behavior and wasted turns.
models: Qwen 3.6 Plus, MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-Flash
best_number: OpenCode 2.0–2.16 vs Goose 0.2–0.3 no-action turns per task (2607.22585)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: cheap to log; track no-action turns and interface mismatches in a harness for a small local model before trusting them as signals.

what_and_how: Recognize which harness, copy or behavior produced a run from outside: an eight-number behavior profile retrieval, a keyed search-order mark checked against other keys, probes of timeouts and masking, and randomized token ranks.
problem: Nobody can tell which harness ran, whether it was copied or how it behaves.
best_number: 34 of 35 GEPA copies detected; gpt-oss-120b: 0 of 6 (2610.21458)
novelty: novel: identifies a harness or its copy from outside, using behavior, keys and probes.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: new in October and November 2026, mostly authors scoring their own marks; relevant only where an organisation's code review flow applies.

what_and_how: Take a harness or skill library built by one model and run it with a different model, with and without it, changing only the profile. Swap libraries between students or solver checkpoints to separate builder skill from runner skill.
problem: A harness built by a strong model may only work for that model.
models: GPT-5.6 Terra high, GPT-5.6 Luna high, Claude Sonnet 5 high, DeepSeek-V4-Flash
best_number: Sol-built harnesses lose 19–26 points when they play them (2610.30499)
novelty: novel: swaps who built the harness and who runs it to isolate each effect.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: three papers from October to November 2026; use when a strong model writes the harness for a weaker runner.

what_and_how: Check that a control really binds real effects: run each case twice on identical state with Approve and Reject, replay a fixed action workload with no model, reconcile control logs with kernel events, and predict checkable paths from source.
problem: A recorded approval click does not prove the decision controlled real effects.
models: GPT-6.1-Sol, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Claude Haiku 5.5
novelty: novel: pairs Approve and Reject runs and checks real effects, with kernel records.
verdict: survived: Approval steps fail at the binding: saved confirmations survive changed state, reject paths still execute, so verify each approval against the actual effect.
recommendation: build: check every approval or policy gate against the real effect, not the log.

what_and_how: Score a learning harness with no gold labels: a stronger same-family teacher supplies pseudo-labels and the score is how far the student moves toward the teacher. Check with sabotaged labels and a same-strength judge.
problem: Gold labels are costly; harness uplift needs a cheap estimate.
best_number: pooled 48% reliability against gold (2608.13608)
verdict: survived: Harness uplift can be estimated without gold labels by using a stronger teacher model, until the capability gap between teacher and student is small.
recommendation: test-first: one author team, small old models, no coefficient reported; try only where labels are missing.

what_and_how: Run harness search for a fixed number of rounds, then report the final harness on existing and held-out tasks, with no validation set to choose when to stop.
problem: A validation stop adds cost and a second split to a search loop.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Naive evolution loops gain most in the first few iterations and later edits can lower held-out scores, so cap iterations and keep the best snapshot.
recommendation: do-not-build: argued only, and a surviving idea shows later edits can lower held-out scores; keep the best validated snapshot.

what_and_how: Run each model in the harness its vendor ships and its users likely use, with nearly all native tools on, instead of one shared scaffold. Compare shared and native designs on the same tasks.
problem: A shared scaffold may favor some models and misstate real-world performance.
best_number: shared harness wins 11 of 20 model-task pairs, native 9 (2608.06301)
verdict: contested: Vendor-built harnesses do not reliably beat neutral or minimal harnesses on the same model; some help their own model, some hurt it.
recommendation: test-first: contested; the benchmark has no bare baseline, so vendor gaps mix model and harness effects.

what_and_how: The model keeps a bounded notes document of findings, leads, approaches tried, lessons and next steps, and rewrites it each round or episode. The full log stays outside context; the harness injects the notes every turn.
problem: Long runs lose what they learned once old turns leave the window.
best_number: GPT-6-Astra 46.7 to 81.7 on EBench (Table 1) (2611.11509)
verdict: survived: When a task needs information that outlives the context, removing that external state costs points on strong models.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; keep notes bounded and harness-injected.

what_and_how: One system prompt sentence asks the model to write anything it wants to carry forward into each visible reply, so facts stay in view after old turns are dropped. No store, no retrieval code.
problem: Facts vanish when old turns are truncated and the model cannot re-observe them.
best_number: 28.5% with notes vs 7.5% without (2610.26632)
novelty: novel: memory carried in the model's own visible output, with no store or code
verdict: survived: On long tasks that outgrow the window, one continuous conversation with summarized old turns and a note-taking instruction scores far above a stateless default setup.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, one run per setup on game tasks; cheapest option, so try it first for small local models.

what_and_how: Give the model the complete unmodified history of every earlier episode, or the whole skill bank, instead of reflections or top-few retrieval. Drop the oldest episodes only when the budget is exceeded.
problem: Reflection and retrieval layers lose detail and sometimes score below the stateless model.
best_number: Kimi K3 MEMORY: Max 63.3, Mean 48.0, learning gain +16.9 (2610.08215)
opposes: Distilled lesson store retrieved into prompt
verdict: survived: Keeping complete unmodified interaction history is at least as good as reflection or rule extraction; reflection harnesses are less consistent than raw context.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; make it the baseline every memory add-on must beat, while history fits the window.

pattern: Raw history kept and searched on demand
what_and_how: Store the full trace unchanged as the authoritative record outside the window. The agent reaches it through grep, a keyed read or a recall tool; the prompt holds only a compressed view or keys.
problem: Truncated or summarized windows drop facts the agent cannot observe again.
best_number: GPT-5.5 pass@1 41.2 versus no-log 24.0 (Table 3, page 9) (2607.20064)
verdict: survived: A truncated or summarized window drops facts the agent cannot observe again; keep such facts in persistent state or make them re-readable.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; keep the raw log and give a search tool.

what_and_how: Before dropping or summarizing tool output, save it verbatim to a file store under an event identifier, and leave a stub with the identifier and size. A recall tool returns the original on request.
problem: Context cuts delete evidence fields silently and break results.
best_number: Mean difference T2 minus T1 is −0.36 percentage points across 32 comparisons (2609.20804)
verdict: survived: Cutting tool output by character position deletes whole evidence fields and breaks results silently; cut by record or keep results re-readable.
recommendation: test-first: re-readability survived on failure counts only, and the one controlled comparison shows no accuracy change; measure your own long runs.

pattern: Distilled lesson store retrieved into prompt
what_and_how: After a run a model distils the trajectory into short lessons, cards or rules, stores them, and retrieves the top few by similarity or tags into the next prompt.
problem: Agents repeat past mistakes and cannot reuse what earlier runs found.
best_number: Qwen3-8B: average 52.22 versus Base+Harness 38.34 (ScienceWorld within-domain) (2610.34724)
verdict: survived: Generic frozen memory or experience add-ons on small models often score at or below the plain model; gains appear only for add-ons built for that task and executor.
recommendation: test-first: most built, but the verdict says generic add-ons often lose to the plain model; test against raw history first on every harness.

what_and_how: Keep separate stores for working state (always in the prompt, flushed per task), episodes (retrieved) and distilled patterns or rules; promote entries upward only after repeated success or corroboration.
problem: One flat store mixes temporary state with durable rules.
best_number: stateless harness 79.4 versus full 86.1 on GenEval2 (2610.39158)
verdict: contested: Structured memory (typed, hierarchical or commit-only records) beats flat raw history in the authors' ablations, but a rigorous raw-history baseline matched or beat reflection and compression.
recommendation: test-first: authors' own ablations only and raw-history baselines matched them; build a flat log first, add tiers if it fails.

pattern: Failure records fed to the editor
what_and_how: Store each failed check, rejected change or failure class as a record (certificate, diagnosis card, forbidden pattern, theme) and show relevant records to the next proposer so it does not repeat the fix.
problem: Self-editing loops retry fixes that already failed.
best_number: Qwen3-Coder-Plus: passing correctness checks 55% to 90% (2609.34069)
verdict: survived: Failure-derived rules help most on tasks the model never solves and add nothing on tasks it mostly solves.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only where the bare model often fails; weak authors-only evidence.

what_and_how: Store every evaluated harness candidate with score, cost, diff and execution trace, rejected ones included, and let the proposer read or retrieve from the archive so search avoids dead ends and recombines parts.
problem: Harness search repeats regressions and forgets earlier winners.
models: Kimi-K3, Claude Opus 4.8, Qwen3.5-9B, Claude Haiku 4.5
best_number: Kimi-K3 held-out resolve rate 64.00% with library added to Meta-Harness, 63.00% without (2609.32423)
verdict: stale: Keeping full traces, not only scores, helps an automatic search for a better memory or retrieval harness.
recommendation: test-first: stale verdict; the held-out gain is one point and a playbook from the archive scored below no playbook; measure before building.

what_and_how: Keep the working artifacts between attempts: demonstration pairs by task, the program that passed, the previous controller file, one workspace per task, the selected harness. Only the model context resets.
problem: Re-deriving solved work wastes budget on repeated tasks.
best_number: brisk 4 of 9 from zero file vs 7 of 8 from previous controller (2611.16867)
verdict: survived: On repeated tasks keep concrete artifacts (demonstrations, programs, the previous controller, the workspace), not model-written prose.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; carry only within the same task family, since carrying across domains is contested.

what_and_how: At every resume after compaction, session-start hooks inject the stored notes into the new window, with provenance labels and a staleness warning; a fire ledger clears at compaction so notes re-arm.
problem: Agents never call memory tools on their own, so stored facts are not used.
best_number: Claude Haiku 4.5: 139 audit-logged deliveries (2607.20972)
verdict: survived: Do not rely on the agent to write or read its own memory voluntarily; the harness must trigger writes and inject stored facts at fixed points such as every compaction.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; zero voluntary memory calls were seen.

pattern: Recap of last finding after compaction
what_and_how: After each compaction the instruction gets the explorer sub-agent's latest answer and a short notes page, filled from session-state slots on every model call.
problem: Compaction drops the last finding the next step needs.
verdict: survived: Memory that only repeats what the agent already saw, such as a recap of its last finding after compaction, adds no measurable success.
recommendation: do-not-build: paired test shows no gain on 98 tasks; repeating what the agent already saw is wasted tokens.

what_and_how: Mark old entries superseded when a new one contradicts them, drop memories for an action after an unexpected verdict, weight evidence by freshness, and penalize stale entries at ranking; retrieval skips stamped items.
problem: Stored entries go stale when the environment changes and blind reuse costs points.
best_number: stale usage 0.009 versus 0.271 for no-invalidation variant, page 11 (2606.01886)
verdict: survived: Stored entries go stale when the environment changes, and reusing them blind costs points; memory-based learners keep acting on stale memories after an unannounced rule change.
recommendation: test-first: verdict survived but evidence is weak, simulated settings; cheap to build, so test on your own changing repositories.

what_and_how: Every memory page carries owner, scope, origin list and authority level; derived memory (summaries) takes the lowest authority of its inputs; a revocation counter forces a reload through the map so old checkpoints cannot revive revoked memory.
problem: Memory from low-trust inputs persists and fires again after revocation.
best_number: none
novelty: novel: derived memory inherits the lowest input authority; revocation counters block restored checkpoints
verdict: unmeasured: Memory derived from low-trust inputs should inherit the lowest trust and be revocable.
recommendation: test-first: argued only, no measurement; prototype and attack it before relying on it.

pattern: Memory tests with matched control arms
what_and_how: Test a memory feature with a no-memory arm, a raw-prior-trajectory arm and the memory arm, repeated runs, and fixed hidden injection so only the memory text varies; add placebo or long benign text.
problem: Apparent memory gains come from noise, placebo text or neutral content.
verdict: survived: Judging a memory feature needs matched controls and repeated runs: rerunning an unchanged setup flipped about one task in five, and placebo arms explain apparent gains.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; every memory feature should pass matched arms before it ships.

what_and_how: Check a memory brief against a read-only archive search tool within a call limit, or compare every notebook entry with its source extracts at build time and repair failed notes.
problem: Memory content steers the agent, so wrong entries lower scores.
best_number: repaired 17 of the 18 notes (2609.33822)
verdict: survived: Memory content steers the agent strongly, for good or ill; validate and filter before reuse.
recommendation: test-first: small model gained only from 10.0% to 14.4% on bad memory; one build-time repair count; measure on your own memory.

what_and_how: Rank stored items by embedding similarity, weighted keyword overlap, recency or salience, merged by rank fusion, with a keyword fallback; the agent picks how many to return.
problem: Memory too large to put in the prompt needs selecting.
best_number: Claude Opus 4.6 Chronos: inline vector 83.6, inline grep 93.1 (2605.15184)
verdict: survived: No single memory storage method wins everywhere; the best depends on the model and the capability tested.
recommendation: test-first: no method wins everywhere and plain grep beat vector search in one paper; benchmark two methods on your own data.

what_and_how: A model extracts entities and relations into a graph beside the text; read by traversal, graph distance or personalized spreading, often merged with vector hits; full snapshot text stays on the event node.
problem: Flat similarity misses causal chains and bridges between facts.
best_number: QWEN3-8B LoCoMo judge score 0.648, against 0.561 for the dense index (Table 1, page 6) (2608.15008)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: authors' own benchmarks; one number shows a graph over dense index but a router gain vanished when held out; test against plain retrieval.

what_and_how: Record each observed fact or verified result with its source call and status (active, superseded, contradicted). An action or answer counts as supported only if matching evidence was recorded earlier; the final answer cites active entries only.
problem: Agents act on claims no observation supports.
verdict: survived: When a task needs information that outlives the context (analysis state, evidence state), removing that external state costs points on strong models.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; evidence outside the transcript beat inside 0.77 to 0.60 pooled.

what_and_how: The agent writes a program that holds state and transition rules; the harness rebuilds state by replaying recorded history under that program, or the coding model designs its own persistent data structure.
problem: Prose notes are lossy and hard to check; learned rules need to survive compaction.
best_number: CN04 level 5 in 279 actions with the program vs 1,219 with prose notes (page 6) (2609.39140)
novelty: novel: state is replayable code, not prose notes, rebuilt from the history
verdict: survived: On repeated tasks keep concrete artifacts (demonstrations, programs, the previous controller, the workspace), not model-written prose.
recommendation: test-first: one measured paper on one game, others argued; promising for small local models since code is checkable; try it on one task.

pattern: Compiled rule memory before the model
what_and_how: Match the current situation against an indexed store of verified rules keyed by state variables. Call the model only on a miss and store its verified proposal; use memory alone when a stored case is nearly identical.
problem: Model calls cost money and give drifting answers for situations seen before.
opposes: Distilled lesson store retrieved into prompt
novelty: novel: memory answers first in code; the model is called only on a miss
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one older model, authors only; check the verifier that admits rules.

what_and_how: A separate model call edits the memory design itself (what to record, filters, limits, schema, insert or revise operations) under a validator with caps, and candidates are scored on a benchmark.
problem: Hand-built memory fits no task well.
best_number: LoCoMo 0.459 against Mem0 0.373 (2604.11811)
verdict: survived: Adding a memory system to a harness does not reliably beat the harness's own built-in memory, and the best added system differs by model.
recommendation: test-first: added memory often fails to beat native memory; only authors measured these searches; search cost is high for little certain gain.

what_and_how: After each instance a revision step rewrites the retrieved notes or hypothesis verdicts from the new outcome (corrected, regressed, unchanged), keeping the original beside it; earlier revisions of a function are read before editing.
problem: Notes written once stay wrong, and append-only memory piles up contradictions.
best_number: Claude Opus 4.8: 0.217 with revision, 0.144 without (Table 3) (2610.12668)
novelty: novel: retrieved notes rewritten from the source trajectory after each outcome
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper measures it and the same paper shows reflection below raw history elsewhere; build raw history first.

what_and_how: Each agent role, bot or customer scope owns its memory file or lesson overlay; retrieval resolves the narrowest scope first under isolation, with provenance and token budget.
problem: Shared memory leaks irrelevant or private lessons across roles.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: all argued, none measured; measure leakage and gain against one shared file.

pattern: Plain files in the repository as memory
what_and_how: Notes, decisions, progress logs, known failures and stage outputs live as plain version-controlled files (markdown or a fixed folder schema); later sessions or parallel agents read them, and each file doubles as a resumable checkpoint.
problem: State is lost between sessions and between parallel agents.
best_number: recurrence from 3 of 5 sessions to 0 of 5 (2610.34938)
verdict: stale: File-backed state and handoff files let long runs resume and raise scores; measured only in March on one small model, other support is argued.
recommendation: test-first: stale verdict, one old measurement; cheap and everywhere, so measure resume success on your own runs.

what_and_how: Store whole successful trajectories or demonstration pairs, parameterized with symbolic queries, and place them in context for matching later tasks without distilling them.
problem: Distilled prose loses the detail that makes an example useful.
best_number: GPT-OSS-20B; LawBench pass@1 18.86 baseline, 44.00 rebuilt memory (Table 4) (2610.27889)
verdict: survived: On repeated tasks keep concrete artifacts (demonstrations, programs, the previous controller, the workspace), not model-written prose.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; rebuild per run.

what_and_how: Keep only the last few actions, views and feedback in working memory with a subgoal table (pending, active, completed, blocked) and a guard against reversing moves; failures go to a full log.
problem: Long episodes overflow the window and loop.
best_number: GPT-5.5 R2R subset success rate 43.0 to 50.0 (2609.15195)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: embodied navigation papers by their authors; the idea transfers to loop detection in any harness but is unmeasured there.

what_and_how: For a 1.5 billion parameter local model, pack the window by scoring messages on similarity, overlap, recency and salience; summary buffers written by the same small model cost far more time than truncation.
problem: Small local models have tiny windows and cannot afford slow summarising.
best_number: duration 1862.3 s at 2K against 43.3 s for truncation (page 30) (2609.13149)
verdict: survived: Generic frozen memory or experience add-ons on small models often score at or below the plain model.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only for small local models; scored packing is lean and summaries cost time; one paper, so confirm on your model.

what_and_how: When history expires a model (the same one, a small separate one, or a fixed-schema compressor) writes a short summary or state capsule that replaces it; typed pages never degrade below a minimum fidelity.
problem: Context fills up and dropping turns loses facts.
best_number: DeepSearchQA F1 0.48 vs 0.52 Full History (2611.06445)
verdict: survived: On strong models with very large windows, the default self-summarization is as good as engineered compaction strategies; a cheaper summarizer hurt two of three models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: engineered compaction matters for small models (8 to 12 points) and tight windows; on strong large-window models use the default.

what_and_how: At the serving layer, decide which session's cached context stays in fast storage by segment lifetime class, by predicted session continuation from past gaps, or by evicting the most recently suspended entry first.
problem: Recomputing context for resumed agent sessions is slow and costly.
novelty: novel: cache policy tuned to agent session gaps and segment lifetimes
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: serving infrastructure measured by its own authors; matters only if you run your own server for small local models.

what_and_how: Store each measured object or place with pose, name, timestamp, last-seen state, images and failure annotations; compute answers from stored geometry instead of re-perceiving.
problem: Embodied agents lose where things are once out of view.
best_number: GPT-6 Astra, success weighted by path length 82.2 first visit, 93.3 revisit (2610.39446)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: robot and navigation papers, authors only; skip unless you build embodied agents.

what_and_how: Archive every frame or timed unit at full resolution outside the context, index by time with captions or structured fields (event, people, place), and fetch selected frames on demand.
problem: Video and visual state cannot fit in the window.
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol: 70.05 to 94.10 RHAE when memory and inspection added (2610.02200)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: authors' own benchmarks on visual tasks; not relevant to a harness that handles text only, unless screenshots are used.

what_and_how: Store verified procedures as skills filed by workflow node, bottleneck or transfer scope (general versus topic), load them under a fixed entry budget, and freeze the bank for transfer runs.
problem: Procedures learned once are lost on the next task.
verdict: survived: Skills distilled from trajectories of the same task family give frontier models modest held-out gains of a few points, and weaker models more.
recommendation: build-in-regime: modest gain on strong models, larger on weak ones; keep skills task-matched and tested bare against with-skill.

what_and_how: Keep a Beta posterior or success count per skill, retrieval policy or user; choose by posterior mean, Thompson sample or Wilson bound; promote tiers by use count and success.
problem: Raw success rates mislead with few trials.
best_number: deepseek-v4-flash: 70.0% Bayesian vs 37.5% raw frequency, RealFin-Bench (2606.08348)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: small statistical rule, cheap to add, measured by authors on narrow tasks; test with a held-out stream.

pattern: Strong model writes playbook for weak executor
what_and_how: A stronger agent drives or teaches a frozen weaker one, then records effective strategies as when-to-intervene rules the weak agent reads.
problem: Weak models cannot write their own good guidance.
best_number: GPT-5.6 Luna with GR00T-N1.7: 66.7% with refined playbook versus 43.8% without (2609.33378)
verdict: survived: A stronger model rewriting or adapting skills to fit a weak executor beats giving the weak model the generic skill or bank directly.
recommendation: build-in-regime: for weak executors only; fits small local models with an offline stronger teacher; two papers, authors only.

what_and_how: Write only entries that pass a check (accepted repairs, feedback-verified lessons, verifier-accepted episodes, failed runs only, confidence above a threshold) and cap the store so the cap forces distillation.
problem: Ungated memory accumulates wrong and redundant entries.
best_number: pooled violations about 0.77 at L=0, 0.20 at L=10, 0.25 to 0.27 at L=20 to 150 (2609.36892)
verdict: survived: Memory has an optimum size: a small curated set beats none, but adding more stored statements stops helping and can hurt.
recommendation: build: survived, medium evidence; cap and gate every write.

what_and_how: Extraction proposes entries; a person confirms, rejects or retitles them before they persist, protected files take drafts that an operator promotes, and permanent sections accept only human edits.
problem: Model-written memory can be wrong or poisoned and then fires for many sessions.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: the gate itself is unmeasured, though 59 of 154 decisions survived triage; fits where humans already review changes.

what_and_how: Parent hands one subtask to a subagent with fresh context, a complete task brief and a limited tool set. The subagent returns a short structured report (outcome, reason, open issues), never its raw history. Parent resumes its own objective and appends the report.
problem: Long transcripts crowd the main context and mix unrelated work.
verdict: survived: Subagents with a specific task and their own tool access help; generic lifecycle subagents and advisory subagents that only recommend actions do not.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only for independent, task-specific subtasks with a full brief; handoffs lose information and cost 1.1 to 1.5 times.

what_and_how: A separate-context agent reads the scene or task and returns only advice, applicability notes or proposals; the main agent decides and acts. Variants include a privileged guide, a skill matcher, an imagination reviser and per-character roleplay calls.
problem: Give the main agent a second view without letting it act.
models: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Subagents with a specific task and their own tool access help; generic lifecycle subagents and advisory subagents that only recommend actions do not.
recommendation: do-not-build: the surviving idea says advisory-only subagents do not help; one character-roleplay paper shows tiny aggregate change.

what_and_how: Group tools by entity or pipeline stage into one specialist each, with a tool allowlist and input and output schema. A lead agent holding no tools delegates to specialists, sometimes seeing only their descriptions. Nested delegation is disabled; results return as structured reports.
problem: One agent with a huge tool catalog picks wrong tools and loses focus.
best_number: 2609.32459: ProgramBench: Qwen3.7-Max +5.91 percentage points
verdict: survived: Subagents with a specific task and their own tool access help; generic lifecycle subagents and advisory subagents that only recommend actions do not.
recommendation: build-in-regime: task-specific tool profiles gained, general subagents lost (2609.32459); added specialists can erase old abilities, so rerun old tasks.

what_and_how: Orchestrator plans several task briefs, launches workers in parallel in fresh narrow contexts or isolated trial directories, and unions their reports in code or by a reducer. Worker count is the main exploration dial; costs flatten past three to five.
problem: A single agent explores too little and runs steps serially.
best_number: ext-harness-engineering-small-language-models-explore: Gemma 4 31B: 33.2% at n = 1, 52.5% at n = 3, 64.7% at n = 15
verdict: survived: Parallel workers or explorers raise coverage quickly, then flatten near three to five workers, and duplicate moves grow with worker count.
recommendation: build-in-regime: wide search tasks and small local models, three to five workers; coverage flattens and duplicate work grows.

what_and_how: A model splits the question into sub-questions or typed record queries; workers or a small reader model answer each part alone; a reducer or plain code aggregates the answers. Variants differ in whether options are hidden from workers.
problem: A long or compound question overwhelms one call.
best_number: 2603.10044: pooled risk difference = −7.3 pp
verdict: survived: Split work along natural boundaries; arbitrary fixed chunks or blind splitting of one input among workers lose context and accuracy.
recommendation: test-first: blind question splitting harmed accuracy (2603.10044); typed manifest-based splitting for document records is one unbaselined run.

what_and_how: Several agents each work in their own worktree or workspace copy on the same problem and return a full diff or plan. Numeric checks or a combiner keep only candidates, or combinations, that beat the baseline; planners may read all candidates side by side.
problem: One attempt can miss; merging parallel edits loses the gain.
best_number: 2610.26770: 79.0% pass at $1.26 with planner, 73.0% at $1.42 without
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one measured gain with a planner (2610.26770); combining all proposals helped only 30% of cases.

what_and_how: Keep several independent search lines, each with its own history and elite archive. A coding-agent mutator or an orchestrator picks each line's parent branch and role (explorer, optimizer, adversarial); high scorers migrate between lines.
problem: One search line stalls in a local optimum.
best_number: 2607.02807: exceeds EvoX on 13/15 tasks
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: author-run searches, one single run (2607.08124); gains near the tuning set are doubtful. Only for harness search, not product work.

pattern: Route task to best harness variant
what_and_how: Keep several harness variants or branch-best heads; a router, using past success on task clusters or tuned instructions, picks one per task. An edit that helps some tasks and hurts others forks a new variant instead of replacing the old.
problem: A single edited harness helps some tasks and hurts others.
best_number: 2606.14249: GPT-5.4 GAIA: global final 49.5 vs ensemble final 87.4
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: only the authors' own runs; routing by task cluster needs held-out checking.

what_and_how: Run many calls of one model on the same prompt with no communication, then aggregate: geometric mean, a branching tree where each node synthesizes its children, or overlapping random-sample merge nodes. Replicated sessions expose run-to-run variance.
problem: One sample is noisy and a single run hides variance.
best_number: 2610.27157: teacher 43.6% with 85 model calls; single-pass student near 36%
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: median 1.7% gain at 30 samples on strong models (2611.16315); a tree helped a 1.7B model. For small local models only.

what_and_how: Run different models on the same task and combine: a router picks complementary proposers and an aggregator (vote, verifier, judge) fuses them; reports are mapped to canonical identities and counted once; file views seen by three or more models are flagged to the main agent.
problem: One model family has blind spots another covers.
verdict: survived: A routed set of cheaper proposer models with an aggregator can match the strongest single model at about one third the cost.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence on one benchmark with the authors' own routing.

what_and_how: A harness hook rewrites each subagent's launch arguments to choose a cheaper model tier per subagent. A subagent starts a fresh conversation, so the switch costs no prompt cache.
problem: Subagents inheriting the expensive parent model multiply cost.
best_number: 2609.28919: $5.09 on Fable 5.1 vs $1.32 on Sonnet 5
verdict: unmeasured: Subagents that inherit the parent's expensive model multiply cost; routing them to a cheaper tier saves money, but quality under routing was never measured.
recommendation: test-first: savings are simulated bills; quality under routing unmeasured.

what_and_how: Several agents each answer or propose an action, read each other's answers or arguments over two or three rounds, revise, then converge or vote. A fixed-pass analyst, critic and engineer variant feeds a moderator that writes a specification.
problem: One answer can be wrong; peers may catch each other.
best_number: 2606.14674: multi-agent debate with Base memory 22.26 versus ReAct with Base memory 8.54 (Figure 4)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: strong models gained 2.1% at fifteen times the cost (2611.16315); mini models gained more on authors' own tests.

pattern: Free peer messaging between parallel agents
what_and_how: Parallel agents on one codebase told a peer exists, or given a shared file, inbox or broadcast channel and synchronization steps. Measured as the failure case: awareness and free messaging do not stop collisions, and merges lose edits.
problem: Parallel agents on interacting work overwrite each other.
models: Claude Opus 4.8, GLM 5.2, Claude Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek V4-flash
best_number: 2611.00314: Claude Opus 4.8: 62% to 16% on contradictory instances
verdict: survived: Parallel agents that talk freely or only know a peer exists collide on interacting work: success collapses, awareness does not fix it.
recommendation: do-not-build: success collapsed from 62% to 16% and awareness did not help (2611.00314). Give parallel agents disjoint files.

what_and_how: Agent A edits the workspace first and agent B starts from A's resulting files; an ABAB variant repeats turns, with optional edit history. Interacting work is serialized rather than run in parallel.
problem: Parallel edits of one codebase conflict.
best_number: 2611.00314: 16% to 54% on contradictory instances
opposes: Free peer messaging between parallel agents
verdict: survived: A second agent that continues from the first agent's output recovers most of the gap against independent parallel runs.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, authors' own tasks, small sample; cheap to try before any parallel design.

what_and_how: Agents claim tasks from a queue showing open, claimed or done with owner, append short findings to one typed shared log, and read only new entries. No lead assigns work. A proxy can inject a cooperation directive on a schedule.
problem: Parallel agents duplicate work and cannot see each other's progress.
models: GPT-6-Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, alias2-mini
verdict: survived: On long decomposable tasks, many parallel agents sharing an append-only typed record, exclusive task claims and one workspace raise score and speed.
recommendation: test-first: weak, authors' own systems, one model in the large study.

what_and_how: Roles share no context; they exchange typed structured events (candidate patch, test result, accepted) over a bus or daemon queue. The patch editor sees only pass or fail and failure text, never validator reasoning. Messages arrive at fixed points in the loop.
problem: Handoffs leak reasoning or lose facts.
best_number: 2606.25514: GPT-5.4-xhigh 67.4% (icat-agent) vs 61.1% (Claude Code)
verdict: stale: Roles that keep isolated contexts and exchange only pass or fail messages beat an orchestrator that shares planning context.
recommendation: test-first: one author-built comparison from June, status stale.

what_and_how: Workers never talk directly. A gateway validates message schema, tags provenance, rate limits and logs; a reference monitor keeps a label per file path, joins writer and reader labels, and refuses calls that combine secret reads with outbound actions.
problem: Injected text and shared files move between agents unchecked.
best_number: 2611.13960: kill chains ABR=1.000 versus 0.667 for the oracle stateless policy
novelty: novel: label joins across agents' file reads and writes, checked by deterministic code, no model
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: 24 trajectories, deterministic checks, tiny model tested only as judge.

what_and_how: Compute one frozen permission ceiling from the trusted request before reading untrusted text; each subagent gets a narrower store checked on every call; policy deltas may only narrow. Attack papers show custom subagents and delegation escalate otherwise.
problem: A subagent runs injected commands with the parent's full authority.
best_number: 2609.08371: 3/75 attacks executed (CapScope) vs 33/75 (task-specific global policy)
verdict: survived: Delegation widens the safety and permission surface: per-agent capability scopes blocked injected effects that one shared policy let through.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, one small model, five tasks.

what_and_how: One agent builds an artifact; a separate evaluator (often with a runner or player role) tests or grades it and returns feedback; the loop repeats until acceptance criteria pass, keeping the better version each round. A plain script may do the running.
problem: A producer misses its own faults.
models: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8
best_number: 2610.33106: 53.45 vs 48.82 without auditor, player and reviewer (Table 2, page 9)
verdict: survived: A separate critic or auditor role that sees the task and the changes lifts coding and retrieval agents at modest cost; self-review adds nothing.
recommendation: build: separate evaluator with the task and changes gains at modest cost; self-review does not.

what_and_how: Split writing rights: planner edits the plan, builder edits code, the checker or reviewer in a fresh context is read-only and returns one verdict or admitted concerns. One owner writes each score; reviewer outputs are filtered before the writer sees them.
problem: Producers approve their own output and roles overstep.
best_number: 2610.05382: Recall 57.81 vs 27.07 for Harness-1 on BrowseComp-plus
verdict: survived: A separate critic or a different coding product, given the task and changes, raises accuracy at modest extra cost; self-review does not.
recommendation: build: separate read-only reviewers help; model reviewers are noisy (82 to 92 percent repeat), so log verdicts.

what_and_how: Models only propose statements, proofs or edits; persisted evidence and deterministic gates decide stage advance and completion. The test executor is a plain script, so feedback comes from program behavior, not a model verdict.
problem: Model judges are noisy and can be argued around.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: A task-specific checker, compile-and-run probe or verifier tool carries most of a harness lift; generic self-critique adds little.
recommendation: build: scripted checks carry most of the lift in measured papers; these two lines are argued only.

what_and_how: A fixed chain of role agents (planner, builder, validator, specialists) with narrow context each, passing short written reports or typed records; some stages are reviewed or gated by humans. Roles and order are set by the designer, not the model.
problem: One agent cannot hold a long multi-step procedure.
best_number: 2609.27424: total profit 31.17 vs 3.81 WBNB
verdict: survived: A small model in a fixed multi-role loop with scripted checks can match a much stronger bare model on narrow structured tasks.
recommendation: build-in-regime: narrow structured tasks with small or cheap models; strong models gain little at equal budget; first versions can fail.

what_and_how: The agent's native subagent ability runs with a prompt block saying when to delegate; the agent picks the decomposition. The harness only checks from the event log whether delegation happened.
problem: Fixed topologies may not suit the task.
best_number: 2609.04898: qwen3.6-flash 66% overall, 70.4% on the 81 tasks where delegation ran, vs 73% baseline and 86% retrieval
verdict: survived: Model-chosen delegation to subagents works only on the strongest models; small or cheap models often never delegate, or score below the bare assistant.
recommendation: do-not-build: delegation never started on 19 of 100 tasks and scored below the bare model on a small model.

what_and_how: Express the harness as a typed graph or program: agent nodes with role, model and tools, edges that pass outputs, fanout clones; a planner writes it, a fixed executor or scheduler runs independent nodes in parallel and waits on dependencies after a cycle check.
problem: Ad hoc agent calls are hard to inspect, test and reuse.
best_number: 2604.20801: Claude Opus 4.6: 84.3% on TerminalBench-2
verdict: survived: Organising skills or tasks by an explicit stage plan or dependency graph beats a flat set; running independent subtasks in parallel is argued, not measured.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, authors' benchmarks; fixed order versus model orchestration is unsettled.

what_and_how: A strong model writes the plan or workflow, with no tools or no workspace edit rights; every worker is the weaker execution model. The planner sees the transcript but not the pending edit and returns root cause and repair.
problem: A weak executor cannot plan its own recovery.
models: GPT-5.6 Sol, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 5.5
best_number: 2610.29870: 79/223 (35.4%) offline; Executor's own model as Planner 12/223 (5.4%)
verdict: survived: A strong model that writes the workflow for weaker executor models can lift them, but the sign depends on which model authors it.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, one run each.

what_and_how: Separate agents analyze failures, propose changes, build edits in an isolated workspace and verify against tests or held-out data; the verifier or orchestrator gates release. The optimizer may not read probe targets. A meta-agent can batch tasks and rewrite subagent prompts.
problem: A single self-editing agent drifts and grades itself.
best_number: 2606.01770: PolyBench all-task accuracy Full System 80.9 vs Static Sonnet 22.2
verdict: contested: Automatically evolved or refined multi-agent harnesses beat fixed hand-built protocols mostly on tasks close to their tuning set; gains often come from wording.
recommendation: test-first: authors' own loops and tuning sets; demand held-out tasks.

pattern: Evolve locally, merge with scoped mechanisms
what_and_how: Clients evolve a broadcast harness in parallel on local workloads and upload deltas or short reflections. The server merges them, tagging each mechanism global, scoped to one domain, or rejected, validates on held-out data, retries once and redistributes.
problem: Merging many local harness edits breaks cases.
best_number: 2610.24007: DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 94.47 existing tasks vs 83.98 isolated (Table 1)
novelty: novel: merger tags mechanisms global, domain-scoped or rejected before redistribution to clients
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: authors' own runs, repeats not stated.

what_and_how: Train the roles of a multi-agent harness with reinforcement learning: engineer and solver on one shared reward, a proposer and reflector sharing weights, mixed task-harness batches, or only the central agent with frozen subagents.
problem: Hand-written roles are not tuned to the model.
best_number: 2610.13025: Qwen3.8-27B: Polyglot 82.1% compared with 62.6%
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: authors' own benchmarks; requires training. Possible for small local models only if training is already in place.

what_and_how: Treat the harness as a network of nodes in layers. A frozen coding-agent optimizer per node reads traces and rewrites only its node; feedback goes backward from the last layer to adjacent upstream ones; same-layer nodes run in parallel.
problem: One global optimizer edits a harness too large to reason about.
novelty: novel: local feedback passed backward layer by layer through a network of harness nodes
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper, comparison to a global optimizer only in figures, run count not stated. Interesting for small local models.

what_and_how: Before building roles, run one agent with the same total inference and tool budget, split into roles only where permissions, models or owners truly differ, and report gained and lost cases per model against the bare call.
problem: Team gains can be an artifact of extra compute or hide losses.
best_number: ext-second-half-harness-design-agents-to-bots: 80.8% improvement to a 70.0% decline (cited study, six benchmarks, 260 configurations)
verdict: survived: Multi-agent effects differ in sign by model and task, so pooled averages hide losses; report gains and losses per model against the bare call.
recommendation: build: any multi-agent design must beat a one-agent baseline at equal budget; effects range from gains to declines.

what_and_how: Rank workers at spawn by predicted lifetime from the spawn record to place their cache, or watch latency, rate-limit replies and memory use and stop launching or pause some subagents under pressure.
problem: Many parallel subagents exhaust memory, rate limits or cache.
best_number: 2610.08378: 1.33–1.54× with reviewer present
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: the measured paper is a serving simulation only, not agent quality. Matters for small local models with limited memory.

what_and_how: A realtime agent sends tasks through one adapter to an external coding agent (Qwen Code, Codex or Claude Code), gets an immediate acknowledgment, and merges results into its context asynchronously.
problem: A conversational agent cannot do long coding work itself.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only, no measurement. Fits a cheap hosted model handing work to a coding runtime.

what_and_how: Each work node runs a complete coding-agent product as a black box; a second, different product reviews its patch, a repair step follows, and the loop repeats until approved.
problem: A same-family reviewer shares the producer's blind spots.
best_number: 2609.39551: 62.5% execution accuracy on HSTU vs 45.8% best single-product
verdict: survived: A separate critic or a different coding product, given the task and changes, raises accuracy at modest extra cost; self-review does not.
recommendation: build: cross-product review lifted accuracy in one paper; judge by cost per solved task.

what_and_how: Wrap each repository file with its own model call that reads and edits only that file. Activate only the files a task implicates, and let each send natural-language requirements to callers, callees, configuration and tests, delivered before the round ends.
problem: Whole-repository context overwhelms one agent on multi-file changes.
best_number: 2610.07832: GPT-5.6 Sol 23.5 without inter-primitive messages vs 31.0 on SWE Refactor Bench
novelty: novel: one model call per repository file with directed messages along dependency edges
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: 20 refactor tasks gained, but SWE-bench Verified moved only 97.00 vs 96.20.

what_and_how: An optimizer reads failure diagnoses and edits harness parts (prompts, memory, sub-agents, skills, tools, control logic) while model weights stay fixed and pinned. Each candidate builds on the previous one, and every change is a diff with a cause and a test.
problem: Improve an agent without retraining, with every change traceable.
best_number: harness-only evolution Abstain 76.7%, Pair 60.0% (2610.06563)
verdict: contested: An automatically evolved harness keeps a positive gain over its starting harness on held-out tasks.
recommendation: test-first: only the authors measured it and results of equal date disagree on held-out gain.

what_and_how: Keep every harness revision as a frozen snapshot, score each on development tasks, and deploy the one with the highest development score instead of the last. The initial harness can win. Cap the number of revisions.
problem: Late harness edits can lower held-out scores, so the final revision is not the best.
best_number: mean held-out gain of 4.53 points over the initial harness, compared with 2.80 for always deploying H2 (2610.30499)
verdict: survived: Evolution loops gain most in the first few iterations and later edits can lower held-out scores, so cap iterations and keep the best validated snapshot.
recommendation: build: verdict survived with medium evidence and costs one selection step.

what_and_how: Keep every scored harness variant as a node in an archive. Merge specialists from different lineages, and keep the merge only if it solves the union of the tasks both parents solved.
problem: A single lineage loses abilities that other lineages found, and merges can silently drop earlier wins.
best_number: Opus 4.8 TerminalWorld held-out: merged 28 of 41 vs specialists 24 to 27 (2608.07545)
verdict: contested: Mixing the work of structurally different harnesses (merged specialists, a shared blackboard) solves more than the best single harness; measured only before September.
recommendation: test-first: one authors run, a gap of one to four tasks of 41, idea contested; try only in a multi-role code pipeline with a held-out check.

what_and_how: Expose the harness as named, separately editable parts (instruction, tools, verification guidance, files under version control). The improver may change only those. History, credentials, gate verdicts and the gate itself sit below a boundary it cannot write, and each edit is one revertible commit.
problem: A self-editing agent can break or game the harness that checks it.
best_number: GLM-5 AppWorld overall 44.4 to 85.0 (2606.09498)
verdict: contested: Restricting evolution to one module per edit beats whole-harness rewriting offline, but letting the agent edit everything during a run beat a predefined scope.
recommendation: test-first: the scope question is contested and most lines here argue the design; build the protected gate regardless.

what_and_how: Split the harness into a fixed list of named parts (for example context, tools, memory, orchestration, verification, execution runtime; four to ten parts). Give each its own specification or editable file, so a failure names one part to edit and a system can be checked part by part.
problem: Harness work needs a shared vocabulary so failures and edits map to one part.
best_number: GPT-5.3-Codex: 0.722 to 0.806 on Terminal-Bench (2607.14159)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: ten papers use it, three measured, one gain had p of 0.617; use as a design checklist, not a proven gain.

what_and_how: Code strips task identifiers, split names, URLs and benchmark names from traces before the improving agent reads them. Failure cases stay in the report, but only task labels, quotas and abstract category notes reach task construction.
problem: An optimizer or task builder that sees benchmark details memorizes them and inflates scores.
best_number: none
novelty: novel: code redaction between failure evidence and the optimizer or task builder.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only, no measurement; cheap to build.

what_and_how: Take a harness evolved on one model and apply it unchanged to another model at the same task, with no target search, fine-tuning or adaptation. Then check the result on the target model.
problem: Evolving a harness for every model is expensive.
verdict: survived: A harness evolved with one model transfers to other models on the same tasks, usually with a smaller gain; check on the target model.
recommendation: build: verdict survived with medium evidence and it costs nothing to try; always measure on the target model.

what_and_how: Collect teacher episodes, keep only those that pass the outcome check and protocol checks, then fine-tune the student on the whole episode (reasoning plus next tool call), with environment output masked from the loss. A small base model learns the harness's tool-use pattern.
problem: Small models fail at multi-step tool use that a stronger model completes.
verdict: contested: Copying a stronger model's full trajectories can hurt or install nothing in a small model; on-policy correction or reinforcement is safer.
recommendation: test-first: gains are authors' own while other papers report harm; test on your small model, keep only verified episodes.

what_and_how: In supervised fine-tuning of agent traces, compute loss only on assistant turns, including tool calls. Tool outputs such as file dumps and test logs stay in context but are not training targets.
problem: Training on environment text teaches the model to imitate logs instead of acting.
best_number: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning-8K, SWE-bench Verified pass@1: unmasked 27.5, masked 37.8 (2610.22019)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one authors' ablation with a ten-point gap; trivial to add whenever you train, so verify on your own model.

what_and_how: Let the student act on its own states, then query the teacher on those states for token-level targets: next-token distributions, or a preference between teacher actions with and without the harness. Score only action tokens, and weight by student-teacher divergence.
problem: Students trained on teacher traces drift into states the teacher never showed.
best_number: 57.4 with the term, 43.5 without (2610.02858)
novelty: novel: teacher queried with and without the harness; student learns to prefer the harness-informed action.
verdict: contested: Copying a stronger model's full trajectories can hurt or install nothing in a small model; on-policy correction or reinforcement is safer.
recommendation: test-first: authors' runs on about 140 tasks without repeats and two teacher calls per state; try only for small local models.

what_and_how: From a checkpoint of a successful run, inject a stage-matched failure (missed grasp, dropped object, slip), let the teacher recover, and keep only branches that still succeed or are verified. Train on them with the clean runs.
problem: Models trained only on clean successes cannot recover once something goes wrong.
best_number: Guava-4B 87.1 with perturbations vs 79.3 without; unseen tasks 90.8 vs 77.1 (2606.18363)
verdict: not judged
