verdict: survived: Skills distilled from trajectories of the same task family give frontier models modest held-out gains of a few points, and weaker models more.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only task-matched skills help, mostly weaker models; general libraries add little and wrong skills cost more than none.

what_and_how: After each episode or batch, a model writes lessons or rules from the outcome, stores them as notes or a memory file, and injects them into later runs. Some versions add an experience library, a dead list of failed ideas, or a knowledge base.
problem: Agents repeat the same mistake across runs.
best_number: affinity accuracy from 62.2% to 81.1% (2610.23791)
verdict: survived: Keeping complete unmodified interaction history is at least as good as reflection or rule extraction; reflection harnesses are sometimes below the stateless model.
recommendation: test-first: widely built but the verdict favours raw full history; beat that baseline with an admission gate before adding notes.

what_and_how: A diagnosis step names the first wrong decision, the failing component or the failure category, then routes the fix to the owner: harness code, prompt, middleware, policy training or memory. Output is a structured record, not free text.
problem: Free-text reflection finds the region but rarely the cause, so fixes go to the wrong place.
verdict: survived: Diagnosis that names the failing component and routes the failure back raises repair success; free-text self-reflection finds the region but rarely the cause.
recommendation: build: medium support from four papers; cheap structured step.

what_and_how: Each recurring failure must change harness code: a gate, prompt overlay, telemetry requirement or completion check, written to a versioned artifact. Compare the agent's success claim with verified results and add a check where they differ.
problem: Lessons in notes get forgotten; code checks persist and repeat exactly.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Targeted runtime rules fired at a logged risky state, or verified tool-health state, raise repeated success and cut waste, while generic self-checks add nothing.
recommendation: test-first: support is weak, from authors who sell the runtime; one paper shows 99 of 100 runs claiming success while 48 pass.

what_and_how: Evolve the checking criteria with the harness: turn failures into new rubric items, keep the top few, retire weak ones, replace a verifier only if it improves the weakest family. The judge is revised by the same loop.
problem: A fixed evaluator is exploited by search and stops detecting new failures.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: all seven papers are self-scored and a changing judge is exactly what search can exploit; hold a frozen outside check.

what_and_how: Run each training task alone, with the current evolver, and with a verifier-informed evolver. Pair outcomes into act, avoid and compare lessons, distill them into a fixed written guide offline, and let an evolver edit the harness during each test run, discarding edits at the end.
problem: Online evolution starts from nothing; self-distilled lessons are weaker than contrasts with real outcomes.
best_number: Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.00 contrastive vs 77.00 self-distilled (2611.05139)
novelty: novel: offline contrastive guide drives online edits that reset each run
verdict: survived: Skills and lessons built from grounded feedback (verifier output, test failures, a teacher's contrast with its own run) beat self-judged or human-written ones.
recommendation: build: medium support for grounded contrast; measured by two papers with small test sets.

what_and_how: Run the harness, keep only trajectories a verifier accepts, optionally with reviewer reasoning masked, and fine-tune a small model or low-rank adapter on them. The model then runs with or without the harness.
problem: Small models fail the harness even when the harness is right.
verdict: survived: Training a 4B to 9B model on traces produced inside the harness it will run in beats prompting it.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, authors' own benchmarks and mostly no repeats.

what_and_how: Run the student, let a teacher write or correct the reply at states the student actually reached, and train on those pairs. The teacher share falls to zero over rounds, or the teacher sees extra state the student does not.
problem: Copying full teacher trajectories installs nothing in small models.
best_number: 61.21 with updated state, 56.29 without state (2609.08919)
verdict: contested: Copying a stronger model's full trajectories can hurt or install nothing in small models; on-policy correction is safer, but results are disputed.
recommendation: test-first: contested and small gains within noise in one paper.

what_and_how: Roll out the model in the sandbox, reward only checked outcomes such as task success, passed goal checks or a matched hidden result, and update with group-normalized policy gradients. Sometimes shaped with partial credit.
problem: Supervised copying does not teach the model to recover from its own mistakes.
best_number: MineStudio All 65.1 before vs 80.7 after reinforcement learning (2610.31162)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: twelve papers, every one self-scored and none judged here; the cost is a training pipeline, so test against supervised training first.

what_and_how: Add partial-credit terms, dense milestone rewards, structure gates or composite scores, and normalize rewards within the same task or across harnesses so harness mean differences do not dominate. Several variants appear.
problem: Binary rewards are sparse and mix harness effects with policy effects.
best_number: Any Medal 27.3 dense vs 13.6 sparse (2604.04872)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper found normalization variants within 1 point of each other and not significant; detail choice may not matter.

what_and_how: Alternate rounds: evolve the harness, collect rollouts under it, fine-tune the policy on them, then re-evolve the harness against the updated policy. Some versions reset the skill library after each weight update.
problem: Harness and policy improve different failures; one alone plateaus.
verdict: survived: Alternating harness evolution with weight training on the same small base model beats either alone.
recommendation: test-first: weak evidence, authors' own methods, one base model per paper.

what_and_how: The system builds the next training tasks itself: tasks never solved become the next search set, a questioner is revised from solver traces, capability patterns drive task synthesis, or the failing environment is redesigned into a certified new task.
problem: A fixed task set runs out of signal and overfits.
models: Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-5.6-Luna, Qwen3.7 Plus, Codex GPT-4o
best_number: Abstain 61.7% to 83.3% on HERA-BENCH (2610.06563)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: self-built tasks add a second thing to check; all papers score their own generator.

what_and_how: The loop that edits the harness is itself edited: an optimizer edits its own prompts and hooks between rounds, a meta-evolver rewrites the evolver strategy, an orchestrator intervenes when an island stalls, or the accepted version becomes the next improver.
problem: A fixed improver stops finding gains after a few rounds.
best_number: +39.3 on BabyAI, +33.0 on Crafter (2608.08466)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: three papers measured, no matched control; extra levels multiply drift risk; keep outside checks fixed.

what_and_how: Before patching, the analysis step writes the suspected mechanism, supporting evidence, expected effect and how it will be checked; each edit declares a predicted impact that the next run compares with the outcome. Source diffs attribute changes.
problem: Edits made without a stated cause cannot be judged afterwards.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: no paper measures it alone; argued designs only; cheap to add and log.

what_and_how: Run each candidate program or trigger over stored episodes or simulated scenes without a model call, record how often its target failure occurs, and install it only if the replay and a held-out score agree.
problem: Testing every candidate with live model runs is slow and costly.
best_number: Make Popcorn success 0.33 initial to 0.94 learned (2607.05369)
verdict: survived: Fixes for one failure often break working behaviour, and models predict their own regressions near chance, so replay earlier cases before accepting a change.
recommendation: build: free and deterministic; survived at medium strength.

what_and_how: Inside one run, watch for repeated failure or user complaint, then revise rules, write a new planner class or recompile a skill, with syntax checks and rollback. Revisions affect the same task.
problem: Waiting for an offline loop misses failures that happen now.
best_number: without in-task evolution 38.9%, full 42.7% (2604.19572)
verdict: survived: Edits made for the current task, instance or batch (in-run review, per-instance patch, per-batch update) beat one global harness evolved offline.
recommendation: test-first: one paper shows planner code evolution scoring Sharpe 0.41 against 2.13 for a reflection variant; harm risk is real.

what_and_how: Keep the trajectory up to the earliest repairable decision and regenerate only the suffix, or let a diagnostic agent and code agent repair a trajectory program after a failed unit test. Repaired runs become training data or the final answer.
problem: Whole-run retries waste tokens and discard good early steps.
best_number: Fable 5.1 73% to 95% unit-test pass (2609.24145)
verdict: survived: More repair rounds with concrete checker feedback lift success sharply until the loop saturates; most gain is within the first rounds.
recommendation: test-first: verdict support is weak and from one benchmark; cap rounds near three.

what_and_how: Each iteration a judge compares the new output with the previous one, appends the verdict to a history, and the next refinement reads that history. A related loop feeds judge feedback back to the generator.
problem: Absolute scores are noisy; relative comparison is easier for a judge.
models: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.8
best_number: reducing inference cost by up to 60% (2607.15524)
verdict: survived: A same-strength or weaker model grading holistically or by pairwise preference is unreliable: position bias, self-preference, inflated scores.
recommendation: test-first: the verdict warns that pairwise judging by a similar model is unreliable; validate the judge against outside checks first.

what_and_how: Remove each harness item in turn, run several repeats per task where it could load, and delete it unless removal costs runs or the item fired. Always-on skills are checked for being read at all.
problem: Harnesses only grow; unused or harmful items stay forever.
best_number: 2 of the harness's 4 items are removable (2610.14216)
novelty: novel: deletion pass measured by paired removal, opposite of add-only evolution
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper on one synthetic repository; cheap to try; measure on your own harness.

what_and_how: Tell the agent to re-read its case files and solver script and critique them before it finishes, with no new outside evidence.
problem: Agents submit without checking their own work.
best_number: Direct Baseline 96.4% (106/110) with and without the reflection prompt (2609.03718)
verdict: survived: A model told to re-check or reflect on its own work, with no new outside information, does not raise success.
recommendation: do-not-build: seven papers and this paper's own measurement show no gain without new evidence; use an outside check instead.

what_and_how: Give the proposer human demonstration trajectories next to its own rollouts, fresh papers on the topic screened against the champion, or a strong solver's trajectory chosen by task type.
problem: The proposer only sees its own narrow experience.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: three papers on different tasks, all self-scored; real human demonstrations are cheap to supply.

what_and_how: Train a small model to write harness patches: sample several patches per failure packet, rerun the same tasks with each, and reward by the change in task score, normalized within the group. Invalid patches score zero.
problem: Untrained small models write poor patches and lose most of the gain.
best_number: supervised-only engineer 46.4%, outcome-trained 53.6% average success (2608.02276)
novelty: novel: the proposer itself is trained with rerun-score rewards
verdict: contested: A small model can write or evolve a harness only if trained for it; untrained weak writers lose most of the gain.
recommendation: test-first: contested and measured by three papers from their own authors.

what_and_how: Revise the harness for the current instance, batch or single task instead of one global offline version: sample a trajectory, let a meta agent edit from the failure, rerun once. Edits may be discarded afterwards.
problem: One global harness cannot fit each task's specific failures.
best_number: BIRD 12.7% to 48.7% mean over three runs (2607.08124)
verdict: survived: Edits made for the current task, instance or batch (in-run review, per-instance patch, per-batch update) beat one global harness evolved offline.
recommendation: build: survived at medium strength; one batch variant scored 67.4 against 68.2 for direct sampling, so compare with equal-budget sampling.

what_and_how: Keep only skill names and one-line descriptions in the prompt. When a task matches, the agent calls a load tool or opens the skill file to get the full procedure and bundled scripts. Variants load per code region or per state, and some add a second tier of reference files.
problem: Standing context bloats if every procedure is always loaded, and costs tokens on tasks that do not need it.
models: Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra, Qwen3.7-Max, DeepSeek-V4-Pro
best_number: 2610.12126: GPT-5.6 Terra (high), 0.25 m: 35.00% success without skills vs 68.33% full (Table 3)
verdict: survived: Whether offered skills get loaded depends mainly on the model and how they are offered; weak models and always-on listings rarely load them.
recommendation: build-in-regime: real on strong models; Claude Code invoked only 15% of offered skills, so preload or route for small local models.

what_and_how: Write one markdown file per task or code module: judging rules, flow, verified parameters, common failures, commands. An expert or analysis agent drafts it, a person reviews it, and it is injected or read when the task starts.
problem: The model lacks niche method or format knowledge that no amount of reasoning supplies.
best_number: 2610.23479: GPT-6-Astra: 85.00 with skills, against 69.92 without
verdict: survived: Task-matched expert knowledge in context lifts success sharply when the model lacks that knowledge, such as a new method or niche format.
recommendation: build-in-regime: large gain where the model lacks the knowledge, near zero on the strongest models.

what_and_how: Put mandatory rules or the matching reference in one file the agent must read before acting, or in the prompt itself, instead of an on-demand skill. Promote recurring patterns to always-loaded rules; make humans the only writers of the rules file.
problem: Skills triggered at the model's discretion are skipped, so rules that must hold every time do not hold.
models: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.6 Luna, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, Gemma 4 12B
best_number: 2609.03718: Claude Opus 4.6 80.9% (89) no tutorial; 92.7% (102) optional; 96.4% (106) must-read on FoamBench
verdict: survived: Rules the agent must obey every time belong in the prompt text; splitting a policy into skills loaded on demand costs accuracy for small models.
recommendation: test-first: verdict weak, one small model and one domain. Worth trying for small local models and where an organisation's rules are mandatory.

what_and_how: Give the agent task meaning and broad criteria only. Withhold molecule-specific recipes, fixed call sequences and heavy domain documentation, and keep added instruction to a short list of task types and permitted tools.
problem: Prescribed procedures and domain priors can narrow the agent or mislead it where the model already knows the domain.
best_number: 2610.12183: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (default); mean 0.465 to 0.595 on six real-world tasks
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged; two papers measured, one found heavy domain context lowered the mean from 14.6% to 10.6%. Try on strong hosted models.

what_and_how: Append security guidance to the coding agent's system prompt, either a detailed task prompt or a whole-system prompt, on top of the stock prompt.
problem: Generated code skips security practices unless the prompt says otherwise.
best_number: 2607.13085: GPT-5 P@2: detailed task prompt 68, whole-system prompt 75, native default 81
verdict: survived: Added instructions over a vendor's tuned default prompt give no gain and can hurt, for example security prompts over the shipped Codex prompt.
recommendation: do-not-build: both measurements show no gain over the default prompt; use a deterministic check in code instead.

what_and_how: Add one short, positive, factual sentence or a rule plus a worked example that targets a measured behaviour: completeness of the rule set, do not repeat a failed call, build correct code before tuning, fixed principles list. Keep prose short and examples multi-line.
problem: Agents repeat failed calls, abstain wrongly or over-engineer; a bare prompt misses these behaviours.
best_number: 2607.13083: five proposers pooled: 15/60 without the sentence, 0/60 with it
verdict: survived: One short, positive, factual sentence reliably changes a measurable behaviour, though prompt lines that forbid a behaviour change nothing.
recommendation: build: cheap, narrow and measured; favour positive sentences over prohibitions.

what_and_how: After rollouts, a separate agent reads raw logs or trajectories, separates success and failure patterns, writes a skill or playbook, and the harness injects it at inference. Variants add a reviewer, regenerate from no-skill runs, or retrieve one strategy per task.
problem: Agents repeat the same mistakes across runs and nothing carries over.
models: GPT-5.4 high, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash, QWEN3-32B-AWQ
best_number: 2609.29964: GPT-5.5 for the roles; Gemini 3.7 Flash: zero-shot 28.9%, seed skills 43.3%, evolved 75.6% average
verdict: survived: Skills distilled from trajectories of the same task family give frontier models modest held-out gains of a few points, weaker models more.
recommendation: build-in-regime: modest gain on frontier models, larger on weaker ones; keep a held-out split.

what_and_how: Match a failed trajectory or tool report to a failure signature, such as a sanitizer error class or a pattern recurring across repositories, and inject or write a trigger plus corrective procedure. Promote fixes to shared knowledge only after holdout success.
problem: Generic advice misses specific recurring failures; fixes found once are lost.
best_number: 2610.35616: GLM-5.2, DeepSWE Pi: 48.7 full vs 43.4 without recovery skills (Table 3)
verdict: survived: Skills and lessons built from grounded feedback (verifier output, test failures, a teacher's contrast with its own run) beat self-judged or human-written ones.
recommendation: build: grounded feedback survives with medium evidence.

pattern: Retrieve skills or examples per task
what_and_how: Index skills or similar worked examples by embedding, keyword score or operation-level support. Pick the top one to five for the task, or inject all of them, and put them in the first prompt. Rerank candidates by how well each covers the task's operations.
problem: Too many skills dilute the prompt; the right skill must reach the model without its choosing.
best_number: 2611.13144: DeepSeek-V4-Flash flat injection, mean of L1 to L3: +11.1; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct flat injection: −14.2
verdict: contested: Giving one agent the whole tool or skill catalog does not reliably help: it raised errors in one paper but pass rate in another.
recommendation: test-first: contested; flat injection helped one model and hurt another. Pick the delivery method per model, bare against with-skill.

what_and_how: Model skills as nodes of a dependency graph, a scenario graph, tiers (interface, subagent, base) or typed ports. The agent follows only the predecessors and successors relevant to the task; tools are clustered into skills by shared parameters.
problem: A flat pile of skills gives the agent no order and floods it with unrelated ones.
verdict: survived: Organising skills or tasks by an explicit stage plan or dependency graph beats a flat set of the same skills.
recommendation: test-first: weak verdict from one measuring paper; gains of 1.3 to 4 points. Try in a code-change pipeline.

what_and_how: Give each agent only the notes for its current stage and role, such as planner strategy notes, executor operational notes, or the procedure of the current state in a state machine. Keep the system prompt to role, overview and index.
problem: Loading all guidance at once costs tokens and distracts agents in later phases.
best_number: 2611.04196: GLM-5.3: 30 of 40 solved complete, 24 without expert knowledge (Table 6)
verdict: survived: Load instructions and skills for the current phase, chosen by the harness, rather than all at once or at the model's discretion.
recommendation: test-first: weak verdict, one measured paper; plausible for role-based factories. Compare against full injection before adopting.

what_and_how: A capable rewriter gets the task, the skill and the executor's tool list. It finds the earliest break, edits only the implicated passages, drops domain nouns the executor cannot use, or compiles around capability gaps found by microbenchmarks.
problem: Generic skills written for strong models fail on weak executors that skip or misread them.
best_number: 2610.33024: Kimi-K3 rewriter: mean 0.294 to 0.387; Gemma-4-E4B 0.029 to 0.170
verdict: survived: A stronger model rewriting or adapting skills to fit a weak executor beats giving the weak model the generic skill or bank directly.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only when the executor is weaker than the rewriter, as in small local models. Gains small to moderate; authors' own methods.

what_and_how: A separate optimizer reads scored rollouts and makes bounded edits to a frozen agent's skill file, rewriting it on a schedule from recent records. Control flow stays fixed, so no extra calls at run time.
problem: Hand-written skill text is stale and nobody knows which line helped.
best_number: 2610.22466: Qwen3.5-4B on ALFWorld: +46.2% search-set gain
verdict: survived: Automated search that edits only prompts or skills gains a few points over a good seed; searching the whole harness gains more.
recommendation: test-first: gains are search-set numbers by the authors; one paper showed no gain from guidance updates alone. Hold out a split.

what_and_how: Give each skill or guidance entry typed fields: trigger or when-to-use, what it provides, use rules, inputs and outputs, preconditions, and examples. Entries may need support from two tasks; proof methods carry required conditions and residual obligations.
problem: Free-form skill text has no trigger, so the agent cannot judge when to apply it.
best_number: 2609.38143: GPT-5.6-Sol builder; full bank macro average 65.31 vs no-skill 56.36
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: mostly argued designs; two measured by authors. Cheap to adopt as a format; measure against free-form text.

what_and_how: Draft a skill, run the agent on test prompts with and without it, grade both, and keep the skill only if a held-out run improved and a replay shows no regression. Search the library first and update a similar skill instead of adding a duplicate.
problem: Unchecked skills accumulate and lower earlier behaviour.
best_number: 2607.22520: sonnet-4.6: +8 on OfficeQA-Pro, p = .039, not significant after correction
verdict: survived: Every self-edit to a harness needs a held-out regression check and rollback; unchecked accumulation of edits and rules lowers earlier behavior.
recommendation: build: medium evidence for admission checks, though the measured gain here was not significant.

what_and_how: Merge duplicate or overlapping skills into a fixed-size bank in one compression pass at temperature zero, drop generic advice, then pick a budgeted subset maximising coverage after a safety scan. Let a model choose which functions to activate from their descriptions.
problem: Skill banks grow with duplicates and dilute the prompt.
models: DeepSeek V4 Pro, GPT-5.5 Medium, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview, Qwen3.5-4B
best_number: 2609.39284: DeepSeek V4 Pro (compression); GPT-5.5 Medium; S-Full-20 51.25%, No Skills 46.63%
verdict: survived: Memory has an optimum size: a small curated set beats none, adding more stops helping and can hurt, and distilled banks matched full history.
recommendation: build: small curated set backed by three independent papers; gains are a few points.

what_and_how: Ask the model for a program per task, check it against every demonstration, store it only if it passes, and run it first when the task returns. Call the model only if the program fails; a refiner rewrites programs that raised exceptions.
problem: Recomputing a solved task costs tokens and time every run.
best_number: 2611.14505: Qwen3.5-9B: share saved on seen test 0.65 [0.46, 0.86], on held-out test 0.03 [-0.02, 0.09]
verdict: contested: Carrying learned knowledge or harness edits to different tasks or domains: some papers show transfer, others show worse scores than resetting.
recommendation: test-first: saves 0.65 on repeated tasks but 0.03 on new ones; only worth it where tasks recur exactly.

what_and_how: When the agent drafts a state-changing tool call, the harness does not run it. It returns a not-executed result, retrieves the skill keyed by the named tool, and the model redrafts with that skill in context.
problem: Skills loaded at the start are forgotten or ignored by the time a risky action is taken.
best_number: 2608.24876: doubao-seed-2-0-pro, tau2-Retail: 65.6 model-controlled to 83.6 Recuris
novelty: novel: skill chosen by the harness at action time, blocking the first call
verdict: survived: Load instructions and skills for the current phase, chosen by the harness, rather than all at once or at the model's discretion.
recommendation: test-first: one paper by its authors, +18 points on one benchmark; plausible for an organisation's rules at write actions. Replicate before relying.

what_and_how: A model studies training demonstrations once and writes task guidance, motion references, helpers and checks, or a card of action order and waypoints. It is frozen read-only; each test episode starts fresh and nothing is written back.
problem: Each episode re-derives task knowledge, and writing back risks drift.
best_number: 2610.35832: GPT-6-Astra on Frame placement: from 1/20 to 13/20 successful episodes with the demonstration
verdict: survived: On tasks the bare model almost never solves, a harness that supplies what the model lacks multiplies scores, even for the strongest models.
recommendation: test-first: verdict weak, unequal budgets, authors' own tasks. Strong on never-solved tasks; check a bare run first.

what_and_how: Freeze a harness state, runbook or policy library evolved on one model and apply it unchanged to a newer or different model, mapped to the host's retrieval format. Compress all languages' rules into ten generic guidelines for a new language.
problem: Re-evolving a harness for each new model is expensive.
models: GPT-5.6 Luna, Gemini 3 Pro, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash
best_number: 2607.26598: Gemini 3 Pro Restaurant 47.83 to 66.13; GLM-5 Taxi 0.00 to 43.08
verdict: contested: A harness tuned on one model often fails to carry over unchanged to another model, but harnesses carrying task knowledge often do carry over.
recommendation: test-first: contested; transfer works for knowledge-heavy tasks but one paper's retention fell below 0.7 on three languages. Test on each target model.

what_and_how: Fine-tune a small model on rollouts from a strong model that pass the verifier, converted to the student's chat and tool-call format, often mixed with the student's own passing runs. Some add a planning-then-execution split.
problem: Small models cannot follow harness procedures from prompts alone.
best_number: 2610.26071: Qwen3.5-4B desktop 22.6 to 44.8, browser 4.4 to 60.0, mobile 14.6 to 26.8 (GPT-5.5 rollouts)
verdict: contested: Copying a stronger model's full trajectories can hurt or install nothing in a small model, though other papers gain a lot from plain trace training.
recommendation: test-first: large gains reported, but one evolved harness fell 78.0% to 63.1%.

what_and_how: Cut each teacher trajectory at its first best submission, or have a teacher estimate each step's success chance and train only on rising segments; mask loss on tokens the model did not generate.
problem: Raw traces contain wasted or harmful steps that training copies.
best_number: 2605.15040: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking: 59.3 resolved-only vs 61.2 with credit-assignment supervised fine-tuning
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: gain is 1.9 points on one paper, authors' own; add only after plain trace training works for small local models.

what_and_how: Train the student to produce the behaviour of a harness it no longer sees: regress on a teacher that sees the prompt, train adapters per group then distill back, or condition each training dialogue on its retrieved strategy card.
problem: Prompt-time harness text costs tokens on every call and small models follow it poorly.
best_number: 2610.34724: Qwen3-8B: ScienceWorld final 52.43 for HaMo against 24.57 for Model only (no memory, no replay)
verdict: contested: Distilling a harness into the weights lets the harness be dropped at run time and can beat the harness attached, but not on every task.
recommendation: test-first: contested and weak; one paper's student reached 30% against 11% empty. Small local models only, after prompt-time version works.

what_and_how: Compile an instruction or harness bundle into a rank-8 shift added after every decoder block of a frozen model, trained on filtered teacher traces; combine two bundles by mixing shifts in shift space, no prompt text.
problem: Stacking two skill texts in a prompt cancels or dilutes both.
best_number: 2611.01415: Qwen3-4B, MBPP: combined +0.624 versus text stacked +0.088
novelty: novel: skills combined as weights rather than stacked text, no inference tokens
verdict: contested: Distilling a harness into the weights lets the harness be dropped at run time and can beat the harness attached, but not on every task.
recommendation: test-first: one paper by its authors on small models and code tasks; needs weight access, so small local models only.

what_and_how: Parse vendor or lab documents offline into text, tables and equations, store as a knowledge graph, and at query time retrieve entry points and expand their neighbourhoods to insert ranked strategies with rationale into the prompt or judge.
problem: Flat retrieval misses linked facts across long technical documents.
best_number: 2611.02784: GPT-5.5 (base model); 21.5× geometric-mean latency speedup versus 10.4× flat retrieval and 3.8× no retrieval
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper by its authors on one domain; a flat-retrieval baseline exists in that paper, so check against it.

what_and_how: Before proposing a harness change, search other agent frameworks' source and documentation for how they solve the grouped failure, adapt the design to this harness's flow, and keep the search record when nothing fits.
problem: Local-only proposals repeat known weaknesses already solved elsewhere.
best_number: 2610.27435: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Terminal-Bench Hard Pass@1 and Pass4 improved by 5.50% and 6% over local-only proposals
novelty: novel: harness changes sourced from other frameworks' code, not papers
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper, gain of 5.5 and 6 points on one benchmark; cheap to try in a pipeline's improvement loop.

what_and_how: A research agent reads each selected paper with its appendix and official code and writes a blueprint of mechanism, target module, state and stop conditions; a coding agent builds it. Group papers by mechanism topic and pick round robin; or query an open scholarly index live.
problem: Models draft ideas from memory and miss recent work.
best_number: 2609.40169: task goal completion 76.8±1.19 without research guidance vs 81.4±1.19 full (Qwen3.5-27B, cumulative row)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper by its authors; gains 4.6 points with interval 1.19. Costly to run; try only in a harness-improvement loop.

what_and_how: Split policy or theory documents into one rule per decision, keeping the verbatim sentence, source and a must or should label. Compile rules into typed forms with a fixed gate and fixtures, or a filesystem tree the agent instantiates only when matching.
problem: Policy prose is too long and ambiguous for a model to apply reliably.
best_number: 2611.13336: GLM-5.2: kappa-star 0.472 without it vs 0.787 full on τ 2-bench (Table 4)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged; extraction measured only by its authors.

what_and_how: Hold about 1,800 hand-written rules, each with a weight. A verdict multiplies the weight by 0.95 if the rule predicted right and by 0.05 if wrong, then normalises; each job mixes 0.2 percent prior back in. No model is used.
problem: Infer which written rule explains repeated yes or no verdicts under label noise.
best_number: 2611.19952: none (Rule+Open 0.551 against kNN-mem 0.492 on pattern A new contexts, Table 2)
novelty: novel: learning is rule-weight updating in code, no model call at all
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: simulated robot placement only, authors' own benchmark; relevant only if verdicts are binary.

what_and_how: Keep knowledge, standards and rules as version-controlled markdown or typed data files with tags and source metadata, in topic folders; humans and the agent edit the same files; the rules document is human-written only. No database.
problem: Knowledge locked in a database or a model prompt is hard to review and edit.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued designs, nothing measured. Cheap; measure whether agents read it.

what_and_how: Treat skills, tool descriptions and policies as code: a named owner, recorded provenance, pinned name and version, frontmatter check, and approval for frozen rule changes. A rule change needs a new version.
problem: Unversioned skills drift and no one can say which version produced a result.
best_number: 2610.37923: ten open-weight verifiers; paired gains -0.2 to +4.6 points
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one measured paper with gains between -0.2 and +4.6 points; the rest argued. Cheap.

what_and_how: Before installing a skill, send its address to a scanning service, reuse recent scans and refuse malicious ones; or reject any skill proposal naming a repository, path, issue or gold patch and freeze the skill.
problem: Unvetted skills carry attacks and leak answers into prompts.
best_number: 2607.25890: Claude Code with Sonnet 4.6: skill scanning 58.3% to 100%; Codex with GPT-5.5: 16.7% to 75.0% (Table II, page 5)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: measured by one paper on scan compliance, not on catching attacks. Still cheap; scan any imported skill.

what_and_how: Keep safety skills in tiers (general, task or tool, recurring mistakes) with success patterns, failure lessons and risk guards from violations; retrieve a few per episode, or bundle a task prompt with shared tools as a skill.
problem: Agents violate domain safety rules without domain-specific guidance.
best_number: 2609.02786: Qwen3.5-4B: harmful score 56.45 without retrieval, 16.80 with default retrieval (Table 3)
verdict: survived: Skill text is an attack surface and a safety lever: unvetted skills raise violation rates, while a safety skill for the domain lowers them.
recommendation: test-first: weak verdict; authors built tasks to elicit failures. Large drops reported.

what_and_how: Activate a learned skill only when its recorded guards hold or a domain record's match confidence passes a threshold; screen transferred rubrics by relevance and generality scores of at least 4 before the target bank takes them.
problem: Skills applied in the wrong situation do more harm than none.
best_number: ext-behavioral-rubrics-agent-harness-evolution: MiniMax-M2.5 overall: 61.79±0.57 all rubrics; 64.44±0.56 human-selected; 64.07±0.49 judge-selected
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: neighbouring idea says wrong guidance costs more than none, but this gate itself is only measured by its authors.

what_and_how: Keep earlier code, templates and scripts as a library: component fragments, behaviour scripts with self-checks, data pipelines reused across chains, default-off parameters on shared functions. The agent copies what it adopts; nothing is imported at run time.
problem: Each task rebuilds common modules and wastes tokens.
best_number: 2611.06254: GPT-5.4-mini: 65.03 with library vs 63.39 without, three benchmarks
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: gains of 1.6 and 2.9 points by authors; a neighbouring idea says fixed libraries add little once the harness works.

what_and_how: Write the skill as a ladder: a standard method first, a test, then an alternative only when the test flags it; each step has a quantitative acceptance criterion and the agent repeats, proceeds or stops with a low-quality verdict.
problem: Agents jump to complex methods without checking if the simple one fits.
models: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Sonnet 5.5, gpt-5.5-xhigh, Qwen3.6-27B
best_number: 2611.16867: SIMBICON written 71 times and passed 43 in 199 hopper, walker and humanoid sessions; most passes from Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Sonnet 5.5
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: four papers, none measured against a baseline.

what_and_how: Separate knowledge into layers: a model-agnostic orchestrator skill, a per-model playbook, a per-iteration state file; rank evidence tiers (live output over notes over training knowledge); keep model quirks in a data catalogue the loop reads.
problem: Mixing stable procedure with changing details forces rewrites for each new model.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only, three papers, nothing measured. Fits a pipeline with several models.

what_and_how: Store per-token keys of each skill from one middle-layer pass of the model; at routing, each task token votes for its top skills by maximum similarity, using two trained linear maps.
problem: Description matching misses the right skill when the task text barely names it.
best_number: 2609.15982: Qwen3-32B; 3.8 points on SkillRet, 13.4 on SRA-Bench
opposes: Retrieve skills or examples per task
novelty: novel: routes skills from the model's own hidden activations, not text embeddings
verdict: survived: Whether offered skills get loaded depends mainly on the model and how they are offered, including routing.
recommendation: test-first: one paper by its authors; needs model internals, so small local models only. Compare with cheap keyword retrieval first.

pattern: Validated commit gate for state writes
what_and_how: Model or tool proposes a typed write. Deterministic code checks schema, scope, role, base version and evidence, then commits or rejects. Rejected proposals leave state unchanged and are logged with a reason. Only the harness commits.
problem: Unvalidated model writes corrupt shared state, and the model grades its own evidence.
best_number: GLM-5 reject-class F1 0.256 to 0.543 on SWE-bench-Live (2610.23996)
verdict: survived: A deterministic gate admitting only findings with a citation or reproduced witness raises precision and cuts unsafe actions; strict gates drop real findings.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; budget for dropped real findings. Fits any harness, most of all where reviewers are in the loop.

what_and_how: Keep each requirement, goal or pending action as a record with status (pending, done, blocked) and evidence. A checker runs on the real tool result; a record moves to done only when the check passes. Model claims never count.
problem: Agents lose approved work and declare done with no real check behind it.
models: GPT-6.1-Sol, doubao-seed-2-0-pro, DeepSeek v4 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5
best_number: doubao-seed-2-0-pro, tau2-Retail: 58.1 base to 82.0 working state only (2608.24876)
verdict: survived: An agent's own report that it finished is unreliable on strong models; a read-only outside check of real files, state or output catches false completion.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; completion checks cost about 1.5 to 3.4 times per attempt. Fits code-change pipelines.

pattern: Typed task state shown each turn
what_and_how: Harness keeps typed objects (goals, constraints, tool results, status, validity conditions) updated by code or a separate extraction call, and renders a compact view into each model step instead of the raw transcript.
problem: Long transcripts bury task progress and why a fact is believed.
best_number: Claude Opus 4.6: ALFWorld average success 96.4 (ReAct) vs 98.6 (with workspace) (2608.05446)
verdict: survived: Keeping task state, evidence or notes in a persistent record outside the transcript raises results for mid-strength models; the strongest models gain less.
recommendation: build-in-regime: gain is for mid-strength models; strongest gain little. Fits a cheap hosted model and a multi-role code pipeline.

what_and_how: Each step, code appends plain text to the observation: location, held items, visited places, step budget, pending obligations, ready calls, and warnings on failed actions or stalls. It never picks or blocks an action.
problem: Small models loop, repeat failed actions and stop early because state stays implicit.
best_number: Qwen3-1.7B from Qwen3-8B, ALFWorld: unseen success rate 63.43 with harness, 37.31 with state tracking hidden (Table 4) (2610.02858)
verdict: survived: Small models loop and repeat failed actions; the harness needs repeat detection, failed-action blocking, budget warnings and a finish gate.
recommendation: build-in-regime: small local models only; one paper compiles text from a replayed reference run, which is not usable live. Fits a harness for a small local model.

what_and_how: Source-linked findings and evidence sit in a structured file or database outside the context, apart from conclusions. The agent reads it by targeted queries; only admitted entries count. Optionally bound it with importance tags and a duplicate filter.
problem: In-context accumulation dilutes evidence as the context grows.
best_number: Claude Sonnet 4.6; pooled 0.77 vs. 0.60 for ReAct plus subclaims without state (p = 0.0012) (2610.40906)
verdict: survived: When a task needs information that outlives the context, removing that external state costs points on strong models.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; one paper shows higher cost with a database (17.66 against 14.74 dollars). Fits any harness.

what_and_how: The agent saves facts to a table, or entity identifiers to a subset. A local script then composes pairs, checks derived claims, or fans out tool calls per entity with no further model calls. Entity text stays out of context.
problem: Long entity lists inflate tokens, and rereading memos misses contradictions.
best_number: GPT-5.6-sol mini-swe-agent 100% ($0.583) vs direct 44% ($1.17) on Outlier Memo Detection (2609.38137)
novelty: novel: agent holds subset identifiers; code fans out tool calls with no model calls.
verdict: survived: Moving repeated steps from model calls into fixed code or batched calls cuts cost or latency about 10 to 25 times at the same success.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence, two papers, own authors. Worth a trial where entity lists are long.

what_and_how: Task progress, decisions, todos, plan and artifacts go to files with a fixed layout, often under version control. Each new session or stage reads them instead of chat history, and evidence is named before any answer.
problem: Progress and evidence vanish when a session resets or the context fills.
models: gpt-5.4-mini, Claude Opus 5, Codex with GPT-5.5 (high), GPT-5.4
best_number: gpt-5.4-mini: SWE-bench Verified 73.00 to 75.60; OSWorld 44.40 to 58.30 (2603.25723)
verdict: stale: File-backed state and handoff files let long runs resume and raise scores; measured only in March on one small model, other support is argued.
recommendation: test-first: built by ten papers but measured gain is one small model in March; rest argued. Cheap, so worth a trial.

what_and_how: At stage end or from a stop hook, write one self-contained record (stage, validated controls, accepted sections, requirements with status, budget, recovery hints), replaced atomically. The next run resumes from it without replaying chat.
problem: Long runs exceed one context window, and replaying history to resume is costly.
best_number: none
verdict: stale: File-backed state and handoff files let long runs resume and raise scores; measured only in March on one small model, other support is argued.
recommendation: test-first: no paper measures resume against replay; verdict is stale. Fits a multi-role code pipeline and a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Save run state at each step or node boundary (variables, sandbox, process memory, queue) with the log. After a crash or pause, resume from the last valid one, or replay a chosen prefix and rerun the rest. Variant: store prior values to undo.
problem: A crash or late error loses progress or forces a full restart.
best_number: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Executor, GPT-5.6 Sol Planner: 79/223 (35.4%) with plan, 9/223 (4.0%) with no plan (2610.29870)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: ten papers build it, yet the numbers are microbenchmarks or authors scoring themselves, not against a plain restart. Fits a code-change pipeline.

what_and_how: Before a side effect, append the intent with an idempotency key; log each result before showing it. After a crash close open turns with unknown-outcome stand-ins, reconcile or replay; duplicate requests get rejected by receipts.
problem: After a crash or lost reply, state disagrees and effects repeat.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: After a write times out agents create duplicate side effects; idempotency keys on every write cut duplicates from 28% to 4%.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence in the tool layer. Fits harnesses whose output is a code change for review.

what_and_how: History is an append-only event log. Compaction adds a marker and keeps earlier entries; a replace masks a span without deleting it. A runtime assertion requires that everything the model saw can be rebuilt from the log.
problem: Compaction and crash recovery destroy history, so runs cannot be replayed or audited.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: seven papers argue it, none measures it against a destructive summary. Low cost.

what_and_how: An approval, task result or handoff carries the version of what it concerned (code head, task version, plan generation). It is used once and is void when that version changes; stale returns are recorded but rejected before reuse.
problem: A saved approval or late result is applied to changed state.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Approval steps fail at the binding: saved confirmations survive changed state; verify each approval against the actual effect.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence, though no paper here measures the fix. Fits setups with human review.

what_and_how: Reuse a cached result only when expected files, hashes, parameters, harness version and provenance all match; remove the completion marker if the save fails; pin datasets by hash manifest; export packages whose reload reproduces predictions.
problem: Stale or mismatched cached state is silently reused, or a failed save looks complete.
models: U-Net v0.6.1, SwinUNETR v0.5.8, SegResNet v0.2.7
best_number: 10 of 10 masks reproduced after reload in all 7 deployments (2610.34884)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: five papers, nothing measured against a baseline. Cheap hygiene for any code pipeline.

what_and_how: Each record carries the hash of the previous one, so verification finds the first break. Write the record before the effect, anchor the root outside the run (public timestamp or owner-held keys), and call a run done only when every node has a receipt.
problem: Operators cannot prove afterwards what the agent did or that the record was not edited.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Strong agents can game or tamper with weak verifiers, so verification evidence must sit outside agent reach and trajectories need audit; measured effect small.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence; only measured as logs verifying. Fits harnesses with outside reviewers.

what_and_how: A sandbox outside the harness records model calls, process runs and file writes in a hash-chained table. A query finds units the harness record lacks; a reverse check finds record entries no outside row holds.
problem: A harness can omit or invent entries in its own run record, and a reader cannot tell.
best_number: claude-sonnet-5: query reports 58 of 72 witnessed alterations; reverse check 32 of the other 43 (2609.32495)
novelty: novel: reverse check catches invented entries, not only omitted ones.
verdict: survived: Strong agents can game or tamper with weak verifiers, so verification evidence must sit outside agent reach and trajectories need audit; measured effect small.
recommendation: test-first: one paper, 14 tasks, own authors. Worth it where reviewers must trust the record.

what_and_how: Append one record per decision or call: input hashes, skill and rule versions, requested and reported model identity, old and new values, requester, decision, outcome, no raw data. Replay can check order (permission, start, end).
problem: After deployment, nobody can show which calls were checked, what changed, or why.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: ten papers build it, none measures a benefit. Required in practice where audit is required; elsewhere cheap but unproven.

what_and_how: Log every step: working state, prompt, tool call, output, token counts, diffs, configuration and versions, one record per line or file. Failures can then be split into harness and model faults, and runs re-graded without rerunning.
problem: A final answer alone cannot show which layer failed.
best_number: exact audit evidence 100.0% versus 43.2% and 27.6%; replay 44/44 versus 0/44 (2610.26101)
verdict: stale: Harness search and debugging work best from raw execution traces; scores or summaries of traces gave far less.
recommendation: test-first: twelve papers log traces but the matching verdict is stale and measured by authors. Cheap and needed for debugging; fits any harness.

what_and_how: Every output value, library entry or report line links to its source: input row, page or caption, operator event, episode, version. The report names every skipped item with its reason and shows assumptions and arithmetic.
problem: Wrong values cannot be traced to their source, and skips hide in totals.
best_number: gpt-5.4: 81.0 (±0.7) full, 70.7 (±2.1) without provenance traces (2606.21005)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one authors' ablation, two measured papers. Cheap where reviewers must follow a change back to its source.

what_and_how: Each self-improvement step appends hypothesis, change, scores, diff, decision and failures to a history. The next optimizer call reads it, so rejected ideas are not retried; a per-edit manifest attributes score change and rolls back edits that did not help.
problem: Later optimizers repeat failed fixes and lose the reason for past changes.
best_number: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: GAIA 64.6 with decision history, 51.2 without (2606.08671)
verdict: survived: The optimizer needs rich, curated failure evidence: raw traces, repeated runs or diagnosed feedback beat scores; more evidence is not better.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; curate and rank entries, never dump the pool. Fits a self-improving loop on a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Every trial stores lineage, score, diff, summary and ideas in a database. The agent gets only the database path and writes its own queries, instead of the harness choosing which records to inject.
problem: Each iteration starts blank and retries failed directions.
best_number: gpt-5.2-codex: 2.63110 with vs 2.63599 without (Table 1) (2605.15221)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: its own table shows no gain from the database (two runs per arm, one task); keep the harness-chosen history until shown otherwise.

what_and_how: Hide the evaluator from the agent. Show only whether the score changed, released only past a noise margin; keep hidden loss vectors, transcript and seeds for replay. Log each candidate with score, trace, cost.
problem: Agents reward-hack the evaluator and steer by exact failure sizes.
best_number: no harness, one run 1167 cycles, two of three runs reward hacking (2605.13821)
novelty: novel: agent sees only a changed-or-not signal; exact losses are hidden and stored for replay.
verdict: survived: A weak or fixed-input evaluator is exploited by search or by the agent, so score with a repaired check, fresh inputs or an outside oracle.
recommendation: test-first: the verdict judges exploitable evaluators, not hiding feedback; one ablation by its authors. Fits a self-improving loop on a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Keep every evaluated candidate with parent link, score, diff and evidence in an append-only tree or graph. Weaker branches stay retrievable; new candidates are seeded from the archive, not only the best one.
problem: Keeping only the best candidate loses branches that later prove useful.
best_number: NaVILA-LH test success 57.5% full, 42.5% with flat history (2609.29204)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: measured only by its authors against flat history; four papers. Fits self-improvement loops on a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Every accepted harness change is saved as a version (commit, diff with old and new values, supporting evidence). Any version can be restored; on a regression the loop returns the best version.
problem: Harness edits can make things worse and cannot be audited or reversed.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Every self-edit to a harness needs a held-out regression check and rollback; unchecked accumulation of edits can end below the unmodified agent.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; pair it with a held-out check. Fits self-improving loops and code pipelines.

what_and_how: Freeze guidance and skill versions before deployment. Every run starts from the same seed and discards its own edits and checkpoint conversations at the end; outcomes are never written back into the guidance.
problem: Edits motivated by one task impose task-specific changes on unrelated runs.
best_number: Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.00 reset per run vs 78.33 retaining edits (2611.05139)
novelty: novel: run edits are discarded at run end; the seed stays frozen.
verdict: contested: Carrying learned knowledge or harness edits to different tasks or domains: some papers show transfer, others show worse scores than resetting.
recommendation: test-first: gain of 2.67 points on 60 tasks by its own authors sits inside run noise. Fits cheap hosted self-improvement.

pattern: Lifecycle labels on failures and criteria
what_and_how: Give failure modes, criteria or scenarios lifecycle states (probation, active, dormant, retired; keep-and-evolve, keep-stable, reseed). Per failure mode, record which tasks still fail and which earlier fixes held or broke.
problem: Stale criteria keep steering edits; optimizers cannot see which fixes held.
best_number: 37.96% validation-selected with audit, 36.73% without (2610.02616)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: the one measured gain is 1.23 points, inside noise. Skip unless a self-improving loop shows repeated regressions.

what_and_how: A model turns each failed run into a short symptom label, the arm, and matches it to an existing arm or makes a new one. Each arm keeps its scenarios and evidence; retry arms rather than single scenarios.
problem: Scenario-level units fragment one weakness; category units mix several weaknesses.
novelty: novel: retry units are model-labelled failure patterns, not tasks or categories.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper, one model, own authors, equal budgets. Fits self-improvement on a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: A proxy between harness and inference server records exact token ids, log-probabilities and masks per call. Calls sharing a prefix merge into a tree; train on sampled tokens, never retokenized text; drop errored trajectories and dead leaves.
problem: Rebuilt transcripts differ from what the policy sampled, so training learns the wrong thing.
best_number: 1,185 request-level updates to 218 merged-trace updates, 189.5 to 35.2 minutes (5.39×) (2605.24220)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: only relevant if you train the model; speed measured, not training quality. Fits a harness for a small local model with training.

what_and_how: Store each run or routing decision (query, state, candidate slate, chosen action, outcome, cost, recipe, lockfile) in one schema so new metrics compute and runs group by recipe without rerunning the agent.
problem: Flat logs cannot be aggregated or reevaluated; runs from different setups cannot be compared.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only, four papers. Worth it when comparing harness variants.

what_and_how: Turn a raw stream into a compact record: log image and state only when the robot touches an object; one fixed 15-action vector per minute of video; an object graph built online at 0.5 Hz; same-day events as one state.
problem: Raw video or frames exceed context and hide state after the fact.
models: GPT-5.6 Sol, Qwen3.5-397B, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol: 82% with vs 64% without keyframe thinking (2610.34370)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: robot and video inputs only, relevant only if a harness ingests video. Each measured by its own authors.

what_and_how: Records are never edited. A defect becomes a new FAIL entry, the fix a new entry; forecasts are archived at issue and never overwritten; assets are written atomically under a lock and revisions point to their source.
problem: Overwrites destroy the old state, and a relayed correction needs another delegation round.
best_number: accuracy −3.0 points (ablation) (2606.10662)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one ablation of shared context, two argued papers. Cheap.

what_and_how: One store with fixed schemas that every worker or server reaches: per-worker state files, an append-only history, private branches merged into a main branch, a shared lock and a fail-closed controller; edits validated before sync.
problem: Concurrent workers corrupt state or drift apart; sessions die during long runs.
best_number: GPT-5.6-Luna 53.45 with engine vs 43.12 without engine, whole engine removed (Table 2, page 9) (2610.33106)
verdict: survived: On long decomposable tasks, many parallel agents sharing an append-only typed record, exclusive task claims and one workspace raise score and speed.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence; another idea shows free-talking parallel agents collide. Fits a multi-role pipeline with many roles.

what_and_how: The harness, not the model, attaches origin and trust labels, correlation ids and metadata to processes, files, stored goals and decision records. Labels only merge, never drop; rules check labels per event.
problem: Injected text takes user authority; fabricated decision records go unseen.
best_number: Qwen3.6-27B: 75.8% with feedback against 53.7% without feedback (Table 2) (2606.25189)
verdict: survived: Labelling where content came from, assigned by the harness and not by the model, stops injected text from taking user authority.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence; one measured paper. Fits where stored goals reach later turns.

what_and_how: Deterministic code owns state hand-off and checks: pass-to-pass hand-offs, scripted completion checks, one line-number assignment, a probability update per tool result. The model never copies state between steps.
problem: Models drop or corrupt state when they carry it by hand.
best_number: without update 0.78 vs full 1.13, −31.0% (Table 2) (2604.08291)
verdict: survived: Code-owned deterministic checks repeat exactly across runs, while model-composed checks and model-driven scanners vary; put gates in code.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence; four papers, one ablation. Fits any harness; cheap to try.

what_and_how: Store findings or component states as typed nodes with typed relations (support, contradiction, lineage, interaction, repair edge). Allowed relations are listed; each update touches only nearby nodes; the next round reads the graph.
problem: Flat text hides which items relate, so proposers rebuild the links each round.
best_number: GPT-5.2: 79.50 average Pass@1 without state graph, against 83.09 full (2607.26598)
verdict: contested: Structured memory (typed, hierarchical or commit-only records) beats flat raw history in authors' ablations, but a rigorous raw-history baseline matched or beat it.
recommendation: test-first: contested; gains are own-author ablations, and plain full history can match. Try against raw history first.

what_and_how: The model proposes typed operations (replace, insert, delete, resize, ban). Code applies them at verbatim, unique anchors in a stored specification and rejects missing or ambiguous anchors. Only changed entries are refreshed.
problem: Regenerating a whole document lets context collapse and erodes earlier decisions.
best_number: Nano Banana 2; w/o corrective layer 41.44 against 50.34 full (2605.30611)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: four papers, measured only by authors. Fits where a code change is a patch against stored text.

what_and_how: Each fix that passes live repair is written into the block script or prelude, so the final artifact holds the repair and a clean rebuild keeps it.
problem: Repairs made interactively vanish on a clean rebuild.
best_number: gpt-5.4-20260305: final 90.7 with patch-back versus 25.9 without (Table IV) (2611.18443)
verdict: survived: Fixes and setup repairs must be written back into the persistent setup artifact; otherwise a clean rebuild loses them.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence, one paper; a large gap, likely the result of the task design. Fits a cheap hosted model.

what_and_how: Store rules that map an action to side effects tool replies omit. A rule is stored only after live testing in a fresh environment, and frozen before test; a tracker folds each reply into state and leaves omitted fields unknown.
problem: Tool replies hide side effects, so agent state goes stale.
best_number: GLM-5.3-Flash: safe task completion 40.0 without the static layer, 75.0 with it, Table 2 (2610.11552)
novelty: novel: hidden-effect rules stored only after live test, then frozen.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one run per configuration, own authors. Fits where an organisation's own tools hide effects.

what_and_how: The model states only the primary change (where a clip plays). One executor derives every dependent change (closed gaps, moved later clips, attached titles) and one write path serves agent and manual edits.
problem: Agents would otherwise compute every knock-on change and drift from manual code paths.
best_number: five rejections in 63 trials without it, against one with it; pass rate unchanged (2610.37690)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: pass rate did not move; only fewer rejections. Fits where an organisation's own editors are used.

what_and_how: Split state by life span and owner: short-lived session state in one store, durable workflow state in another, tenant data in a third; identity and memory load separately from the code body.
problem: One store for short-lived, durable and tenant data leaks or loses state.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued only, two papers. Matters where several tenants share a harness.

what_and_how: Model a count limit as marks in an extra place, starting at the budget. Each limited firing spends one; with no mark, the call is refused. Approvals become consumable.
problem: Count limits such as one approval per run need unbounded counting that simple checks lack.
best_number: none
novelty: novel: budgets and approvals as consumable marks in a formal supervisor.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: argued with no model run. Only for provable one-approval-per-run limits.

what_and_how: Give the model a shell, file read, write and search (grep, list) and nothing else; let it call installed command line programs it already knows. Add typed tools only where a task needs them. Keep a bounded set of record operations if files are the domain.
problem: Large tool catalogues cost tokens and misfire; shells already do most of the work.
verdict: survived: On strong models, a plain shell plus file editing matches richer sets of overlapping generic tools; extra tools add tokens, not success.
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models only; one small-model run shows bash-only far behind predefined tools (10.20 against 25.20).

what_and_how: Replace a bare shell with a small set of typed tools: read a bounded file window, write, a separate localized edit, glob, search. Fuzzy or edit-distance matching repairs near-miss patches, and the runner exports the diff itself instead of parsing it from chat.
problem: Bare shell edits fail on formatting, wrong line numbers and lost patches.
models: GLM 5.1, Qwen3.7-Max, GPT-4 Turbo, Kimi K3
best_number: GPT-4 Turbo: resolved 10.7% more SWE-bench Lite tasks than a shell-only interface (ext-harness-aware-evaluation-llm-agents)
verdict: survived: Small models need natural-language, typed or structured tool layers; forcing raw code or free-form actions collapses success, while strong models cope.
recommendation: build-in-regime: weaker and small models, where raw shell edits fail; strong models match it with a plain shell.

what_and_how: Clip long tool output in the middle (keep start and end), say how much was cut, and save the full text to a file the model can search. Return typed fields, metadata beside each hit, and the exit code; do not echo the failed call back inside an error.
problem: Long or lossy tool output wastes context and hides evidence.
models: GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.4 Codex CLI, Claude Opus 4.6, Kimi K3
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol: BrowseComp-Plus score rises from 34 to 90 (2609.38372)
verdict: survived: Limits on tool output and reply length cause much of the loss between harnesses; truncation markers that tell the model how to narrow help.
recommendation: build: cheap and measured; keep inline delivery for short results because file-only delivery scored far lower (55.2 against 93.1).

what_and_how: When there are many tools, pick a connector or server first, then rank its tools by description similarity, intent and graph links, and show only a short list. Retrieval runs in code, outside the model.
problem: Hundreds of visible tools lower success and cost tokens.
best_number: none (retriever is model-independent); availability 77.8% connector-first versus 19.4% flat at 2,048 tools (2610.21098)
verdict: survived: A large visible tool menu lowers success, mostly through truncated replies, and costs tokens; narrowing candidate tools cuts cost.
recommendation: build-in-regime: only for large menus (dozens to thousands of tools); one router used ground truth.

what_and_how: Send few tool schemas up front: either hide tools behind a search and describe step the model must call first, or delete overlapping tools and shorten schemas to task-focused ones. Install domain libraries in the terminal instead of adding tools.
problem: Full schemas and overlapping tools bloat the prompt and confuse tool choice.
best_number: H1 to H2 mean pass@1: GLM-5.1 52.5 to 56.5; GPT-5.4 55.0 to 58.5; Kimi K2.6 52.0 to 59.0 (bundled with compression and retry) (2605.23950)
verdict: survived: Narrowing candidate tools cuts cost, but hiding tool names behind a search step fails small models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: pruning and short schemas for all; deferral behind search only for strong models, since a small model rejected direct calls in 95 of 96 episodes.

what_and_how: Each agent, stage or graph node gets only its own tool subset; unlisted tools are absent from its schema and every call is checked again before running. Writes are limited to a role-owned directory.
problem: One agent with every tool can call what it should not.
best_number: GPT-5.5; all 30 workflows complete correctly versus 23/30 without; unapproved files 0/30 versus 22/30 (2610.26101)
verdict: survived: Deterministic checks outside the model, such as capability scope, provenance and a per-action policy gate, block attacks at near-zero benign refusals.
recommendation: build: cheap, deterministic, no model call; stage allowlist finished 30 of 30 workflows against 23 of 30.

what_and_how: Before a shell command runs, parse it into segments and match each against allowed or denied patterns; deny by default for unknown commands, add read-only and workspace-write presets, and block deletion of checked outputs. No model call.
problem: Unchecked shell commands cause damage and injected attacks succeed.
models: GLM-5.2, Terra, GPT-5.4, Claude Code with Sonnet 4.6
best_number: GLM-5.2: attack success 98.1% to 50.0%; utility 99.2% to 97.7% (2610.07639)
verdict: survived: Command allowlists and denylists cut attacks cheaply but leak through other routes such as an allowed interpreter, a shell edit, rewritten parameters or partial egress.
recommendation: build: pair it with operating system limits, because lists leak (attack success only fell from 98.1% to 50.0%).

what_and_how: Each call is checked against identity, role, declared capability or argument provenance before any side effect; a per-turn grant lists allowed operations, and calls outside it are denied and logged. Rule scores on parameters and call sequence rank risk.
problem: Tool calls run with more authority than the task needs.
best_number: none
verdict: survived: Deterministic checks outside the model, such as capability scope, provenance and a per-action policy gate, block attacks at near-zero benign refusals.
recommendation: build: judged by other papers with medium evidence even though these twelve designs only argue it.

what_and_how: A small model labels each shell command high or low risk; only high-risk commands go to a frontier model that judges them against the user request. The judge never sees the agent reasoning.
problem: Rules miss new risky commands; a big judge on every call is slow.
best_number: Qwen3.5-0.8B gate, Claude Opus 4.6 rater; escalation risky rate 19.4% with full harness, 58.3% without classifier (Table 2, page 9) (2606.19380)
verdict: contested: Model-based judges as action gates are contested: small or bolt-on judges raised false refusals and latency, while an optimized judge cut attacks.
recommendation: test-first: judge gates are contested and this one is measured only by its authors. Prefer code gates; use as a second layer.

what_and_how: Run each rollout in a fresh container or pod with its own browser context and credentials, started from the unchanged task image with a small injected agent, destroyed afterwards. Block named domains or credentials to keep arms apart.
problem: Runs interfere with each other and leak state or credentials.
best_number: 2.7 points average and 5.0 worst against official OSWorld over 13 models; memory 0.6 GB against 3.8 GB (2610.26071)
verdict: unmeasured: A harness that runs generated or self-edited code needs sandboxing, explicit permission boundaries and a hard time limit.
recommendation: test-first: judged unmeasured; the papers only show it matches the official environment (2.7 points off). Needed anyway for a multi-role code pipeline and a harness with outside reviewers.

what_and_how: Check each proposed call against the tool registry, schema and argument rules before running; on failure run nothing, return the reason with the available tools and the required correction, and require a different next call. One uniform result envelope for success and failure.
problem: Malformed or invented calls waste turns and cause damage.
best_number: Qwen3-4B-Instruct: w/o Action Airline -61.7% (Table 4) (2605.22166)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: built in a dozen papers but only one measures it (Qwen3-4B-Instruct, -61.7% without). Cheap to build; measure for small local models.

what_and_how: Fix model output instead of rejecting it: repair escaping and truncation, normalize arguments within bounds, convert custom call formats, ban the exact failed string at decoding, or move tool definitions into the system message so the model calls them.
problem: Small models emit broken tool calls and repeat failed ones.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: big gains on gpt-oss-20b come from its own authors.

what_and_how: Put code at the tool call point: correct arguments silently, block a call whose prerequisite is missing, append a warning after many calls without output, run policy helpers inside the tool wrapper. Edits must act on a real event, not give advice.
problem: Prompt instructions get skipped; behavior rules need enforcing in code.
best_number: gpt-5.4-mini inner, claude-opus-4.7 outer; Retail MeanLift 14.9 full, 4.7 with unconstrained edits (2609.05736)
verdict: survived: Targeted runtime rules fired at a logged risky state, or verified tool-health state, raise repeated success and cut waste, while generic self-checks add nothing.
recommendation: test-first: evidence is weak and from the authors; restrict edits to three patterns (unconstrained edits gave 4.7 instead of 14.9).

what_and_how: Attach an idempotency key to every write; the service runs each key once and returns the first result on repeats. Wrap database writes in pre-image and post-image statements so rollback restores rows. Apply patches all-or-nothing and record one terminal state per call.
problem: Timeouts and retries create duplicate or half-done changes.
best_number: claude-opus-5.5, gpt-6-sol, gemini-3.8-flash, mai-code-1.1-flash (pooled): late-commit duplicates 61% native, 9% keys everywhere (2609.29095)
verdict: survived: After a write times out agents create duplicate side effects; idempotency keys on every write cut duplicates from 28% to 4%.
recommendation: build: medium evidence on strong models and several harnesses.

what_and_how: Move arithmetic, date math, identity lookup and constrained optimization out of the model: it lists the inputs, code computes in a fixed order and returns the result, and checked lookup tables return canonical identifiers.
problem: Models miscalculate and invent identifiers.
best_number: Sonnet 4.6 T2 normalization 0.881 vs T1 0.282; Haiku 4.5 T2 0.103 (2610.19999)
verdict: survived: Tools that give information or actions the model cannot get from text alone, such as a computation tool, give large gains for weaker models.
recommendation: build: strongest and cheapest rule in the set; one paper saw a calculator offload turn out worse.

what_and_how: Code owns the procedure: fixed project template, fixed interface, install scripts, route classifier, command line tools that write input files and check consistency. The model picks steps or fills named slots; unfilled parts return an explicit error.
problem: Open-ended agent loops drift and break structure.
best_number: Claude Sonnet 4.5 Avg 56.4 (Direct CoT 27.1), Table 3 Full ReFlect (2605.05737)
verdict: survived: Where the domain has explicit rules, moving plan checking and repair into deterministic code beats model feedback loops and lifts small models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: domains with explicit rules, and small models.

what_and_how: Group independent tool calls: tell the model to batch them, offer one search call with several query rewrites, fuse an edit with its test run, or send several typed questions in one request. Results come back in input order.
problem: Many small tool calls cost turns, and each turn re-reads the context.
best_number: GPT-5-mini 4.79 average tool calls versus 6.79 without multi-query search (2605.05538)
verdict: survived: Moving repeated steps into fixed code, compiled behaviors or batched calls cuts cost or latency by about 10 to 25 times at the same success.
recommendation: test-first: gains are small (up to 30% fewer turns, one 1.02 cost ratio) and self-measured. Cheap to try on a cheap hosted model.

pattern: Model writes code that composes tools
what_and_how: The model writes a short program per step that calls tools, filters results and keeps only what matters; a sandboxed interpreter runs it with a time limit and the full results stay out of context. Restrict the program to one allowed call per line.
problem: Many round trips with big raw results flood the context.
best_number: GPT-6-Luna: overall Hit at 1 75.2 vs 72.8 for predefined graph tools (Table 3) (2610.18616)
verdict: survived: Giving a strong model the data as files with a shell or code matches or beats pre-built query and search tools, and is cheaper.
recommendation: build-in-regime: strong models only; small models collapse when forced to write raw code.

pattern: Tools built or mined from experience
what_and_how: The agent writes a helper for repeated work, validates it privately, registers it, and reuses it across later tasks; chains of validated calls run without model calls. Tools can also be mined offline from logs and expert traces with a check that quotes are verbatim.
problem: The same multi-step tool sequence is rewritten every task.
best_number: gpt-5.6-sol: AppWorld cost per task $0.141 vs $0.359; SREGym median diagnosis 81 to 53 seconds (2611.00463)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: cost per task fell from $0.359 to $0.141 in one paper, but learned reuse is not judged and learners can hurt strong models.

what_and_how: An optimizer agent rewrites tool descriptions, tool code or the harness folder, and may add a tool such as a file downloader; syntax is checked and only the tool files may change. Tested on held-out tasks.
problem: Hand-written tool descriptions and code are not tuned to the agent.
best_number: Claude Opus 4.7 optimizer; GPT-4.1 agent; Telecom 29.50% to 36.75% (2610.34679)
verdict: contested: Automatic edits to tool descriptions and code raise pass rate on the tuned tasks and agent, but the gain does not transfer across agents.
