recommendation: test-first: contested; gains do not transfer and description rewrites alone lowered reward. Only for a fixed agent and task set with held-out tests.

pattern: Structured query tool over indexed data
what_and_how: Build tables or graphs offline (file rows, line ranges, call graph, timeline) and give the model a read-only query tool with bounded rows and a deadline; answers come from one join or one graph lookup, not many greps.
problem: Scanning raw files turn by turn is slow and loses evidence.
best_number: Qwen3-8B 2.2% non-harness to 15.5% DSH-SQL on Spider 2.0-SQLite (Table 3) (2610.12274)
verdict: survived: When material is too large to read, a structure-aware index or retrieval tool raises localization and pass rates, most for weaker models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: large corpora and weaker models; strong models gained nothing in one graph run (-2.5).

pattern: Retrieval pipelines with fusion and fallback
what_and_how: Retrieve with several rewrites, engines or rankers, merge and de-duplicate candidates, rerank, and walk a fallback ladder (relax filters, raw lexical search, wider window) before concluding nothing exists; the model iterates its own queries.
problem: One query misses evidence, and a miss is read as absence.
models: Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek V4 Flash, GPT-5 mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5
best_number: Claude Opus 4.8; Audit@1 70.0% with the full system, 42.3% without single-step prediction (page 8) (2610.24744)
verdict: survived: Single-shot search with the raw question as the query adds nothing over closed-book answering; the gain comes from search the model iterates.
recommendation: test-first: the verdict supports iterated search, not each fusion design; numbers are self-measured.

pattern: Direct call instead of tool agent
what_and_how: Skip the agent loop: send the documents or the claim once to the model, or force one tool call per stage, and compare against the tool-using agent. Use the direct call as the baseline.
problem: Agent loops add cost and no gain when the bare model can answer.
models: Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.7 Flash
best_number: Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.7 Flash; Claude mean paired difference +0.033, not significant (2610.37851)
verdict: survived: For document-reading reconstruction tasks, strong models run as native coding agents with tools do not measurably beat calling the same models directly.
recommendation: build-in-regime: read-and-answer tasks on strong models; run it as the baseline in every harness.

what_and_how: Give the agent real checkers as tools: compile and run probe, simulator, interactive debugger with reverse execution, static analyzers, per-line profile files, test-to-function footprints, fail-fast validators run in order. Results return to the loop.
problem: Models cannot see program behavior from text alone.
models: DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini-3.1 Pro Preview
best_number: DeepSeek-V3.2: full 179 (89.5%); GDB-only 164 (82.0%); without debugger 154 (77.0%) (2604.03610)
verdict: survived: A task-specific checker, compile-and-run probe or verifier tool carries most of a harness lift; generic self-critique adds little.
recommendation: build: medium evidence from several papers; some gains small or null (Verilog tools 47.61 against 47.39).

what_and_how: Wrap a vision, audio or document model as narrow callable tools (find, measure, inspect region, caption span, depth query, text recognition, coarse-to-fine video search) so the main model asks questions and receives text or numbers; keep raw media out of context.
problem: The main model cannot see or hear the input well.
models: gpt-5.4, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, GPT-5.6 Sol
verdict: survived: Tools that give the model information or actions it cannot get from text alone, such as perception, give large gains, especially for weaker models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: tasks with images, audio or video; tools gave nothing for mammography reading (0.108 to 0.106).

pattern: Object, pixel and semantic action tools
what_and_how: Let the model name an object, a pixel in a view or a semantic step, and code converts it to coordinates, plans the path, checks safety and returns the outcome; the model never sends joint angles. One shared small call set across robots.
problem: Raw low-level control from a language model fails.
models: GPT-6-Astra, Gemini-3.7-Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra, Gemini-3.1 Pro
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol: 82% with vs 28% without whole-body control (2610.34370)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: many robotics papers, all self-measured on different benchmarks. Outside harnesses unless a product controls a device.

pattern: Hand control to a learned policy
what_and_how: Add one tool that starts a trained policy or navigation executor for a bounded number of steps and returns a few images and status; the language model plans, checks the result, and re-invokes or takes over. Code decides which executor runs.
problem: Language models are slow and weak at fine control.
models: GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Luna, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B
best_number: Claude Opus 5: success rate 73 without delegation, 76 to 81 with it; cost 0.99 dollars to 0.35-0.40 dollars per episode (page 12) (2610.10787)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: delegation raised success and cut cost per episode in one paper, but self-measured. Idea transfers to delegating to any bounded specialist tool.

pattern: Typed domain operations with stable references
what_and_how: Replace free text with typed operations on the domain (extrude, edit table column, add node): the harness binds ids to the document, returns stable references, applies constraints in fixed order, and rejects bad operations; the model cites ids, never describes shapes.
problem: Free-form edits to structured artifacts break and are hard to refer to.
best_number: Qwen3.8-27B structural success 33.33% (6/18) with tile edits alone to 77.78% (14/18) with high-level tools (ext-agentic-pcg-harness-controlled-local-models)
verdict: survived: Small models need natural-language, typed or structured tool layers; forcing them to write raw code or free-form actions collapses success.
recommendation: build-in-regime: structured artifacts and small models; every gain is self-measured.

pattern: Native files and code, not renders
what_and_how: Hand the model the original file plus file reading and code execution so it computes measurements itself, rather than showing fixed rendered images or adding viewer tools. Viewer tools added on top gave no gain.
problem: Rendered views throw away exact data the model could compute from.
best_number: GPT-6 Astra 0.5291 native versus 0.2498 rendered images (2611.04087)
verdict: survived: Giving a strong model the data as files with a shell or code matches or beats pre-built query and search tools, and is cheaper.
recommendation: test-first: one benchmark, one author group (0.5291 native against 0.2498 rendered). Check on your own data formats.

what_and_how: A small resident language model reads the tool schema and turns the caller's plain-language need into the typed call, retry count and priority; the caller never sees the schema. A router fills step arguments and dispatches.
problem: Small models cannot fill complex tool schemas.
best_number: Qwen3-8B; ToolBench pass rate from 55.8% to 75.1% (2611.07461)
novelty: novel: a second model, not code, turns plain need into the typed call
verdict: survived: Small models need natural-language, typed or structured tool layers; forcing them to write raw code or free-form actions collapses success.
recommendation: test-first: two papers, weak evidence (75.1 against 16.1 without). Try for small local models with their own tool set.

what_and_how: Rewrite tool names and descriptions as instructions, keep each action atomic, separate callable tools from documents, let the model decide whether to invoke a skill, and measure how often skills are loaded per model.
problem: Models ignore or misuse tools and skills as described.
best_number: GPT-5.6-Sol: 11% to 63% (skills only); GPT-6 Astra: 92% to 61% (skills only), 85% (skills on demand) (2611.18359)
verdict: survived: Whether offered skills get loaded depends mainly on the model and on how they are offered; weak models and always-on listings rarely load them.
recommendation: test-first: results are model dependent (one model fell from 92% to 61%); description rewrites alone can lower reward. Measure on each model.

what_and_how: Point an unchanged harness at a proxy that forwards model calls, records every request and reply, can swap the backend model, enforces credentials outside the container, or runs the policy for training rollouts.
problem: Harness code cannot be changed, but its model traffic must be logged or controlled.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: infrastructure, not a quality gain; the 3.8% to 26.4% number measures training use. Useful for logging in a multi-role code pipeline and a harness with outside reviewers.

what_and_how: Write one small adapter per harness or framework that maps native tools, logs and tasks onto a shared case and trace format, so models, cases and metrics stay unchanged and new harnesses are compared with one interface.
problem: Comparing harnesses needs a pairwise port for each one.
best_number: Qwen3.8-Max / Qwen Code mean 70.2%; Qwen3.8-Max / OpenCode mean 58.3% (2610.35773)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: evaluation plumbing; the one measurement shows the harness pairing moves scores (70.2 against 58.3). Useful when comparing harnesses.

what_and_how: Put tools in separate servers with their own dependencies behind the Model Context Protocol, with typed inputs and outputs, so any harness can call them; start long computations asynchronously with a concurrency cap and timeout.
problem: Tools tied to one harness cannot be reused or isolated.
best_number: gpt-5.6-sol; 32.0% fewer tokens, 6.784M vs 9.982M, Problem 17.91 (2607.27705)
verdict: contested: Whether tools arrive through a protocol server or a command line sets neither score nor cost reliably.
recommendation: test-first: contested; a command line beat it in at least one paper (59.90 against 45.52). Use servers for isolation and reuse, not for score.

pattern: Live tool and process state signals
what_and_how: Measure tool health (probe success, latency average, circuit state, age) in code and show the model a snapshot before it picks a tool; detect idle or waiting processes from system call samples; list claimable tasks.
problem: The model picks failing or slow tools with no knowledge of their state.
models: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.7 Flash
best_number: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.7 Flash; mean regret 4,251.54 ms to 131.12 ms (2611.05391)
novelty: novel: verified tool-health snapshot shown to the model before it chooses a tool
verdict: survived: Giving a model verified, fresh tool-health state before each action cuts regret and failed completions against a neutral control of the same shape.
recommendation: test-first: one paper, own benchmark, 9 live decisions per condition (regret 4,251.54 ms to 131.12 ms). Cheap to test in a multi-role code pipeline.

what_and_how: Give tools that control the running environment: pause, step frames, inject actions, read node state, take screenshots, return the screenshot with the action result, read transient notifications, run tasks on virtual displays.
problem: The model cannot observe or pace a live environment.
best_number: GPT-5.6-Luna 53.45 with engine vs 43.12 without engine, whole engine removed (Table 2, page 9) (2610.33106)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: the engine as a whole gave 53.45 against 43.12, parts were not isolated. Relevant only to game or screen products.

what_and_how: Give each parallel agent its own git worktree or virtual workspace from the parent branch, deliver group messages in one order, and run workflows in background with a worker limit that the agent can inspect and stop.
problem: Parallel agents overwrite each other.
best_number: gpt-5.2-codex and gpt-5.1-codex-mini: speedup 3.2x to 3.9x with 4 agents (Table 2) (2605.15221)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: speedup measured in one paper (3.2x to 3.9x); the standing rule already requires worktrees for parallel writers.

what_and_how: Expose harness functions as normal actions the model calls and pays for: track, commit, recall, note, a private think tool, and load or unload a module that changes the active rules. The harness records and enforces them.
problem: Always-on harness steps waste budget; fixed steps cannot adapt.
best_number: Qwen3-8B; ALFWorld average success 95.0 (learned) vs 88.6 (always-on) (2608.05446)
novelty: novel: formal modules loaded and unloaded by actions that change allowed tools
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: learned use beat always-on (95.0 against 88.6) on one small model; the think tool result was weak. Formal paper ran no model.

what_and_how: Return typed measured values plus one sentence of conclusion with units and frame, a coarse evidence grade instead of a raw number, a labeled failure category for each command, and report what a tool measured, not what it meant to do.
problem: Raw tool output misleads the model or hides failure.
best_number: Qwen3.8-27B: MMSI-Bench 66.5 full, 65.2 without interpreted readout; ReVSI 82.3 full, 81.1 without (2610.28354)
verdict: survived: A command that returns success without doing the action misleads agents; a wrapper that reports the real effect removes most of the confusion.
recommendation: test-first: one measured gain is small (66.5 against 65.2); others argue only. Cheap to add for small local models.

what_and_how: The agent writes import-time stubs that stand in for database calls and return symbolic values bounded by schema constraints from models and migrations; the symbolic tool then explores code paths, and the agent writes a reproducing test per finding.
problem: Symbolic execution cannot run code that touches a database.
novelty: novel: model-written stubs with schema-bounded symbolic values let symbolic execution reach database code
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: one paper, one model, ablation of three settings (4.5%, 29.5%, 81%); costs far more than the baseline. Narrow use: bug finding in an organisation's code.

what_and_how: Run the grader in a separate container or host, on held-out cases and ground truth the agent cannot read or edit. The agent claim of completion never counts; only the checker reading real files and state does.
problem: Agents report false success and can tamper with checks they can reach.
models: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra
best_number: with checker hidden: 83.2 to 63.5 and 42.0 to 26.1 (2611.18359)
verdict: survived: An agent own report that it finished is unreliable on strong models; a read-only outside check of real files, state or output catches false completion.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence and cheap in code; fits every harness, most of all a multi-role code pipeline and a builder on a hosted model.

what_and_how: After the builder stops, a separate critic in a fresh context receives the task and the change set, gets sandbox access, runs its own checks and returns findings before acceptance. Use a different model or product where possible; one critic and one round gives most of the gain.
problem: Builders overrate their own finished work and miss defects a fresh reader finds.
best_number: one critic and one round 62.7%; four rounds 66.1%; four critics 65.8% (2610.34577)
verdict: survived: A separate critic or different coding product, given the task and the changes, raises accuracy at modest extra cost; self-review at completion does not.
recommendation: build: separate critic survived at modest extra cost (1.13 to 1.25 times).

what_and_how: A reviewer model, often the same model given the manual, approves or blocks every state-changing tool call and gives a reason; riskier tool tiers go to the reviewer, safe ones pass. A block returns the reason to the agent.
problem: A single tool call can break a rule or do damage the agent did not foresee.
verdict: contested: Per-action review by a reviewer model may cut rule violations in a rule-heavy domain but showed no pass-rate gain on shell work.
recommendation: test-first: contested; violations fell in one rule-heavy domain but no pass-rate gain on shell work; trial it first where an organisation's own rules apply.

what_and_how: Code, not a model, checks every tool call before it runs: read a script before running it, scope and provenance rules, collision or deadlock tests, identifiers must have appeared in an earlier result. Violations are blocked and explained to the agent.
problem: Models skip safe-use steps and take unsafe actions that prompt text alone does not stop.
verdict: survived: Deterministic checks outside the model, such as capability scope, provenance and a per-action policy gate, block attacks at near-zero benign refusals.
recommendation: build: outside-model checks survived with medium evidence.

what_and_how: Ask the same model to re-check, critique or grade its own draft or step: a checklist inserted every few steps, a second call with a checklist, or a lower-only sceptic pass. No new outside information is added.
problem: A cheap attempt to catch errors without tests or a second system.
models: GPT-5.5 Codex high, GPT-5, gpt-5.4-nano, GPT-6 Luna
best_number: ReAct Base 30.39 to Self-Refine 32.74 (2606.14674)
verdict: survived: A model told to re-check or grade its own work, with no new outside information, does not raise success and sometimes discards correct work.
recommendation: do-not-build: survived verdict shows no success gain and some discarded correct work; use an outside check instead, in every harness.

what_and_how: Add a short standing sentence to the system message telling the agent to run the deliverable through its real interface, inspect the output and report results as observed, not assumed. No harness code enforces it.
problem: Agents stop without running their work and report assumed success.
best_number: system-role instruction averages +3.3 points on Terminal-Bench (2610.34577)
verdict: survived: One short, positive, factual sentence (verify the work, report the retrieval status, state a rejection) reliably changes a measurable behaviour.
recommendation: test-first: changes behaviour but gains are small and uneven per model, and an always-verify line matched the baseline; cheap to trial on a builder on a hosted model.

what_and_how: The harness treats the model stop as a proposal. Before accepting it re-injects the task, runs the task checks and requires evidence of the right kind: command result, probe or independent review. Gaps send the agent back; any edit clears earlier check results.
problem: Agents declare completion early or on thin evidence.
best_number: Terminal-Bench Hard Pass@1 56.75 seed to 64.00 with all four cumulative mechanisms (2610.27435)
verdict: contested: A finish gate that checks outside evidence before handoff gives small to moderate gains on strong models, but the gain is uncertain.
recommendation: test-first: contested; gains of 2 to 6 points often cross zero on strong models; keep for small local models, where loops are the failure.

what_and_how: After each change run the tests, compiler or checker, send failure text naming the failing file and assertion back to the agent and let it repair, with a round cap near three. Detailed messages beat pass or fail only.
problem: A one-shot model rarely gets code or configuration right without seeing what failed.
models: GLM-5, gpt-5.4-20260305, DeepSeek V3.2, Codex GPT-4o
verdict: survived: Concrete outside feedback that names what failed raises success far above no feedback, and detailed feedback beats minimal.
recommendation: build: concrete failure feedback survived with medium evidence; cap rounds near three; for small local models test per task, retries gave nothing on some.

what_and_how: Execute the model plan in a simulator or on a state graph in code. Where a precondition fails, apply the repair the rules imply or return the error, with a small retry cap. No model judges feasibility.
problem: Models write plans that break the rules of the domain.
best_number: Qwen3-4B: 67.7 ± 1.6 success (gavel-basic) vs 21.8 ± 1.5 (llm-only) (2609.19315)
verdict: survived: Where the domain has explicit state and rules, moving plan checking and repair into deterministic code beats model feedback loops and lifts small models.
recommendation: build-in-regime: survived with medium evidence where the domain has explicit state and rules and the model is small.

what_and_how: Before any run, check cheaply and deterministically that the proposal is well formed: graph wiring, schema, imports, interface, a crash test on one tiny input. Failures return an error for repair and cost no scoring budget.
problem: Broken candidates waste evaluation runs and are scored as model failures.
best_number: none
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and no line measures it against a baseline; very cheap, so trial it first in a multi-role code pipeline.

what_and_how: Sample several candidates (4 to 8), run each through a real evaluator (compile, test, timing) and keep the best by evaluator score; a model judge only breaks ties. A trained value model can rerank.
problem: One sample is often wrong; a real signal can pick the right one.
best_number: 3%→33% correct from n=1 to n=8 (2611.12079)
verdict: survived: When several candidates can be sampled, choosing among them with a real executed check or critique signal recovers part of the gap.
recommendation: build-in-regime: survived with medium evidence; pays most for small or cheap models and needs a real evaluator.

what_and_how: Several judge models, ideally from different families, score or compare candidates; a majority, weighted win rate or chief judge picks the winner, and the panel abstains when judges disagree.
problem: One model judge is noisy and biased; combining judges tries to average the error out.
best_number: 11.4% without ranking versus 51.7% (2606.27243)
verdict: survived: A same-strength or weaker model grading holistically or by pairwise preference is unreliable: position bias, self-preference, inflated scores; it cannot be the only grader.
recommendation: test-first: judges of similar strength show position bias and self-preference; use only beside an executed signal; measured on authors own benchmarks.

what_and_how: A strong judge scores each checklist item separately, given a reference, tool output or rendered evidence, and returns a labelled verdict per item; code applies weights and gates. Calibrate against human labels first.
problem: Open-ended outputs have no test; whole-output grades are vague and unstable.
models: Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude Opus 5
best_number: 95.8% agreement with humans on 264 judgments (2611.05512)
verdict: survived: A strong judge scoring each rubric item separately, with a reference or rendered evidence, agrees with humans in roughly 83 to 96 percent of cases.
recommendation: build: strong per-item judge survived with medium evidence (83 to 96 percent human agreement); validate on your own labels.

what_and_how: After a draft, run decomposed pass-fail checks or rule checks plus a critic that returns per-dimension defects and corrections; the agent patches only the failed items, up to about three rounds, and keeps the best output so far.
problem: Open-ended outputs need targeted fixes, not regeneration.
best_number: w/o refinement loop 44.86, w/o directive critic 45.30, full 50.34 (2605.30611)
verdict: survived: Rubric or verifier-guided revision of open-ended outputs beats direct generation, and the detail of the reviewer feedback matters more than self-checking or more reasoning.
recommendation: build: rubric-guided revision survived with medium evidence; detail of feedback matters; cap rounds.

what_and_how: Write checks as ordinary code over the output or trace: regular expression, schema, recomputation, assertion, each returning pass or fail. Use a model only for what code cannot decide, and cap any model judge weight.
problem: Model graders vary between runs and can be talked around.
models: Claude Sonnet 4, deepseek-v4-pro, GPT-5.5 (Codex), Claude Haiku 4.5
best_number: prompt-only 15 / 15 violations, validators 0 / 0 (2607.08028)
verdict: survived: Code-owned deterministic checks repeat exactly across runs, while model-composed checks and model-driven scanners vary; put gates in code, not in a model prompt.
recommendation: test-first: survived with weak evidence (repeat exactly is near-trivial); cheap and default for every harness, but measure accuracy against labels.

what_and_how: Count a task as accepted only when separate gates pass: build, target test, regression test, quality or policy checks, constraint compliance; a fatal gate zeroes the score. Passing the project tests alone is not acceptance.
problem: Test-passing results often violate constraints, policies or quality bars.
best_number: Constraint-Missing Compliance 4.7 vs Full 98.7 (2610.18090)
verdict: survived: Passing the project own tests or compiling is a weak signal of acceptable work; a separate quality or acceptance gate rejects many test-passing results.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence across eight papers.

what_and_how: A finding enters the report only if the harness runs a reproducer, planted-secret oracle or counterexample that shows the fault, or a cited receipt that a code check accepts; unproven findings are withheld or downgraded.
problem: Review and security agents report many false findings.
models: Claude Opus 5.5, GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, Sonnet 5
best_number: precision 1.000 with oracle, 0.422 graph without, 0.193 bare ReAct (2610.31831)
verdict: survived: A deterministic gate admitting only findings backed by a citation or reproduced witness raises precision, but strict gates also drop real findings.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; strict gates drop real findings, so keep a tier for unproven ones.

what_and_how: For each claim check that the cited source exists, was actually retrieved in this run, and that its span supports the claim; unsupported claims are edited or dropped. Use a judge from another model family for support.
problem: Models cite real but irrelevant sources, or sources they never read.
best_number: 1 of 186 closed-book citations relevant (2610.29812)
verdict: survived: A check that a cited source exists is not enough; verify that the cited evidence supports the claim.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence in four October papers.

pattern: Check against reference, simulator or proof
what_and_how: Run the candidate against an independent reference: differential test on fuzz inputs, symbolic equivalence, simulator, legal-move check or formal proof checker, and accept only on a match.
problem: Output looks right but is wrong in ways only an executable comparison shows.
best_number: total wall time 966.50 s without gate, 389.81 s with gate (2611.02784)
verdict: survived: A check that uses new evidence outside the model own output (a test, a rule document, a strict proof checker) catches real errors.
recommendation: test-first: outside-evidence checks survived but only with weak evidence from authors own benchmarks; worth building where a reference exists, in a multi-role code pipeline.

what_and_how: Treat model-written tests as suspect: they must pass the reference, fail the unmodified base and fail variants that each break one requirement; calibrate with a blind solver and keep a hidden suite.
problem: Generated tests reject correct work and pass wrong work.
best_number: first suites missed 271 of 1,307 fixed mutants (20.7%) (2611.02440)
verdict: survived: Verifiers and tests written by the model reject correct work more often than wrong work, so they need checking against reference solutions.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; generated verifiers accepted valid solutions only 21 to 70 percent of the time.

what_and_how: Before a task joins a benchmark or training pool, require the reference solution to pass, the unmodified repository to fail, mutants to be caught and no-work attempts to fail; verdicts must repeat across reruns.
problem: Defective tasks and scorers move scores by tens of points.
models: Claude Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek-V3.1, DeepSeek V3.2, Claude Opus 4.8
verdict: survived: Benchmark and grader defects are common and move scores by tens of points; audit tasks, oracles and scorers with a reference solution and by replay.
recommendation: build: survived with strong evidence; run before trusting any number, in every harness evaluation, the testing method first.

what_and_how: Audit the evaluation apparatus itself: replay archived calls on a fresh database to relabel episodes, run state invariants and known-answer controls, re-grade stored outputs with a stronger suite, scan for hack paths.
problem: Scoring defects are counted as model failures or successes.
best_number: pooled success 94.3% archived, 65.5% replayed (2610.16067)
verdict: survived: Benchmark and grader defects are common and move scores by tens of points; audit tasks, oracles and scorers with a reference solution and by replay.
recommendation: build: survived with strong evidence.

what_and_how: Score each proposed change to prompts, tools or rules on held-out tasks the proposer never sees; keep it only if the score does not fall, else restore the previous version. Cap iterations and keep the best validated snapshot.
problem: Self-edits nobody checks drift the harness worse.
best_number: MiniMax M2.5 Terminal-Bench-2.0 held-out 40.5 to 61.9 (2606.09498)
verdict: survived: Letting a model accept its own harness edits without an outside held-out check makes the harness drift worse; an outside gate with rollback stops it.
recommendation: build: outside gate with rollback survived with medium evidence; one gate is noisy, so pair with paired margins.

what_and_how: Admit a change only when paired runs of old and new harness on the same tasks show a gain above a margin: paired permutation test, lower confidence bound, repeated trials, noise floor from unchanged reruns.
problem: Small samples let noise and harmful edits through the gate.
models: GPT-5.4, GPT-4.1 agent, GPT-5 medium, Qwen3.6-27B
best_number: Telecom AT-AT p value 0.0033, gain 7.25 percentage points (2610.34679)
verdict: survived: A gate that admits harness edits on the same visible tasks admits noise and harmful edits; gates need fresh held-out instances and a statistical margin.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; spend repeated runs where gains are small; weigh the cost, gates multiply runs.

what_and_how: Keep a protected set of earlier passing cases and replay the whole corpus under each candidate; reject any change that drops a protected case or loses a previously solved task, even if the target failure improves.
problem: Fixes for one failure often break behaviour that worked.
models: Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5 mini, Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview
best_number: +55.0 points of pass rate on held-out rule families (2610.14216)
verdict: survived: Fixes for one failure often break behaviour that worked, and models predict their own regressions near chance, so replay earlier cases before accepting a change.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence (replay rejected 383 proposed rules, 211 of them regressed).

what_and_how: On failure, record observed against expected output, map the failing check to the component it implicates, and send structured feedback to only that component for the next round, instead of free-text reflection.
problem: Agents retry blindly and fix the wrong part.
models: GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.4 mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, deepseek-v4-flash-preview
best_number: 92.6 without diagnosis feedback vs 97.0 on SWE-bench Verified (2610.07832)
verdict: survived: Diagnosis that names the failing component and routes the failure back raises repair success; free-text self-reflection finds the region but rarely the cause.
recommendation: build: survived with medium evidence; keep the diagnosis typed.

pattern: Leakage and tampering scan of edits
what_and_how: A reviewer with fresh context and no search data reads each candidate diff and rejects edits that encode task names, answers or literal artifacts; an auditor also reads applied diffs for tampering with the checker.
problem: Evolving harnesses cheat the benchmark.
verdict: survived: Evolved harnesses can cheat or tamper: hard-coded answers, removed model calls, ignored anti-cheating checks; scan edits, read diffs, and keep a held-out check.
recommendation: build: survived with strong evidence that evolved harnesses cheat; read every edit that touches scoring.

what_and_how: Keep only trajectories whose final result passes an executable or hidden check and drop failed runs or invalid actions; use verifier outputs as the reward. Applies only to builds that train a model.
problem: Unfiltered traces teach wrong behaviour.
best_number: 63.0 selected vs 58.9 unfiltered (2609.08919)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and measured only by authors; relevant only for small local models if training is planned.

what_and_how: After a tool reports success, read the authoritative state back by a separate path and compare it with the intended effect; retry only after a verified no-commit; treat a timeout as uncertain, not failed.
problem: A returned success does not prove the effect happened.
best_number: without effect verification 410/450 physical completion, verified completion not certifiable (2609.32184)
verdict: survived: An agent can finish a harmful action and report only success, so reviewers must check actions and state, not the agent own summary.
recommendation: build: agents reporting success wrongly survived with medium evidence; cheap in code.

what_and_how: Verify after each step or every k steps and roll back to the last accepted checkpoint when a segment fails; choose k from verifier cost and error rate; run cheap checks first and detailed diagnosis only on failure.
problem: Errors compound over long chains, and checking everything is expensive.
models: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5 mini, GPT-4o, GPT-5.4-mini
best_number: k = 4 selected, 1/100 failures, weighted cost 25.2 [24.1, 26.4] (2610.02488)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged; every-step checks cost 1.5 to 3.4 times in the cost idea; trial selective checks on long pipeline tasks.

what_and_how: A model judge flags outputs; a domain expert re-reviews each flag and reclassifies confirmed errors; a second model relabels a sample and humans arbitrate disagreements; near-threshold cases go to people.
problem: Model judges err systematically and need human ground truth.
best_number: 9 of 72 labels revised from pass to fail (2611.14493)
verdict: survived: Routing items to human review by a model score raises task quality in one study, but raw model confidence is poorly calibrated.
recommendation: test-first: survived only with weak evidence from one author-run study; keep where people review each change anyway.

what_and_how: Train a small verifier on teacher or outcome labels: a completion detector that reads the executor hidden states, a student judge distilled from a frontier teacher, or a decision-only verifier reading one token.
problem: Prompting a large model to verify is slow and costly.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and measured on authors own tasks; worth it only for small local models where a large critic is unaffordable.

what_and_how: A separate agent or script recomputes every headline figure from primary records, ties filed totals to source lines, checks that differences cluster where a known cause explains them, and reproduces results in a fresh run.
problem: Reported numbers are wrong or cannot be reproduced.
models: claude-opus-5, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5
best_number: 8 of 8 checked vs 1 of 8 unchecked re-derived headline numbers, p = 0.001 (2609.23957)

what_and_how: The model extracts requirements from the issue, predicts an input and expected output for each, simulates the patch by reasoning alone or writes its own reference, and repairs on mismatch. No code is executed.
problem: Running tests is costly or impossible; reasoning checks claim to catch the same errors.
best_number: MiniMax-M3 57% versus 27% (2610.23782)
verdict: survived: A model told to re-check or grade its own work, with no new outside information, does not raise success and sometimes discards correct work.
recommendation: test-first: authors own gains conflict with the survived verdict that reflection without outside evidence does not help; try only where tests cannot run.

what_and_how: Before each run query the served model identifier at the pinned backend and compare it with the pin; for audit, run calibration batches of the claimed model and compare channels with a permutation test.
problem: Hosted models change or are swapped silently, invalidating results.
best_number: channel-first fusion detects 66.7% vs. 100% of the 4-bit derivative of Qwen3.5-27B (2611.01950)
novelty: novel: tests whether the claimed model is really the one served, by statistical audit.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and one paper; cheap to add and useful for a builder on a hosted model, where the provider can change the model.

what_and_how: Every gate ships with a good and a bad fixture proving it still fires; a gate that cannot run counts as skipped, never passed; each hook writes a heartbeat row; a dependency is broken to confirm tests then fail.
problem: Silent gates and fake-green checks give false confidence.
best_number: none
novelty: novel: gates carry their own fixtures and fail closed; inability to run counts as skipped.
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and no line measures it against a baseline; cheap, so build it in a multi-role code pipeline with many gates and hooks.

what_and_how: Bind each verdict to the exact candidate: hash the files, have a fresh reviewer return the digest, re-check the fingerprint before commit, sign a receipt from a separate host; any edit invalidates earlier verdicts.
problem: A verdict on one version can be applied to a changed one.
models: Codex with GPT-5.5 (high), DeepSeek v4 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5
best_number: w/o Evidence Feedback 65.23 vs Full HoH@3 71.52 (2609.01481)
verdict: not judged
recommendation: test-first: not judged and only whole-harness measures; sensible where reviewed changes must match what ships.

what_and_how: Do not add more gates of the same kind; change the verifier model family, modality or evidence source, because gates share blind spots and total reliability stops below one.
problem: Stacked checks look independent but fail together.
best_number: none
verdict: unmeasured: Stacking several gates adds less than independent-error maths predicts, because gates share blind spots; changing verifier family or evidence source is argued to help.
recommendation: test-first: unmeasured, theory and synthetic data only; the cost idea warns redundant verification multiplies cost, so diversify checkers before adding any.

what_and_how: A deterministic check refuses an identical test rerun when no edit happened since the last green result; the stop rule runs the relevant suite once after the final edit and reruns only after a relevant change.
problem: Redundant re-verification wastes budget and adds no success.
best_number: none
novelty: novel: refuses redundant re-verification instead of adding more checks.
verdict: survived: More feedback or repair rounds is not monotone: gains flatten after about three rounds, and redundant verification multiplies cost with no success gain.
recommendation: build: redundant verification multiplying cost with no gain survived with medium evidence; trivial in code.

what_and_how: Replay each approval workflow twice, Approve and Reject, with fixed upstream content and intercepted external services, and fail if the protected action still fires after Reject; show approval on a trusted screen bound to the action.
problem: Human approval steps often do not actually block the action.
best_number: 4 of 59 comparable public n8n workflows execute the protected effect after Reject (2611.19237)
novelty: novel: executes the reject path to prove human approval actually blocks the effect.
verdict: survived: Approval steps fail at the binding: saved confirmations survive changed state, approvals are dropped in joins, and reject paths still execute.
recommendation: build: approval binding failures survived with medium evidence.
